episodes.title: Antenna 3 Lombardia : Sathya Sai Baba : Giancarlo Rosati, Father Mario Mazzoleni, Filippo Polenghi
episodes.description:
An early 1990s broadcast, this rare interview with several devotees is from an episode of the show "Paranormale." 

Father Mario Mazzoleni (Don Mario Mazzoleni): A Catholic priest and theologian who worked for the Vatican Radio. After visiting Sai Baba in India, he became a devoted follower and wrote the controversial book A Catholic Priest Meets Sai Baba. Because he publically declared Sai Baba to be a divine incarnation, he was officially excommunicated by the Catholic Church in 1992.

Giancarlo Rosati: An Italian physician, surgeon, and author. He wrote extensively about his personal experiences, scientific observations, and spiritual transformation after witnessing Sai Baba's alleged materializations and healings.

F. Polenghi (Filippo Polenghi): An Italian photographer and filmmaker who documented life in Sai Baba's ashram (Prasanthi Nilayam). He captured historic footage and photos that helped introduce the guru to the Italian public.

Antenna 3, formerly known as "Antenna 3 Lombardia" and also known as "Antennatre" is a private TV station. It was founded in Legnano in 1977 by Renzo Villa with the help of Enzo Tortora. Antenna 3 was one of the first Italian private TV stations, born once the state monopoly on television broadcasting was ended by the small TV station Telebiella. In those years Atennatre was the largest out of 1500 private Italian TV stations.

episodes.title: Giancarlo Rosati Films : Gesù in Kashmir
episodes.description:
Gesù in Kashmir.

Giancarlo Rosati’s Gesù in Kashmir is an alternative historical and documentary project examining the theory that Jesus of Nazareth did not die on the cross, but instead survived the crucifixion and journeyed eastward to spend his remaining years traveling, teaching, and eventually being buried in the Roza Bal shrine in Srinagar, Kashmir.

The film serves as a visual and investigative companion to Rosati's independent research and subsequent literary works, drawing from local traditions, regional legends, and texts that attempt to trace the "silent" or "unknown" years of Jesus outside of traditional biblical canon.

Dr. Giancarlo Rosati, an Italian physician and author, traveled to Kashmir in 1988/9. This specific trip inspired him to write his alternative historical book Gesù Ribelle Palestinese and produce the companion documentary film "Gesù in Kashmir."

episodes.description:
Giancarlo Rosati Films : INTERVISTA DI DON MARIO MAZZOLENI.

Interview with Don Mario Mazzoleni, Puttaparthi, India.

Lingua Italiana ~ Don Mario Mazzoleni interview, Puttaparthi https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n0pc5qv4VRQ

A CATHOLIC PRIEST MEETS SAI BABA (1991) In the course of his spiritual inquiry, a Catholic priest meets an enlightening and extraordinary being: Sathya Sai Baba, a spiritual Master who lives in Puttaparthi, India. Like Jesus, Sai Baba performs miracles, materialises objects, heals the sick, and knows the past, present and future of everything that exists. Above all a transcendent peace and harmony flow from Him.

Who is Sai Baba? A saint, a magician, a demon, God in person? Don Mario Mazzoleni discovers how Sai Baba's teachings mirror those of Jesus Christ. Telling the story of his encounter with Sai Baba, and describing life in the ashram, he narrates the progress of his own spiritual search. His path begins with the need to detach himself from dogma and prejudice, and leads to the discovery of the fundamental unity of all religious creeds, a unity which transcends all cultural differences.

Don Mario Mazzoleni is 48 years old. He has a degree in Moral Theology from the Higher Institute of Theological Sciences of the Alphonsian Academy in Rome. In the 1970s he was associated with the Vatican Radio and the newspaper L'Avvenire. He was particularly concerned with the relationship of the mass media to spiritual instruction. He has been studying the miracle that is Sai Baba for twelve years, and has made eight trips to His ashram.

episodes.title: The Sacred Science of Meditation presented by Norman Paulson
episodes.description:
Norman Paulsen was born on February 3, 1929 in Santa Barbara, California. Norm’s early childhood search for God was inspired by his awareness of Spirit within and around him, and aided by learning that Moses had once seen God face to face.

As a young man he met Paramahansa Yogananda, the founder of Self-Realization Fellowship. He spent several years living at the SRF monastery learning and practicing the sacred techniques Kriya Yoga meditation. While living at SRF he received the vision that would lead to the founding of Sunburst.

After Norman left the monastery in 1951, he had a series of profound spiritual realizations, culminating in an experience of cosmic consciousness – a direct encounter with the light of God. This transformational encounter ignited his lifelong mission: to share the possibility of this possibility of God-realization with all sincere seekers.

In 1969, Norman founded Sunburst as a spiritual community centered on meditation, simple living, and an awakening to the Divine within. This way of life grew into a decades long involvement in organic farming and natural foods enterprises, including some of the first large-scale natural foods markets in the United States.

His autobiography, Christ Consciousness (1980), recounts the extraordinary spiritual experiences of his life and has inspired countless readers. A newly revised edition, Life-Love-God (hyperlink to store item), continues to share his message with all soul seekers.

Sunburst’s guiding light has always been Norman’s lifelong mission to help others to their own meeting with the Divine. Sunburst remains a growing community dedicated to sharing the Sunburst teachings and way of life.

Norman Paulsen left his earthly body on December 30, 2006 consciously and peacefully just as he entered it. His teachings, visions, and blessings live on through the Sunburst community and in the living presence of Christ Consciousness—the eternal “I Am That I Am.”

episodes.title: Living the Mystery of Life : Sri Sri Ravi Shankar (1990)
episodes.description:
Ashrams of India Volume 1 : Art of Living Ashram, the principal ashram of Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, near Udipalya Village, Bangalore

Sri Sri Ravi Shankar (13 May 1956 - present) was born in Papanasam, Tamil Nadu. His parents named him Ravi because he was born on a Sunday, and Shankar as it fell on the same date as the 8th century Hindu saint, Adi Shankara. It is reputed that from the age of four he could recite verses from the Bhagavad Gita and was often found in deep meditation. His first teacher was Sudhakar Chaturvedi, an Indian Vedic Scholar and a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi.

After graduating with a BSc from the St. Joseph’s College of Bangalore University he travelled with his second teacher, Maharishi Mahesh Yogi (1918-2008), giving talks and arranging conferences on Vedic science, and setting up Transcendental Meditation and Ayurveda centres.

Shankar founded the Art of Living Foundation in 1982 to teach the breathing technique “Sudarshan Kriya,” a rhythmic breathing exercise. In the early 1990s, he added the honorific Sri Sri to his own name so as not to be confused with the renowned sitarist Ravi Shankar (1920-2012).

Sri Sri Ravi Shankar and the Art of Living Ashram https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FkYUJ0bmWHI&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

episodes.title: Vadim Zeland
episodes.description:
Reality is like a movie with infinite versions already filmed.

Vadim Zeland is a reclusive Russian author and former quantum physicist. He is famous for creating “Reality Transurfing,” a spiritual and metaphysical philosophy. His book series teaches ways to control reality by changing one’s thoughts and attitude.

He taught people to “slide” between them by changing their inner state. Treating goals like “no big deal” made them manifest faster than wanting ever could. 

The core insight: Reality exists as infinite parallel tracks, like movie versions already filmed. Your inner state determines which track you experience.

Why it matters: His work influenced countless people to shift from forcing outcomes to allowing them. A fundamental change in how we interact with reality.

The infinite reality tracks.

Reality as parallel timelines.

The key idea: Reality exists as infinite parallel tracks, each representing a different version of events that could unfold.

How it works: Your inner state (your thoughts, emotions, and energy) determines which track you experience. You are constantly tuning in to different versions of reality.

The problem of importance: When you assign high importance to something, you create energetic turbulence that actually pushes you away from what you want.

The solution: Lower the importance, and you naturally slide to better timelines where your desires already exist.

The excess potential trap.

Why wanting too much blocks you.

What happens when you care too much: Treating desires as urgent or life-or-death creates what Zeland calls “excess potential.” This is energetic resistance in your reality field.

The universe’s response: The universe balances excess potential by creating obstacles. The harder you push, the more resistance you create.

Real-world example: Ever notice how desperately wanting something seems to push it further away? That’s excess potential in action.

The no-big-deal approach: Removes this resistance and allows you to slide into timelines where your desires exist naturally. No force required.

The pendulum trap.

Stop feeding your problems. What are pendulums? Zeland discovered that problems and obstacles are “pendulums.” These are energy structures that feed on your emotional reactions.

How they work: When you fight problems or give them attention, they grow stronger. Your resistance gives them energy to persist.

The counter-intuitive solution: Step aside mentally rather than engage. Don’t fight the pendulum. Simply stop feeding it your energy.

The result: Starving the pendulum allows you to move to a reality track where the problem doesn’t exist or loses its power over you.

What actually happens.

The energy mechanics of manifestation.

Why desperation blocks you: Desperation and attachment create energetic resistance, like trying to swim upstream against a powerful current.

The neutral state: When you treat your goal as “no big deal,” you remove the excess potential that creates obstacles.

Energy flow: Your energy becomes neutral and flowing, like water finding its natural path downhill.

The shift: This neutral state allows you to slide naturally into the reality track where your desire already exists. No struggle required.

The 3-step method.

Step 1: Lower the importance. Release the pressure by treating your desire as “nice to have” rather than “must have.”

Step 2: Act as if it’s already arranged. Move through your day assuming the universe has already handled it for you.

Step 3: Slide between realities. When obstacles appear, mentally step sideways into a parallel reality where they don’t exist.

The core principle: These steps work together to remove resistance and align your energy with the reality you want to experience.

Why this actually works.

The science of letting go.

Your Emotional Broadcast: Your emotional state sends out afrequency that attracts matching circumstances. Desperation only attracts more reasons to feel desperate.

The Manifestation Paradox: Calm confidence draws opportunities and synchronicities. The less you need something, the faster it arrives.

The Highest Frequency: The no big deal state is actually the highest manifestation frequency because it carries zero resistance.

What to Watch For: Synchronicities increase, doors open more easily, helpful people appear, and obstacles dissolve naturally. These are signs you are sliding into better timelines.

The truth about reality.

What you chase runs away. What you allow comes closer. 

The core lesson: Treat your desires as no big deal and watch them manifest with ease.

Why most manifestation fails: People try too hard. They create importance around desires, which generates the exact resistance that blocks them.

The path forward: The no-big-deal approach dissolves resistance and allows manifestation through the path of least resistance.

episodes.title: Stairways to the Mayan Gods (1973)
episodes.description:
Skilled in mathematics and astronomy Mayan priests developed one the most complex and accurate calendars ever created.

Directed by Elda and Irving Hartley
Narration written by Joseph Campbell

Joseph Campbell, the celebrated Western expert in world mythology, wrote the narration for this delightful journey to the Mayan religious centers of the Yucatan, Central America. The Mayans, like ancient Vedic seers were master astronomers, mathematicians and translated their heavenly perceptions into architectural wonders, pyramid-like temples and palaces. Questions such as why this flourishing religious metropolis-so advanced in many fields of knowledge - suddenly disappeared are intelligently probed by the film. With Mayan teachings now in resurgence in North America, this video will be enjoyed by both the spiritual seeker as well as the scholar probing the overlap of Hindu and Mayan teachings. The filming, like other Hartley productions, is artistically handled and professionally executed.

episodes.title: Science and the Power of Prayer (1999)
episodes.description:
Science and the Power of Prayer by Elda Hartley explores the convergence of medicine and faith.

According to polls commissioned in 1996 by USA Today Weekend and Time, four-fifths of patients surveyed believe in the healing power of prayer and want their doctors to address spiritual issues with them. For centuries, Christians, Jews, Muslims, Buddhists, and Hindus have prayed and meditated as part of their spiritual practice. It is only recently that researchers have produced solid scientific evidence of the healing power of these efforts.

This film directed by Elda Hartley explores the convergence of medicine and faith. Dr. Larry Dossey, the most articulate spokesperson for this contemporary phenomenon, appears on the program explaining the extraordinary reach of intercessory prayer. Also appearing are a doctor who calls upon God before an operation in order to help clear his mind, a researcher who discusses the future of medicine in the twenty-first century, a priest who has experienced the restorative power of a laying on of hands ceremony, and a spiritual writer who assesses the role prayer plays in various religions.

episodes.title: Requiem for a Faith (1968)
episodes.description:
Requiem for a Faith with Huston Smith on the Tibetan Culture and Religion.

Originally produced and distributed by the Hartley Film Foundation. 

Elda Hartley Films https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxAByIDUroF0Ie91XO-an0tL

In a country where one-sixth of the males become monks, all things are religious in Tibet, according to narrator Huston Smith. The religious philosopher and author (The World's Religions) explains the tenets of the Tibetan's unique brand of Buddhism, while noted spiritual filmmaker Elda Hartley provides astonishing footage of monks engaged in discussions with dance-like movement, the faithful making strings of prayer flags and artisans carving prayer blocks and ceremonial masks. Smith's prose ranges from poetic to over the top ("a society left on the shelf, set in amber, left in deep freeze"), but Hartley's range (from breathtaking skyscapes to small moments like a monk protectively removing a single snail from an oft-trodden path) may justify Smith's enthusiasm. Tibet had already been long occupied by China when this 27-minute documentary was shot in the late 1960s, and unfortunately, nothing has changed for the Tibetan people since.

The traditional life of Tibet is depicted by Huston Smith, Professor of Philosophy at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Smith shows the extent to which traditional customs have been invaded and corroded by the West. All social and economic activity revolves around religious practice. The importance of the Dalai Lama is emphasised. Set in Gyuto Tantric Monastery in Northern India, this moving film explores the essence of Tibetan Buddhism and focuses on the unusual chants of the Gyuto monks, whose training enables them to chant in chords. The film was shot mainly in Dalhousie, India, where the two Tantric Colleges, Gyuto and Gyume, were re-established in exile.

episodes.title: Edgar Cayce (1975)
episodes.description:
Edgar Cayce was a mystic and a psychic, one of the greatest of all times.  He seemed to tap a universal mind that could peer into every troubled cell of the human body and could roam through time to see past lives and future events.  

Now, thirty years after his death, his medical cures, confirmed during his lifetime, are helping people more than ever.  His cure for the malaise of our time, based on reincarnation and the teachings of Christ, is in the mainstream of all the great spiritual philosophers. 

This film recounts his early life, how he discovered his psychic talent, and how, reluctantly, he came to use it.  It interviews many of the people who know him best and summarises his basic concepts.

The Hartley Film Foundation
Cat Rock Road, Cos Cob, CT 06807

Elda Hartley Films PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxAByIDUroF0Ie91XO-an0tL

Edgar Cayce (March 18, 1877 – January 3, 1945) was an American clairvoyant who reported and chronicled an ability to diagnose diseases and recommend treatments for ailments while asleep. During thousands of transcribed sessions, Cayce answered questions on subjects including healing, reincarnation, dreams, the afterlife, past lives, nutrition, Atlantis, and future events. Cayce said he was a devout Christian and was not a spiritualist or communicating with spirits. Cayce is regarded as a founder of the New Age movement and a principal source of many of the movement's characteristic beliefs.

In 1931, Cayce founded a non-profit organiSation, the Association for Research and Enlightenment. In 1942, a popular and highly sympathetic biography of Cayce titled 'There is a River' was published by journalist Thomas Sugrue.

episodes.title: Renovation of the Beatles Ashram, Sankaracharya Nagar, Chaurasi Kutiya
episodes.description:
This video is from https://www.youtube.com/@Rishikeshwritings that brings to you local & spiritual stories from the heart of Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, India . 

Ashrams of India Volume 2 : Maharishi Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia Ashram), the former principal ashram of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi, popularly known as the Beatles Ashram.

Rishikesh's iconic Chaurasi Kutia ashram complex is set to undergo a major renovation at an estimated cost of ₹100 crore. The redevelopment project is expected to be completed by 2027, giving the historic spiritual site a new look while retaining its cultural and religious significance.

Without altering its original form in any way, restoration work began in January 2026 on various historical structures - including the 84 meditation huts. This project is estimated to cost ₹101 crore.

Maharishi Mahesh Yogi, world-renowned for Transcendental Meditation, established Shankaracharya Nagar here in 1961 by leasing 15 acres of land from the Forest Department near Swargashram (Rishikesh).

Subsequently, he developed this site into a meditation and yoga centre by constructing 84 small huts featuring a remarkable architectural style, along with over a hundred caves. Additionally, the centre features 135 dome-shaped huts to serve as accommodation for practitioners.

Sitchin's research identifies them as ancient aliens, known as the Anunnaki, who came to earth from the planet Nibiru.

Over the years, startling evidence has been unearthed, challenging established notions of the origins of Earth and life on it and suggesting the existence of a superior race of beings who once inhabited our world. The product of thirty years of intensive research, The 12th Planet is the first book in Zecharia Sitchin's prophetic Earth Chronicles series - a revolutionary body of work that offers indisputable documentary proof of humanity's extraterrestrial forefathers. Travelers from the stars, they arrived eons ago, and planted the genetic seed that would ultimately blossom into a remarkable species... called Man.

The 12th Planet brings to life the Sumerian civilization, presenting millennia-old evidence of the existence of Nibiru, the home planet of the Anunnaki and of the landings of the Anunnaki on Earth every 3,600 years, and reveals a complete history of the solar system as told by these early visitors from another planet.

Zecharia Sitchin's Earth Chronicles series, with millions of copies sold worldwide, deal with the history and prehistory of Earth and humankind. Each book in the series is based upon information written on clay tablets by the ancient civilizations of the Near East. The series is offered here, for the first time, in highly readable, hardbound collector's editions with enhanced maps and diagrams.

Zecharia Sitchin (1920 - 2010) was born in Russia and grew up in Palestine, where he acquired a profound knowledge of modern and ancient Hebrew, other Semitic and European languages, the Old Testament, and the history and archaeology of the Near East. A graduate of the University of London with a degree in economic history, he worked as a journalist and editor for many years prior to undertaking his life’s work - The Earth Chronicles.

One of the few scholars able to read the clay tablets and interpret ancient Sumerian and Akkadian, Sitchin based The Earth Chronicles series on the texts and pictorial evidence recorded by the ancient civilizations of the Near East. His books have been widely translated, reprinted in paperback editions, converted to Braille for the blind, and featured on radio and television programs.

episodes.title: Angkor ~ The Lost City (1961)
episodes.description:
Angkor Wat ('City/Capital of Temples') is a Vaishnava Hindu and Theravada Buddhist temple complex in Siem Reap, Cambodia, and the largest religious complex in the world. Located on a site measuring 162.6 hectares (1.6 km2; 401.8 acres) within the ancient capital of Angkor, it was constructed between 1113 and 1150 CE during the reign of the Khmer king Suryavarman II as a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu. From the late 13th century onward, the complex was gradually transformed into a Buddhist temple and has remained an active center of Buddhist worship for centuries. Angkor Wat is noted for its monumental scale, extensive bas-reliefs, and architectural unity characteristics of Khmer architecture. Unlike most Angkorian temples, it is oriented toward the west. 

Ashrams of India Volume 1 ~
Just before he arrived in Siem Reap, Cambodia in December 2014 to host a three-week, $10,000 meditation workshop at the Empress Angkor Hotel, Paramahansa Nithyananda, (also known Nithyananda Sangha), claimed that the earliest Khmer temples in Siem Rep were built in Southern India and that the Angkor Wat temple was constructed 3,000 years ago, making the temples are far older than the 900 or 1,000 years asserted by Western historians, and that many of the temples were not built in the Kingdom at all. 

Nithyananda claims to be an expert on Hindu Temples and has established over 32 in India and around the world. Information, he says that is drawn from the Akashic records, declare that many of the temples were first built and carved in Mahabalipuram, dismantled and numbered and then moved 60 km north to Chennai, where they were loaded onto a ship and then transported to Cambodia. There, they were re-assembled, using a coding system in Prakrit, that was not dissimilar to modern day barcoding, once assembled they were re-carved.

The elephants necessary for the work also had to be shipped from India, as Cambodians did not during this period train their elephants for the construction of temples. Elephants are required to undergo specific training to maneuver blocks. This type of work differs from that of logging, where working in a team is not necessary. The elephants move the blocks by working together, pulling from the front and pushing from the rear. Temple-building elephants are trained as a whole team using a single language to communicate, rather than the individual communication between a mahout who works with an elephant over a period of years. Usually, in Kerala a child will be given to an elephant and the elephant will be given to a child, both of them grow together developing a unique language between the two.
Nithyananda says that the Pallava Kings established trade and a sea route with Cambodia. A Pallava King then married the Cambodian tribe’s head’s daughter.  Eventually, Cambodia embraced the Pallava culture and requested the Pallava King to settle there and build a kingdom. At the time, Cambodia did not have the craftsmen or expertise, so the initial temples were built in India, dismantled and shipped to Cambodia. 

Sailing on this route during this time in history had a success rate of only sixty percent, the whole temple had to be carved twice to ensure that enough blocks reached the Cambodian shores to be reassembled. The passage took from sixty days to anywhere around six months, as replenishment stops on the islands in the Bay of Bengal were required. The amount of food and water needed for the elephants for the entire journey could not be stowed onboard, so suitable islands were identified where food and water could be loaded. On those islands, temples were constructed for the resident population of a few hundred to service the stopovers.

After reaching Cambodia, only twenty-five percent of the work was done, as the discharge, foundation work and reassembly with final detailed carving was to be undertaken. Eventually, perhaps a generation later, the Cambodians were able to commence a temple building program after the skills were passed on.

episodes.title: Have Guru Darshan
episodes.description:
Have Guru Darshan

David Berry Productions. 

Have Guru Darshan (1986) is a 43-minute documentary and visual essay by filmmaker David Berry. It is composed of rare home movies and footage shot between 1977 and 1981, capturing the spiritual teacher Shri Haidakhan Babaji at his ashram in the Himalayas.

This impressionistic video about the late Shri Hairakhan Baba (Babaji) conveys more mood than information. Yet, its message, enriched with exquisite music and photography, is unforgettably potent. 

Film maker and highly-acclaimed special effects expert David Berry makes the most of limited resources in this home movie. 

He leads us through compellingly unpredictable fast-forward sequences interposed with still shots and contrasted with inventive time-lapse photography, leaving us with a sense of viewing a series of portraits in motion. 

We watch Babaji dance, reeling and twirling in bliss to some seemingly irresistible inner force, while at each crucial turn he's caught, poised and suspended in action, allowing us to relish a detail. Then, suddenly, we are whisked to the top of a mountain to watch hours of Storm clouds gather in an instant – all to the exquisite, original and moving music of the accomplished Turkantam. 

Have Guru Darshan is not narrated but doesn't need to be. It's a moving drama of spiritual feeling. Shot in 1977, 1979 and 1981, this video is accompanied with printed material briefly explaining Babaji's 14-year Saivite Hindu mission (1970 - 1984). His message was: "Truth, Simplicity, Love."

episodes.title: The Secret of Nikola Tesla (1980)
episodes.description:
The Secret of Nikola Tesla (Serbo-Croatian: Tajna Nikole Tesle), is a 1980 Yugoslav biographical film which dramatizes events in the life of the Serbian-American engineer and inventor Nikola Tesla. This somewhat fictionalized portrayal of Tesla's life has him contending with Thomas Edison and J.P. Morgan in his attempts to develop alternating current and then "free" wireless power.

Nikola Tesla meets Swami Vivekananda https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_8BLruOoHrI

Nikola Tesla meets Swami Vivekananda https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GkGOMSVUG2U

Alternate Knowledge PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxAV8kKWPZagN54-kSsC2cZ4

Tesla in a hotel room in 1943 talks to a reporter. He then reminisces about how things would be different if J. P Morgan had listened to him.

Tesla arrives in the US in the 1880s. He tries to convince his new employer, Thomas Edison, to adopt his newly invented electric induction motor running on an alternating current (AC) system but Edison claims direct current (DC) is better and turns him down. Robert Underwood Johnson and his wife Katharine, who were at the meeting, later find Tesla digging a ditch, having quit his job at Edison. Tesla strikes a business deal with two investors to finance development of his motor. He shows off his AC system at meeting of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers but Edison, in the audience, claims it is impractical. After the reporters, and even Tesla's own investors, walk away George Westinghouse convinces Tesla to sell him his AC patents and offers a contract to pay Tesla a royalty on his motor design. They end up in a public battle with Edison trying to demonstrate their system is not dangerous (as Edison claims) and is actually better than DC. J.P. Morgan, pulling the strings in the background, calls Tesla and Edison into a meeting and, unhappy with Edison's progress electrifying his factories, tells Tesla he can try to prove AC would work better.

At a banquet celebrating the building of an alternating current power plant at Niagara Falls Tesla confuses the audience with his futuristic ideas about his high frequency wireless AC transmission system and then tells someone he is off to Europe to see his family (who he has been having flashbacks about). On that trip he visits his bed-ridden mother who dies in his arms. He then wanders out in the country side having flash backs about his childhood and the death of his brother, all punctuated by visions of falling water and lightning. Westinghouse and Katharine visit Tesla back at his New York lab where the inventor tears up his royalty contract to save Westinghouse from financial ruin. Tesla goes on to develop his wireless power system, making several reports to Morgan on his progress. Morgan tells Tesla he is unhappy with wild stories about the inventor but keeps backing him.

Westinghouse warns Tesla (who is now building his Morgan financed Wardenclyffe wireless power station) to watch out for Morgan's motives and Katharine tells the inventor how she wished they could have had more of a relationship together. Tesla learns from Morgan that Guglielmo Marconi has stolen his wireless patents and that Albert Einstein has new theories about matter and energy. Tesla tells Morgan these new theories are a "crime against nature" and tries to get Morgan to back his free wireless power system before it is too late. After Tesla leaves Morgan says he won't back a system that would put him out of business and orders all further interaction with Tesla cut off. Tesla looks over his demolished Wardenclyffe station and complains, at the end of his life in a world choked with smog, that he wished Morgan had listened to him.

episodes.title: Author John Gray Interview ~ Sri Kaleshwar Ashram
episodes.description:
Best selling author John Gray talks with Alan Steinfeld in India at the ashram of Swami Kaleshwar (08 January 1973 - 15 March 2002) in 2000, about healing and practical miracles. John Gray (born December 28, 1951) is an American relationship counselor, lecturer, and author. His parents were both Christians and taught him Yoga and took him to visit Paramahansa Yogananda during his childhood. Yogananda's book 'Autobiography of A Yogi' inspired him greatly later in life. In 1969, he began a nine-year association with Maharishi Mahesh Yogi before beginning his career as an author and personal relationship counselor. In 1992, he published the book Men Are from Mars, Women Are from Venus, which became a long-term best seller and formed the central theme of his subsequent books and career activities. His books have sold millions of copies.

Ashrams of India Volume 1 : Sri Kaleshwar Ashram, the ashram of Sri Kaleshwar. In 1993, Sri Kaleshwar founded the five-acre Sri Kaleshwar Ashram in the South Indian village of Penukonda. Penukonda is a sacred power spot with a long history of association with many saints and divine souls. The ashram is situated next to the summer residence of King Krishnadevaraya (1471 - 1529) and within the walls of the ancient fort. The Shiva Sai Mandir contains temples to both Shirdi Baba and Jesus, the Dwarkamai, a meditation temple that is used in divine processes to open the higher spiritual channels. A multi-story apartment complex sits in the south and southwest of the ashram.

Over the years, startling evidence has been unearthed, challenging established notions of the origins of Earth and life on it and suggesting the existence of a superior race of beings who once inhabited our world. The product of thirty years of intensive research, The 12th Planet is the first book in Zecharia Sitchin's prophetic Earth Chronicles series - a revolutionary body of work that offers indisputable documentary proof of humanity's extraterrestrial forefathers. Travelers from the stars, they arrived eons ago, and planted the genetic seed that would ultimately blossom into a remarkable species... called Man.

The 12th Planet brings to life the Sumerian civilization, presenting millennia-old evidence of the existence of Nibiru, the home planet of the Anunnaki and of the landings of the Anunnaki on Earth every 3,600 years, and reveals a complete history of the solar system as told by these early visitors from another planet.

Zecharia Sitchin's Earth Chronicles series, with millions of copies sold worldwide, deal with the history and prehistory of Earth and humankind. Each book in the series is based upon information written on clay tablets by the ancient civilizations of the Near East. The series is offered here, for the first time, in highly readable, hardbound collector's editions with enhanced maps and diagrams.

Zecharia Sitchin (1920 - 2010) was born in Russia and grew up in Palestine, where he acquired a profound knowledge of modern and ancient Hebrew, other Semitic and European languages, the Old Testament, and the history and archaeology of the Near East. A graduate of the University of London with a degree in economic history, he worked as a journalist and editor for many years prior to undertaking his life’s work - The Earth Chronicles.

One of the few scholars able to read the clay tablets and interpret ancient Sumerian and Akkadian, Sitchin based The Earth Chronicles series on the texts and pictorial evidence recorded by the ancient civilizations of the Near East. His books have been widely translated, reprinted in paperback editions, converted to Braille for the blind, and featured on radio and television programs.

episodes.description:
Ashrams of India : Volume 1 

Sri Aurobindo Society Ulsoor Road, the Sri Aurobindo ashram in Bangalore.

110 Gangadhara Chetty Road
Opposite Ulsoor Tank (Lake)
Ulsoor 
Bangalore 560008
Karnataka

Phone: +91 80 25559885

Main Ashram: Sri Aurobindo Ashram
Sri Aurobindo Ashram 
St. Gilles St, Pondicherry/Puducherry

The ashram Sri Aurobindo Society Ulsoor Road, is in a peaceful environment of nearly five acres facing Ulsoor Lake. The bhavan provides a choice of learning experiences at the hands of qualified teachers in the diverse yet creative fields of crafts, paintings, music, naturopathy, yoga, Ikebana and bonsai. 

Built in 1932 and originally the home of Princess Rajalakshmi Aishwarya Devi who was sister of the King of Nepal, it was gifted to the Sri Aurobindo Trust in 1979. This palatial building of colonial architecture is one of the best conserved heritage sites in Bangalore.

Relics of Sri Aurobindo are enshrined here in one of the meditation rooms. 
Products from the Sri Aurobindo Ashram, Puducherry that include Ayurvedic remedies are available. The library contains all the books written by Aurobindo and The Mother along with other related publications and periodicals.

There are regular weekly programmes of study and collective meditations. Talks by knowledgeable persons from the ashram and other branches are arranged periodically in addition to occasional programmes of devotional songs. Seminars and workshops are also arranged on the thoughts of Sri Aurobindo and The Mother.

The Sri Aurobindo Bhawan is run by devotees who work on an honorary basis.

The meditation centre is open from 7.00 am to 6.00 pm every day.

episodes.title: Frédérick Leboyer interview, August, 2006
episodes.description:
Frédérick Leboyer interview, August, 2006.

https://newdimensions.org/

New Dimensions Radio, is an independent US public radio program founded in 1973.

This station holds ‘New Beginnings for Child and Adult,’  a 1978 conversation with Frederick Leboyer that has never been released. It’s one of 692 long-form recordings sitting in the archive.

The station is running a campaign to fund the restoration. From 1973, New Dimensions has been conducting and disseminating deep dialogues with wisdom leaders and innovators through an international network of public radio stations and digital media platforms.

Over 1500 programs can be downloaded.

“To have children . . . it is one of the greatest privileges that life holds.” Frédérick Leboyer (1918 - 2017), the Poet of Birth and Obstetrician best known for his revolutionary 1974 book, Birth Without Violence. In an interview, Irena Edrovska asked Leboyer about the father’s role during birth, to which he replied “He has to move away. Being pregnant is like going on a pilgrimage. The woman is going on an inner pilgrimage. She is going to the spring of Life. And the man cannot follow, he cannot go there. And he should not try.” He met perhaps the biggest influence on his life, Swami Prajnanpad while travelling through India, who believed human beings carried the memory of their births deep within themselves. Françoise Freedman, Founder and Director of Birthlight, says “Swami Prajnanpad, influenced him in his quest from non-violence (ahimsa), to yoga and on to “inner light,” the art of breathing and the art of loving touch and sound in the sacred gateway of birth.”

Sathya Sai Baba filmed by Jack Lenchiner (1982).

This video documents New Year's Eve day 1982 in Prasanthi Nilayam that includes a wedding, darshan, and bhajans. It has not been edited. Those who did not visit the ashram before the Sai Kulwant Hall was built can get a sense of what it was like to be at darshan in those earlier days.

00:00 The video starts with a parade accompanying a car with the wedding party traveling from the ashram for the wedding at the old mandir. Sathya Sai Baba arrives and spends some time there. 
17:30 Sathya Sai Baba leaves the old mandir, the wedding ceremonies continue
24:00 People then proceed back to the ashram.
48:31 Darshan
58:00 As bhajans go on, daylight slowly comes to an end as we hear and see the crows and other birds, which came every evening. The lights come on in the mandir just before arathi, and after arathi the sun sets.

episodes.title: Mithila (1974)
episodes.description:
Mithila is an ancient kingdom in the Indian state of Bihar, bordering Nepal. For centuries, the women of Mithila have decorated the walls of their homes with paintings and motifs for weddings and other ceremonies. Painting is an integral part of women's education. Mithila painting is an art form expressed in the decoration of the kohbar (the bridal chamber) walls at the time of the wedding. These paintings draw inspiration from mythological and folkloric themes as well as Tantric symbols, although the central theme is invariably love and fertility. The film depicts this ancestral tradition through the figure of Sita, the heroine of the Ramayana.

This film is from Georges Luneau https://www.youtube.com/@GeorgesLuneauFilms/videos
and see his other channel https://www.youtube.com/@GeorgesLuneauDocumentaires/videos

Mithila est un ancien royaume de l'Inde dans l'Etat du Bihar à la frontière du Népal. Depuis des siècles, les femmes de Mithila décorent les murs de leurs maisons de peintures et de motifs à l'occasion de mariages et d'autres cérémonies. La peinture fait partie de l'éducation des femmes. Les peintures Mithila est un art qui s'exprime dans la décoration des murs du kohbar (la chambre nuptiale), au moment des noces. Elles s'inspirent de thèmes mythologiques et folkloriques ainsi que de symbole tantrique, bien que le thème central soit invariablement l'amour et la fertilité. Le film montre cette tradition ancestrale autour de la figure de Sita l'héroïne du Ramayana

episodes.title: La Fortuna Interiore
episodes.description:
The Inner Fortune

Directors Lucia Veronesi and Valentina Bonifacio
Editing Lucia Veronesi and Valentina Bonifacio
Animation Lucia Veronesi
Shooting Lucia Veronesi and Giuseppe Drago
Audio Valentina Bonifacio and Lucia Veronesi
Audio postoproduction Marian Alexander Mentrup

Among the white plasters and the grey cones of the roofs, suddenly bright colors are released: a dome with red and yellow segments, arches and capitals of cream on top of white columns. It is the temple of the Ashram, a place dedicated to Babaji Haidakhan Baba, one of the first built in the West. For forty years it has stood out among the trulli of Cisternino, in the Valle d’Itria, in Puglia.

Lisetta Carmi, a cardinal figure of the Italian artistic twentieth century, founded it. Born in Genoa to a family of Jewish origin, at the end of the seventies she built the Ashram with her temple, which perfectly reproduces that of Haidakhan, an Indian village on the slopes of the Himalayas, where Babaji appeared for the first time in 1970, and where she met Lisetta for the first time.

Thus began, in 1979, at the age of fifty-five, the “third life” of Lisetta Carmi, as she herself defines it, after those of pianist and photographer of international fame.Through her close-up portrait and other interviews, La fortuna interiore investigates the interaction that has been created between the place, its inhabitants and those who decided to move to the Itria Valley to stay close to the Ashram.

Haidakhan Babaji PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxArye1y9RVlkyqGZwfL66XD

Regia Lucia Veronesi e Valentina Bonifacio
Montaggio video Lucia Veronesi e Valentina Bonifacio
Animazioni Lucia Veronesi
Riprese Lucia Veronesi e Giuseppe Drago
Montaggio audio Valentina Bonifacio e Lucia Veronesi
Supporto audio postproduzione Marian Alexander Mentrup

Fra i bianchi intonaci e i coni grigi dei tetti, all’improvviso si sprigionano colori sgargianti: una cupola a spicchi rossi e gialli, archi e capitelli di panna in cima a candide colonne. É il tempio dell’Ashram, luogo dedicato a Babaji Haidakhan Baba, uno dei primi costruiti in Occidente. Da quarant’anni spicca fra i trulli di Cisternino, nella Valle d’Itria, in Puglia.

Lo ha fondato Lisetta Carmi, figura cardinale del Novecento artistico italiano. Nata a Genova da una famiglia di origine ebraica, alla fine degli anni Settanta costruisce l’Ashram con il suo tempio, che riproduce perfettamente quello di Haidakhan, un paesino indiano alle pendici dell’Himalaya, dove nel 1970 Babaji apparve per la prima volta, e dove avvenne il primo incontro con Lisetta.

Inizia così, nel 1979, a cinquantacinque anni, la “terza vita” di Lisetta Carmi, come lei stessa la definisce, dopo quelle di pianista e fotografa di fama internazionale.

Attraverso il suo ritratto da vicino e altre interviste, La fortuna interiore indaga l’interazione che si è creata tra il luogo, i suoi abitanti e chi per stare vicino all’Ashram ha deciso di trasferirsi in Valle d’Itria.

episodes.title: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi’s 1970 performance for Sathya Sai Baba
episodes.description:
Pandit Bhimsen Joshi’s 1970 performance for Sathya Sai Baba took place in the Brindavan Ashram in Whitefield, Bangalore. This historic recital marked the beginning of a lifelong spiritual connection between the legendary Kirana gharana vocalist and the spiritual master.

The performance was held during the famous Summer Course on Indian Culture and Spirituality, which Sathya Sai Baba organised for university students at Whitefield.

Singing directly in the "Divine Presence," Bhimsen Joshi delivered a powerful repertoire of Hindustani classical ragas and devotional bhajans. Archive footage from the event highlights his signature high-energy taans (rapid melodic phrases) and intense emotional immersion.
This was one of the earliest high-profile interactions between the maestro and Sathya Sai Baba, initiating a tradition where the singer would perform at the ashram across subsequent decades (including notable returns in 1978 and 1990).

Following this initial 1970 event, Pandit Bhimsen Joshi remained a deeply devoted follower.

Joshi later recollected that his very first glimpse (darshan) of Sathya Sai Baba occurred at the home of the renowned vocalist Smt. Hirabai Barodekar, where he sang a bhajan and was deeply moved.

The bond culminated in a widely cited event in 1998, when Joshi faced an urgent, high-risk brain surgery to remove a tumour. Sathya Sai Baba reportedly sent materialised vibhuti (sacred ash) through a student just before the procedure, which the maestro's family credits for his swift recovery and the non-cancerous nature of the tumour.

episodes.title: Many Paths, One Truth (1977)
episodes.description:
Many Paths, One Truth

Oscar-nominated director John D. Goodell (Always a New Beginning) made a documentary that chronicled the preparation for the Yoga Ecumenical Service, talks by the celebrants and the actual interfaith service. On the 30th anniversary of the film’s original release, the digitally re-mastered film was released on DVD. Sri Swami Satchidananda, a pioneer in the interfaith movement, often gathered with clergy of various faiths to discuss how to promote unity in diversity. During one of these interfaith retreats and symposiums, he had another innovation: the Yoga Ecumenical Service (now known as the Light of Truth Universal Service), in which representatives of different faiths gathered together around a circular altar and performed a worship service to a central light. This light - in the form of a lit candle - was adopted as a universal symbol of the Divine. Performing the service were celebrants representing their respective faiths, and offering worship to the central light from their own faiths’ traditions.

Celebrants included:

Sri Swami Satchidananda,
Rabbi Joseph Gelberman,
Brother David Steindl-Rast, OSB,
Reverend Gesshin (Roshi Prabhasa Dharma),
Father Robert Beh,
Murshida Taj Inayat
 
“Because we are one in Spirit, it doesn’t mean that you should renounce your own path or approach. That is not unity; that is conversion. Real unity means accepting all the various approaches, and that is what interfaith understanding is all about. Only by having a universal and spiritual vision can we bring positive change into the world.” - Sri Swami Satchidananda.

episodes.title: Haidakhan Babaji, 1979
episodes.description:
Ashrams of India Volume 2 - Haidakhan Vishwa Mahadham Ashram, principal ashram of Haidakhan Babaji, who claimed to be Babaji. 

The Haidakhan Babaji ashrams in Ashrams of India Volume 2 $3.95 : eBook Ashrams of India Volume 2 https://www.amazon.com/Ashrams-India-Bronte-Company-Limited-ebook/dp/B08MVXX75L/ref=sr_1_1?

Haldwani - Kathghariya Dham/Hairakhan Kathghariya Ashram
Ranikhet - Anandpuri Ashram 
Sitlakhet - Siddhashram 

According to Paramahansa Yogananda, Babaji chooses to live in obscurity in place beyond Badrinath. Yogananda’s autobiography revealed the existence of Babaji to the world and since Yogananda’s death, many more stories relating to Babaji have emerged. 

Babaji has been identified with Old Herakhan Baba who lived in the foothills of the Himalayas in the Kumaon region between 1800 and 1922/24. His followers expected him to return after his departure in 1922/24 and established a number of ashrams for him throughout India. 

Another teacher, Mahendra Baba throughout the 1950s and 1960s predicted Babaji’s return and devoted his life to facilitating the reappearance of Babaji. Mahendra restored the old ashrams, wrote books about Babaji, and asked everyone to receive Babaji. Mahendra died in 1969, before the return of Babaji (Haidakhan Babaji).

In June 1970, a young man identified as Haidakhan Babaji appeared and moved among the Babaji ashrams for 14 years, until his death in 1984. He travelled around India teaching and healing as more ashrams were opened for him. 

Babaji told his devotees that he appeared in many incarnations to restore the Sanatana Dharma, and urged them to live in truth and simplicity, regardless of religious affiliation.

He said that true devotion will replace material obsessions and will cultivate the presence of divine wisdom, and urged people to chant the name of God, using the mantra Om Namah Shiva, literally “I take refuge in God.” 

Leonard Orr and Sondra Ray, founders of the Rebirthing movement, were among his American disciples. 

The Self-Realization Fellowship founded by Paramahansa Yogananda, believe that Haidakhan Babaji is not Babaji, and Sri M states that Haidakhan Baba is a disciple of Babaji.

episodes.title: Mandukya Upanishad Chanting (AUDIO)
episodes.description:
This Upanishad is the kernel of Vedanta, the most profound among all the Upanishads. It is the chief one, having the distinction of being recommended as enough, by itself, to lead man to salvation. It is very brief, consisting of just a dozen mantras! They are divided into four chapters: origin (agama), falsehood (vaithathya), non-duality (a-dwaitha), and extinction of the firebrand (alatha-santhi). In the first chapter, the secret doctrine of the Om (Pranava), which is the key to self-realisation, is expounded. In the second chapter, the doctrine of dualism, the great obstacle to liberation, is discussed and rebutted. In the third, the non-dual (a-dwaitha) Unity is propounded. In the last chapter certain mutually contradictory non-Vedic doctrines are described and rejected.

No sound is beyond the ken of Om; they are all Om, its permutations and products. Brahman is also Om, identified by It and with It. The Brahman, which is beyond vision, is manifest for vision as Atma.

The Mandukya Upanishad is in prose, consisting of twelve terse verses and it discusses the syllable AUM, presents the theory of four states of consciousness, asserts the existence and nature of Atman.

The Mandukya Upanishad is notable for having been recommended in the Muktikā Upanishad, as the one Upanishad that alone is sufficient for knowledge to gain moksha, and as first in its list of eleven principal Upanishads.

The text is also notable for inspiring Gaudapada's Karika, a classic for the Vedanta school of Hinduism. Mandukya Upanishad is among the oft cited texts on chronology and philosophical relationship between Hinduism and Buddhism.

Our Humble Pranams & Thanks to Our Bhagavan Sri Satya Sai Baba and to the following team for all their hours of hard work and love poured in this offering!!! episodes.title: SWAMIJI, UN VOYAGE INTÉRIEUR (SWAMIJI - AN INNER JOURNEY) (1983)
episodes.description:
SWAMIJI - UN VOYAGE INTÉRIEUR, le documentaire réalisé en 1984 par Patrice Chagnard reste toujours le film référence sur Henri Le Saux. Il est désormais librement visible sur le web en qualité master. Merci PATRICE CHAGNARD de l'avoir confié à Henri Le Saux TV https://www.youtube.com/@HenriLeSauxTV

Sous la forme de récit autobiographique, combinant les textes d'Henri Le Saux, souvent d'une grande beauté, et le souvenir de ses proches, l'itinéraire de ce moine bénédictin converti à l'hindouisme. Parti en Inde en 1948 pour y fonder un ashram, lieu de dialogue et de confrontation de la mystique chrétienne et des différentes traditions spirituelles de l'Inde, il choisit de se retirer dans la solitude, aux sources du Gange, dans l'Himalaya, et de mener là, jusqu'à sa mort, en 1973, l'existence d'un moine errant hindou, d'un sadou.

Réalisation : Patrice Chagnard
Écriture : Patrice Chagnard
Production (structure) : CFRT Productions - Comité Français de Radio Télévision
Diffuseur : TF1
Ayant droit : CFRT Productions - Comité Français de Radio Télévision

SWAMIJI - AN INNER JOURNEY, the documentary directed in 1984 by Patrice Chagnard, remains the definitive film about Henri Le Saux. It is now freely available online in master quality. Thank you, Patrice Chagnard, for entrusting it to Henri Le Saux TV https://www.youtube.com/@HenriLeSauxTV

A autobiographical narrative, combining the texts of Henri Le Saux, often of great beauty, and the memories of his loved ones, the journey of this Benedictine monk converted to Hinduism. Leaving for India in 1948 to found an ashram, a place of dialogue and confrontation between Christian mysticism and the different spiritual traditions of India, he chose to withdraw into solitude, at the source of the Ganges, in the Himalayas, and to lead there, until his death in 1973, the existence of a wandering Hindu monk, a sadhu.

episodes.title: Chartres Cathedral (1962)
episodes.description:
Chartres Cathedral by John Barnes

An in-depth study of this famous cathedral. "What is the special character of Chartres Cathedral that we should call it the greatest of the medieval churches?" Narrated by New York Times art critic John Canaday, Chartres becomes a visible fusion of faith, engineering and architecture. The camera pictures the cathedral in its awesome entirety, with detailed closeups, and as an enduring triumph of man's skills. For more on Barnes, visit http://www.afana.org/barnesbio.htm

episodes.title: Moments with Sri Nisargadatta Maharaj
episodes.description:
Moments with Sri Nisargadatta Maharaj : Archival Films 1979/1981 is a 115-minute documentary shot by Belgian devotee Jozef Nauwelaerts (often spelled Nauwelaerts in sources), documenting the final years of the Advaita master. The film provides a rare, intimate look at Nisargadatta's daily life in Mumbai, including a 35-minute Q&A session.

This film contains a short travelogue of Bombay and the colorful Maharaj district (including prostitutes) circa 1980, as well as a fully subtitled satsang featuring Nisargadatta Maharaj. The archival footage is astonishing. See if you can spot a young Ramesh Balsekar in the group. Another rare six-minute clip of Bhagavan Nityananda is also worth checking out.

This is a fine documentary filmed about two years prior to the passing of Nisargadatta Maharaj. Filmed, directed and narrated by the Belgium devotee Jozef Nauwelaerts. English subtitles. A gracious introduction from Stephen Wolinski. It provides a guided tour of Bombay and the section where Maharaj lived (Mumbai), and the upstairs room where Maharaj saw visitors. This rare footage features all of the activities of Maharaj... the morning ablutions, Puja, Satsang, purifications, bhajans indoors and outdoors. And he always scrubbed the alters and pictures of teachers and Gyanis. Self Realized beings are extremely rare. And probably even more rare are Realized ones who are articulate on this matter & who were recorded in real time both on film and word in book form. I can only think of two such beings, and therefore no one and no entity can twist their words. The message from Maharaj was to "seek only the Inner Knowledge." This film provides almost the experience of visiting his room when he was alive and many who did actually experienced the bliss (those ready for it). Blessings.

episodes.title: UFOs : The Contacts ~ a film by Michael Hesemann
episodes.description:
UFOs : The Contacts ~ a film by Michael Hesemann.

Alien visitors and their spacecraft have been depicted in Stone Age cave paintings and recorded in the sacred writings of virtually every ancient culture in human history. This feature-length movie presents evidence of ancient alien interventions that continue to shape our world today.

When Michael Hesemann was around 14 years old, his father had a UFO sighting that (as Michael Hesemann would recall three decades later) inspired his son to become a UFO researcher. Hesemann studied History and Cultural Anthropology at the University of Göttingen in Germany.

From 1984 to 1990 Hesemann published the German magazine Magazin 2000, which dealt with paranormal phenomena and religious topics. In 1990, he sold the Magazine and served as its editor-in-chief for the next decade. In 1995, together with his co-editor at Magazin 2000, Hesemann hosted a global ufology congress in Düsseldorf, Germany, where he presented alleged video evidence for the alien autopsy.

In 1999, he was accredited to the Holy See Press Office. In 2010, the Wall Street Journal described him as "a religious historian who helps the Vatican date relics". He is German representative of the Pave the Way Foundation (PTWF) for which he did research at the Vatican archives in 2010.

He co-founded Deutschland pro Papa, a conservative Catholic initiative which claims to represent the "silent majority of Rome-loyal Catholics." In 2013, he compiled an exhibition on the Turin Shroud for the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, touring through Germany and Austria as of 2015.

Together with Georg Ratzinger, Hesemann co-authored "My brother, the Pope".

In 2014 he claims to have located 2000 pages of documents on the Armenian genocide in the Vatican Archives. For this, in October 2016, he received an honorary doctorate of the National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Armenia.

Vatican

In the Vatican, he investigated the history of the alleged relic of the inscription of the cross of Jesus, hidden in Rome for nearly 1700 years. It was dated by seven Israeli experts for comparative palaeography - the established method to date inscriptions - into the 1st century. The relic is exhibited in the Basilica di Santa Croce.

His book The Pope who Defied Hitler. The Truth about Pius XII (2008) led him to claim that Pope Pius XII, sometimes referred to as the "Hitler Pope," was in fact responsible for saving hundreds of thousands of Jews.

Court order against Hesemann

In January 2013, a court in Hamburg ruled that Hesemann would have to pay a fine up to €250,000 if he continued libeling the German theologian David Berger. According to the ruling Hesemann had falsely affirmed that Berger had been one of the authors of the extreme right-wing Catholic (now closed) web site kreuz.net.

episodes.title: SADHANA (1988)
episodes.description:
A travelogue about India, seen through the eyes of Marcel Poulin, a young seeker following the call of his soul to the East. He travels from southern India to the source of the Ganges River in the Himalayas. Along the way, he meets holy men and spiritual teachers and spends time at the Hindu festival Kumbha Mela.

Jean-Pierre Piché, Sid Goldberg, Marcel Poulin, Productions des Temps Modernes (Firm), Productions Jean-Pierre Piché.

Television and Film PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxB1DoiLGVztJOvpgc0ZwdeU

In 1986 a film crew and I ventured to India's Kumbh Mela festival, humanity's largest gathering of people for the religious Hindu festival that occurs once every 12 yrs. Along the way, we met a number of spiritually inspiring leaders whose uplifting messages directed our attention, Back to the Source.

This is a must for all spiritual seekers interested in India’s legacy and it gives insight into the living spirit of Hinduism. This doco has been compared to SIDDHARTHA and MEETINGS WITH REMARKABLE MEN.

Travel through exotic India with a Western Seeker. See sacred religious events like the Kumbh Mela. Meet extraordinary Holy-men; Fr Bede Griffiths, Bhairav Muni, Swami Shyam and Swami Premananda, Swami Durgananda.

This feature film was seen on the Canadian Broadcasting Channel and played in over 100 repertory theaters across the US. 

This 80-min documentary is produced by Jean-Pierre Piche, with the on-camera experience of Marcel Poulin, and co-produced by Sid Goldberg.

“Breathtaking. It teaches us to understand the world by understanding the self” - Toronto Festival.

“A compelling docudrama and spiritually uplifting film” - Montreal Gazette.

A Spiritual Odyssey – Festival Review, Toronto

“Sadhana, the Enchanted Journey Back to the Source, a new Canadian documentary by Jean-Pierre Piché and Marcel Poulin recounts a singular and subjective search for freedom and self-knowledge. “Sadhana” means “the path to enlightenment” through yoga of the mind and body, but this is not a ‘how-to’ film, nor does it attempt to convert the onlooker; it documents Marcel’s conversations with his various spiritual leaders and uses narration to reveal Marcel’s own thoughts during his off-times stormy odyssey.

Fittingly, Marcel’s first spiritual guide is an old benedictine monk named Bede Griffiths who practices a combination of Christianity and Hinduism and guides his student toward the Eastern emphasis on meditation and mind relaxation as a means to attaining knowledge of the self. Beginning at the sacred mountain at Arunachala and the ashram, or temple dedicated to Sri Ramana Maharshi whose teachings on the self proved an inspiration to Marcel, this young disciple goes in search of a Hindu spiritual guide.

Swami Premananda is a smiling, soft-spoken young man who counsels Marcel to immerse himself in Indian culture and tradition as a starting point to his search for truth.

Marcel joins Bhairav Muni, a sadhu, a ‘seeker’ of enlightenment, accompanying him on his pilgrimages from one holy place to another until the ascetic leads him to the Kumbha Mela, a 40-day religious festival held at Hardwar, a holy city at the foot of the Himalayas. At the river basin where the Ganges starts its course along the plain, 80 million faithfuls come every 12 years to bathe in the water into which, according to Hindu mythology, the nectar of immortality had been dropped thousand of years ago. Weaving its way through endless crowds, the camera documents Marcel’s initiation to the ritual.

After the Kumbha Mela festivities, Marcel travels alone to the Valley of the Gods where he meets Swami Shyam (it means ‘Blue Space’) who helps him sort out his feelings and his experiences. “He was the living answer to my questions,” says Marcel of this charming, articulate and inspiring sage. Alone, these scenes of Marcel’s talks with Swami Shyam, a living example of Hindu enligthtenment are worth the price of admission. Breathtaking shots of the Himalayan valley tempt one to book a flight to India, while Marcel’s enlightening walks with the swami prepare him to finally seek his own answers with renewed self-confidence.

Sadhana is technically straightforward in its approach, well-paced and coherent. The screenplay, co-written by Marcel Poulin, Jean-Pierre Piché and Sid Goldberg focuses on a subjective journey toward self-knowledge; it is not overladden with religious or historic information and succeeds as a documentary by making the viewer curious for more details.

In our increasingly impersonal world of computers, multi-national corporations and ecological chaos, it is logical for an individual to search for a meaning to his life. Some will search for it in ritualized religion while others will strive to find it in ancient Eastern belief systems more closely aligned with nature. Sadhana teaches us to understand the world by understanding the self, for while the world may be in turmoil, our minds and spirits need not be.”

episodes.title: Stigmata : The Wounds of Christ? (1985)
episodes.description:
Arthur C. Clarke's World of Strange Powers : Stigmata : The Wounds of Christ? first aired on 24th April, 1985.

Arthur C. Clarke's World of Strange Powers is a thirteen-part British television series looking at strange worlds of the paranormal. It was produced by Yorkshire Television for the ITV network and first broadcast in 1985. It was the sequel to the 1980 series Arthur C. Clarke's Mysterious World.

The series is introduced by science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke in short sequences filmed at his home in Sri Lanka. Individual episodes are narrated by Anna Ford. The series was produced by John Fairley and directed by Peter Jones, Michael Weigall and Charles Flynn.

In 1984, G.P. Putnam's Sons published a hardcover book with the same name, authored by Simon Welfare and John Fairley, where the contents of the show were further explored. It featured an introduction written by Clarke as well as his remarks at the end of each chapter or topic. In 1985, a paperback of this book was released by HarperCollins Publishers.

The series was followed by Arthur C. Clarke's Mysterious Universe, broadcast in 1994.

episodes.title: Meeting Mary : Visions of the Virgin (1994)
episodes.description:
Arthur C.  Clarke's Mysterious Universe : Meeting Mary : Visions of the Virgin (1994) (ITV 1995) ~ Series 1, Episode 22.

Virgin Mary PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxALOcPW40XNBgFlAzW_igDP

Arthur C. Clarke investigates modern-day apparitions of the Virgin Mary in three distinct locations. Was a vision of the Virgin Mary really seen in Fatima, Portugal? In Ireland, believers and non-believers say they've seen a statue move. And is there a secret to the apparition of the Virgin Mary on a church wall in another part of Ireland? Does a video create doubt about the claims by young people in Bosnia Herzegovina of seeing visions?

Arthur C. Clarke's Mysterious Universe is a 26-part television series looking at unexplained phenomena across the universe. It was first broadcast in the United Kingdom by independent television network Discovery Channel. It premiered on 15 July 1994. It was the sequel to Arthur C. Clarke's Mysterious World and Arthur C. Clarke's World of Strange Powers.

The series is introduced by acclaimed science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke in short sequences filmed at his home in Sri Lanka, with individual episodes narrated by Carol Vorderman. The series was produced by John Fairley and directed by Peter Jones, Michael Weigall and Charles Flynn.

episodes.title: Hill Temples of Gujarat (1964)
episodes.description:
Hill Temples of Gujarat is a 1964 black-and-white documentary produced by the Films Division of India. Directed by Biren Das, this 13-minute English film provides a detailed pictorial survey of the architectural and sculptural beauty of prominent, elevated temples in Gujarat, specifically highlighting Palitana, Girnar, Taranga Hill, and Pavagadh. 

Locations:
Palitana: Jain temples on Shatrunjaya hill.
Girnar: Temples on the Girnar mountain range near Junagadh.
Taranga Hill: Known for its ancient Jain temple architecture.
Pavagadh: Site of the Kalika Mata temple.

episodes.title: Sree Chakravarti and Shirdi Sai Baba
episodes.description:
Sree Chakravarti and Shirdi Sai Baba is from https://www.youtube.com/@ThinkingAllowedTV

"This treatment is no hushed, mystical, spiritual experience," writes Veronica Hauge, "For a moment, before she starts to treat you, Sreema will sit quietly, her face turned away as she takes a deep breath to center herself and concentrate her powers. 

But while her hand vibrates, she will chat about everything under the sun, smiling and laughing." Hauge is relating her experience with Sree Chakravarti, a self-described "Delhi housewife" who possesses an extraordinary power to diagnose and treat illnesses. 

"My theory," explains Sreema, "is that sickness is caused when electrons in the atoms of the ailing area act abnormally. It seems my right hand possesses some kind of magnetic vibration, and I believe this vibration, or radiation, helps to adjust the electrons and create a magnetic field that balances the body. I believe that my power to heal comes from Sai Baba, the saint of Shirdi (who passed on in 1918)."

Sreema's book, A Healer's Journey, is a kind of shaman's Travels of Marco Polo, with our heroine periodically departing her relatively sheltered life in Delhi to heal the ill and convert the skeptical. She travels far and wide, treating the Saudi royal family, dumbfounding groups of Western doctors in Lebanon, the United Kingdom and America, and in general demonstrating a truly extraordinary gift. The book abounds with descriptions and testimonies of her healings. 

James George, former ambassador of Canada to India (also Sri Lanka and Nepal), testifies that Sreema healed a tumor on his back. George told Hinduism Today, "She is one of those exceptionally rare people who know the inner power is not their own, but is a power they serve. She is an exceptional soul."

Ashrams of India Volume 1 : Samadhi Mandir of Shirdi Sai Baba

Shirdi Sai Baba (27 or 28 September 1838 - 15 October 1918). Also known as Sai Baba of Shirdi and Shirdi Baba, he was regarded by his devotees as a saint, fakir, and satguru. He was revered by both his Hindu and Muslim devotees. During and as well as after his life, it remained uncertain if he was a Hindu or a Muslim, this however was of no consequence to Sai Baba himself. Sai Baba opposed all persecution based on religion or caste. Although Sai Baba himself led the life of an ascetic, he advised his followers to lead an ordinary family life, encouraging them to pray, chant God’s name, and read holy scriptures. He advised his devotees to lead a moral life, help others, love every living being without any discrimination, and develop two important features of character: devotion to the Guru (Sraddha) and waiting cheerfully with patience and love.

episodes.title: Sathya Sai Baba 50th Birthday Celebrations
episodes.description:
This 1976 Documentary is of the 50th birthday celebrations (23rd November, 1975) of Sathya Sai Baba that was a 10 day (14th - 24th November) Brahmotsavam (a festival of Divine bliss and ecstasy).

In this film, we see the first Rathotsavam and the inauguration of the Sarva Dharma Aikya Stupa, interviews by devotees such as Dr. S Bhagavantham and Dr. John Hislop. 

Sathya Sai Baba arrives in a helicopter on the morning of His birthday, officiating the 3rd World Conference of SSSIO, presiding over the Purushottama Yagna, inaugurating the Sarva Dharma Stupa, and swinging on the Jhoola on the final evening.

This film has been previously posted on the channel as Sathya Sai Baba (November, 1975).

episodes.title: Yogi S.A.A. Ramaiah and Mahavatar Babaji's Place Of Birth
episodes.description:
Ashrams of India Volune 2 : Babaji Temple (the birthplace of Mahavatar Babaji) Place of birth in 203 AD of Indian saint, yogi and deathless avatar Babaji, who currently resides in the remote Himalayan regions of India, revealing himself only rarely to a blessed few...

00:00 Intro
05:07 Mahavatar Babaji's Place Of Birth

S.A.A. Ramaiah who co-founded the Kriya Babaji Sangah to propagate the Kriya Yoga teachings of Babaji, built a temple for him here at his place of birth, as revealed to himself and V.T. Neelakantan in 1953. Ramaiah and Neelakantan say that Babaji was born in 203 AD in Parangipettai (Porto Novo) near Cuddalore and is still thought to be alive in the Himalayas, near Badrinath. The Mahavatar Babaji temple is a very simple single shrine temple with an adjacent meditation hall. On either side of the sanctum sanctorum, there are sculptures of Lord Ganesha and Lord Muruga as he appeared before Babaji in Kataragama, Sri Lanka. There is a Yaga Gundam in front of the shrine called Gowri Shankar Peetam. On the sides of the shrine are panels depicting various incidents conveyed to S.A.A. Ramaiah by Babaji, that occurred in his life and that of his primary disciples. There are two decorative pillars in front of the shrine which bear images of his primary disciples. Behind the temple is a meditation hall that has an idol of S.A.A. Ramaiah and paintings of Mahavatar Babaji and incidents of his life. Every Thursday, abhishekam is performed for Babaji and special pujas are held on his birthday. 

The temple is open from 6.00 to 9.30 am and 6.00 to 9.00 pm daily, however you may need to call the caretaker in advance to get on to the grounds and so that the meditation room can be opened for you.

29:10 December, 1994

Ashrams of India Volume 2 : Yogi Ramsuratkumar Ashram ~ Ashram of Yogi Ramsuratkumar (01 December 1918 - 20 February 2001) a saint and mystic.

Yogi Ramsuratkumar Ashram is on 3.5 acres of land. There is a hall that can accommodate 4000 people, and a small museum with Ramsuratkumar’s artefacts. Yogi Ramsuratkumar’s mahasamadhi is inside the hall. Annadhanam (offering food) for Sadhus is provided every day. There is a dormitory to accommodate devotees.

The Bhagawan Yogi Ramsuratkumar Kindergarten is run by the ashram. It runs on the foundation of Indian culture, dharma and tradition. A free medical camp is organised by the ashram on every second Sunday. 

The ashram is now under the care of Justice Arunachalam and is assisted by Ma Devaki and Ma Vijayalakshmi.

03:24 Traveling by ship and automobile through Europe ~ The entourage visited England, Scotland, France, Belgium, Holland and Switzerland. In Italy they visited Venice, Assisi and Rome, and embarked from Brindisi for Athens

episodes.title: Howard Levin's interviews with Sathya Sai Baba
episodes.description:
American Howard Levin first arrives on the Whitefield ashram Brindavan, June 5th, 1970. He visited India during the late 1960s and while on his travels, he had heard about Sathya Sai Baba from others who had visited his ashram in South India. Howard decided to visit. He enjoyed many interviews with Sai Baba, and also experienced other phenomena that took place around the ashram. His book, Good Chances is an account from those days. Toward the end Sai Baba said to him “You must remember these days we’ve spent together. Now it is outside, next memory goes into your mind, then a permanent picture is there. When you all go back to America, if you think of these ‘good chances’ with Swami, it will be the same as meditation.

Howard’s books ~ 'Good Chances' (1985) and the sequel 'Heart to Heart' (1996).

Shiva Mahavatar Babaji by Pola Churchill. In the Kumaon foothills of the Indian Himalayan mountains, where great saints and yogis of the past and present have made their ancestral homes since the beginning of creation, resides Shiva Mahavatar Babaji, known to millions in the West through Paramahansa Yogananda's book, Autobiography of a Yogi. In 1970, Shri Babaji, the deathless Master, appeared as a youth of 18 years old in a cave at the foot of Mount Kailash in the state of Samadhi. He displayed great wisdom and divine powers and was recognized by people as the great Mahavatar reincarnated. His coming was foretold both by saints and ancient scriptures. He came to reform the hearts and minds of men, uplift humanity during troubled times, and to teach and restore the Sanatan Dharma (eternal religion) of truth, simplicity, love, unity, and selfless service to God. (Karma Yoga). This book records His teachings and the extraordinary accounts of people's dreams, visions and encounters that bear witness to His omnipresence. This book is written with the intention for people to experience Babaji through these pages, so it will inspire you to investigate this fascinating Being for yourselves.

Eternal Breath : A Biography of Leonard Orr Founder of Rebirthing Breathwork by Pola Churchill. Eternal Breath-A Biography of Leonard Orr by Pola Churchill is a unique classic. There is beautiful "light" streaming both from the writing style and content, it touches the soul. It is explosive and revolutionary!

Leonard Orr is one of the Pioneers and Originators of the Human Potential Movement along with contemporary folk heroes, Earl Nightingale, Maxwell Maltz, Carl Rodgers and Abraham Moslow.

Leonard has written thirty books in over a dozen languages including: Rebirthing in the New Age, The Story of Rebirthing Breathwork, Babaji Angel of the Lord, Government without Taxes, How to Make Democracy Work, Breaking the Death Habit.... His International Rebirthing Breathwork Movement has served over a ten million people on six continents.

Ashrams of India Volume 1 : Sri Kaleshwar Ashram, the ashram of Sri Kaleshwar. In 1993, Sri Kaleshwar founded the five-acre Sri Kaleshwar Ashram in the South Indian village of Penukonda. Penukonda is a sacred power spot with a long history of association with many saints and divine souls. The ashram is situated next to the summer residence of King Krishnadevaraya (1471 - 1529) and within the walls of the ancient fort. The Shiva Sai Mandir contains temples to both Shirdi Baba and Jesus, the Dwarkamai, a meditation temple that is used in divine processes to open the higher spiritual channels. A multi-story apartment complex sits in the south and southwest of the ashram.

episodes.title: God's Pharmacy of Herbs ~ Maria Treben (1984)
episodes.description:
Maria Treben became famous through her two books: Health Through God's Pharmacy and Maria Treben's Cures. The first was translated into 24 languages and sold over 8 million copies.

Treben addressed seminars and presented at natural health conferences in Germany, Austria and across Europe, attracting hundreds of people. She is perceived as a pioneer of the renewed interest for natural remedies and traditional medicine at the end of the 20th century.

Remedies: Treben used traditional German and Eastern European remedies handed down from previous generations. She only used local herbs and always accompanied her remedies with advice on diet. She commonly used Thyme, Greater Celandine, Ramsons, Speedwell, Calamus, Chamomile, Nettle and Lady's Mantle. She treated a broad range of conditions from psoriasis to constipation and diabetes to insomnia. She used her own recipes as well as traditional healing remedies like Swedish bitters that she used as a cure-all. Some of her remedies and advice proved to be controversial, such as some of the more esoteric ingredients used in the greater Swedish bitters recipe. To this day she is widely read and referred to for her knowledge of European medicinal herbs.

episodes.title: Conrad Rooks
episodes.description:
Conrad Rooks (December 15, 1934 in Kansas City, Missouri – December 27, 2011 in Massachusetts) was an American writer, director and producer most well known for his 1972 filmed adaptation of Hermann Hesse's novel Siddhartha.

Conrad Rooks’ life is fascinating in many ways. Partly through the outer life experience in itself – a comfortable financial background, becoming a misfit, an escapist, getting caught in various forms of dependency, inheriting $3 million in the 1960s, using the money to make his films. But also partly through the inner journey, with initial restlessness, losing his free will to drugs and drink, later reclaiming it and, even later, the need to tell of his experiences in a very poetic manner.

Through all of these phases, inner as well as outer, Rooks has had metaphysical beacons guiding him through the stormy seas of the soul: American Indian shamanism, psychedelics, Hinduism and Buddhism. The phenomenon that he has mostly become associated with - the ”Beat” culture - is probably what affected him the least.
