episodes.title: Mother Krishnabai
episodes.description:
Ramdas continued his travels over India for the next few years, finally settling down in a small ashram built by one of his devotees at Kasaragod, Kerala. It was here where a chance meeting in 1928 between Swami Ramdas and Mother Krishnabai, a moment she describes as being one of the most peaceful in her life, having just lost her husband she decided then to dedicate her entire life to his service and the institution established by him. 

Eventually, the will of God caused him to leave Kasaragod and settle down in Kanhangad, where the present Anandashram was founded in the year 1931. The ashram worked to improve the living conditions of the local people and continues to this day to share Swami Ramdas’s vision of Universal Love and Service.

After Swami Ramdas’s mahasamadhi in 1963, the running of the ashram went to Mata Krishnabai who continued to serve and look after the affairs of Anandashram until her mahasamadhi in 1989.

Mother Krishnabai told her devotees, “Sai Baba is an Avatar, a full incarnation of Krishna. He is Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva together in one form! She recommended they spend as much time in His presence as possible.

episodes.title: Frédérick Leboyer in India
episodes.description:
Ashrams of India Volume Volume 2 : Channa Ashram, the ashram of Niralamba Swami.

“To have children . . . it is one of the greatest privileges that life holds.” Frédérick Leboyer (1918 - 2017), the Poet of Birth and Obstetrician best known for his revolutionary 1974 book, Birth Without Violence. In an interview, Irena Edrovska asked Leboyer about the father’s role during birth, to which he replied “He has to move away. Being pregnant is like going on a pilgrimage. The woman is going on an inner pilgrimage. She is going to the spring of Life. And the man cannot follow, he cannot go there. And he should not try.” He met perhaps the biggest influence on his life, Swami Prajnanpad while travelling through India, who believed human beings carried the memory of their births deep within themselves. Françoise Freedman, Founder and Director of Birthlight, says “Swami Prajnanpad, influenced him in his quest from non-violence (ahimsa), to yoga and on to “inner light,” the art of breathing and the art of loving touch and sound in the sacred gateway of birth.”

episodes.title: Staying On
episodes.description:
Staying On (1980) is the follow up to the 'Raj Quartet' (later to be filmed as The Jewel in the Crown) and was made prior to the filming of The Jewel in the Crown. The success of Staying On paved the way for Granada to film the Raj Quartet book series.

Pankot, India, 1972. Colonel Tusker Smalley and his wife Lucy live in the annexe lodge of the Smiths Hotel, which dates back to the Raj. They are childless. The Colonel was a deskbound soldier in the British army who opted to stay back after India gained independence in 1947.

The passing years have made the Colonel more and more irascible and foul mouthed. The hotel is run by Frankie Bhoolabhoy, who manages it, and his wife, the owner. While Frankie meets the Colonel for a drink almost every evening and reminisces about the old Raj days, Mrs Bhoolabhoy plots to get rid of the Smalleys from her property.

Lucy is lonely but happy and caters to the Colonel's every whim. They also have a love-hate relationship with their manservant, Ibrahim. The Colonel suffers from a heart attack, and his activities are severely curtailed. He grows irritable over the smallest of things, and begins dwelling on his own mortality.

Eventually, Mrs Bhoolabhoy makes plans to sell the hotel and sends a notice to the Smalleys. The Colonel is unable to bear the shock and dies. Lucy is left alone.

The Jewel in the Crown is a 1984 British television serial about the final days of the British Raj in India during and after World War II, based on British author Paul Scott's Raj Quartet novels. Granada Television produced the series for the ITV network.

episodes.title: Indian Journeys
episodes.description:
Celebrated travel-writer William Dalrymple, author of the award-winning book “City of the Djinns,” travels across India looking at the country’s great spiritual past and troubled present.

This 2002 trilogy, written and presented by William and produced and directed by Hugh Thomson, makes three ambitious journeys into what is for William familiar territory.

00:00 Programme 1 “Shiva’s Matted Locks” 
In the first of the 50 minute programmes William walks in the tracks of the many bare-footed pilgrims and holy men who have journeyed up into the High Himalayas to reach the breathtaking source of the River Ganges. The pilgrimage is an awe-inspiring journey and one that is revered by India’s Hindus.

48:32 Programme 2 “City of Djinns” 
The second of William’s journeys takes him deep into the soul of Delhi to discover the ancient rites of Sufism - a potent mix of the traditions and customs of many religions, chiefly Hinduism and Islam. He discovers, too, the deep-seated antagonism that exists between India’s two major religions and asks ‘is Sufism the answer?’

01:37:39 Programme 3 “Doubting Thomas”
The final part of the trilogy begins with an extraordinary, epic voyage supposedly undertaken by Christ’s apostle St Thomas in the first century, when he sailed from Palestine down to the south of India. William follows an ancient manuscript - The Acts of St Thomas - which details the apostle’s legendary journey and sets out to discover whether the fabled voyage and subsequent spread of Christianity in Southern India by ‘doubting Thomas’ is fact or fiction.

As an 18-year-old back-packer William Dalrymple fell in love with India - a country which has been his home, on and off, in the years since that first visit.

He has put his remarkable understanding and passion for the country - he’s a confident speaker of Hindi - to great effect in several best-selling books, his most-recent being ‘The Age of Kali.’

William is not only an expert on the ancient world but has also been The Independent’s correspondent in India and a special feature writer for The Sunday Times.

Series producer and director Hugh Thomson has made many arts and travel documentaries for the BBC, including the award-winning Dancing In The Street: A Rock and Roll History.

Indian Journeys is a welcome return to Asia for Hugh and Icon Films, who made one of their popular and critically acclaimed films there - In The Kingdom of the Thunder Dragon - in which Joanna Lumley traced a journey made by her grandparents in 1931 through the Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan.

episodes.title: Autumn in the Himalayas
episodes.description:
Elderly nuns from Ladakh and their call for dignity. Directed by Malgorzata Skiba. Producer and Commissioning Editor: Rajiv Mehrotra. Produced by PSBT in partnership with Doordarshan India http://www.psbt.org/ http://www.ddindia.gov.in

This is a film from 2008 about the position of the non-ordained nuns in Ladakh, who are known as Chomo. Their position historically has been very poor and disadvantaged, often lacking any formal education, either secular or religious, living as single women in their parents’ home and looking after their relatives’ children, while working for their living.

Recently this has begun to change and the women have started organising themselves, building nunneries and raising donations, etc. which in itself has raised their status in society. They have also managed to get support from the male monasteries, and donations from abroad, all of which will help a new generation in the future.

This film by Malgorzata Skiba looks first at the old life, and contrasts it with the life of novices and monks in the nearby monasteries, then shows how they have been working to improve their lot, often building with their own hands the roads and buildings needed. It is in many ways an inspiring story and simply told, but one can’t help wonder why their position was so poor for so long.

episodes.title: Divine Shiva Yogi Come to Me
episodes.description:
Edited from two reels of 8mm colour film recorded in Adivarapupeta in March of 1963 https://www.youtube.com/@TheShivabalayogi/videos

Shivabalayogi PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxA1q03pBO49LlbcaKxDG6ps

These are believed to be the earliest film of Shivabalayogi. They were taken around the time of Mahashivaratri and shortly before Shivabalayogi left Adivarapupeta for the first time to begin three decades of travel throughout India, then in the West.

We see the place by the Godavari River canal where 14-year-old Sathyaraju experienced samadhi (enlightenment) and was made to sit in tapas – 23 hours a day meditating in samadhi.  We also see the Dhyana Mandir, the meditation temple in which Shivabalayogi spent the last ten of his twelve years of tapas, and where he consecrated Ardhanarishwara linga and an idol of Parvati Devi.

The films also show Shivabalayogi in procession with his mother, Parvatamma Allaka, through Adivarapupeta village, and many, many scenes of bhava samadhi – divine trance.
Most amazing are scenes of Shivabalayogi in samadhi inside the ashram building – and when he opens his eyes.

The original films have no soundtrack.  The bhajans “Shivayogideva Ravela” (Divine Shiva Yogi Come to Me) and “Om Namah Shivaya” were recorded in Adivarapupeta in 1994.  The procession sound was also recorded in Adivarapupeta, in March of 1994 when Shivabalayogi entered in procession for his final return in his physical body.

Shivabalayogi https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxA1q03pBO49LlbcaKxDG6ps

Ashrams of India Volume 1 : Shiva Bala Yogi (24 January 1935 - 28 March 1994) was given the name of Satyaraju at birth. At the age of 14, Lord Shiva manifested to the boy in the form of an imposing seven-foot ascetic touching the boy between the eyebrows (the third eye) and he immediately experienced samadhi (enlightenment).

This event marked the beginning of an intense tapas in which Shivabalayogi meditated in samadhi for 23 hours every day for eight years, then at least 12 hours every day for four more years. Throughout these twelve years, there were periods when he stayed in samadhi continuously for months at a time.

episodes.title: Bharatanatyam (1956)
episodes.description:
Featuring the danseuse Kamala, the film explains the unique features in the technique of Bharatanatyam. It also presents the various dance numbers of Bharatanatyam beginning with the 'Jati Swaram.'

Discover the enchanting world of Bharatanatyam, an ancient Indian classical dance form originating from South India. With its roots dating back to the Natya Shastra and the Tamil epic Silappatikaram, Bharatanatyam is a cherished art form that expresses profound religious and spiritual themes of Hinduism and Jainism.

Bharatanatyam is characterized by its distinctive bani or tradition, which varies according to the guru or school. The dance style is renowned for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and flexed knees (Aramandi), combined with intricate footwork and a vocabulary of expressive gestures using hands, eyes, and facial muscles.

Originally known as Sadiraattam, Bharatanatyam holds a special place as the state dance form of Tamil Nadu. Over the centuries, it has evolved from its origins in Hindu temples to become a popular art form celebrated across India and beyond. Despite facing challenges such as colonial restrictions, Bharatanatyam has persevered and flourished, thanks to the efforts of dedicated practitioners and supporters.

The performance repertoire of Bharatanatyam includes pure dance (nrita), expressive movements (nritya), and dramatic storytelling (natya), accompanied by live music and vocals. The Thanjavur Quartet played a significant role in shaping the modern structure of Bharatanatyam, ensuring its continued relevance and innovation.

Join us on a captivating journey through the timeless beauty and cultural significance of Bharatanatyam, as we explore its rich history, vibrant expressions, and enduring legacy that continue to inspire audiences worldwide.

#india

episodes.title: Patachitra (1980)
episodes.description:
Patachitra is a scroll painting practised by village folk of India. During Buddha’s time it was known as Charan Chitra. Patas were used as audio-visuals for religious and social instruction and entertainment. In Maharashtra, the entertainer Patas are called Chitrakathi. Patas of Rajasthan, Orissa, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh are also interesting. The district of Midnapore in West Bengal has the remnants of once flourishing Patua community.  They are said to be the children of Viswakarma, the celestial architect. In Birbhum district also Patuas once painted wonderful patas. But now they have to struggle a lot to make their both ends meet. This film presents various facets of the pata tradition.

Discover the vibrant world of Patachitra, a cherished form of scroll painting practiced by village communities across India. Rooted in ancient tradition, Patachitra, also known as Charan Chitra during Buddha's time, is a unique blend of art, religion, and entertainment.

In this captivating documentary, we journey through the diverse landscapes of India, from Maharashtra to Rajasthan, Orissa to Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal. Each region boasts its own distinct style of Patachitra, reflecting the nation's rich cultural tapestry.

Originally used for religious instruction and entertainment, Patachitra has a long history dating back centuries. In Maharashtra, these storytellers are known as Chitrakathi, weaving tales of myth and legend through intricate paintings.

However, the story of Patachitra is not without its challenges. In West Bengal's Midnapore district, we encounter the remnants of the once-flourishing Patua community. Despite their rich cultural heritage, many Patuas now face economic hardships, struggling to preserve their traditions in a modernized world.

But amidst these challenges, the spirit of Patachitra endures. In Birbhum district, we witness the enduring legacy of Patuas who once painted magnificent scrolls, preserving their cultural heritage for future generations.

Through stunning visuals and heartfelt interviews, this film celebrates the timeless beauty of Patachitra and pays homage to the artisans who keep this ancient tradition alive. Join us on a journey into the heart of India's folk art tradition, where every brushstroke tells a story and every scroll is a testament to the enduring spirit of creativity and resilience.

episodes.title: Chartres Cathedral ~ A Sacred Geometry ~ Professor Keith Critchlow
episodes.description:
This 2003 documentary is unique in its attempt to combine information about some of the architectural features of Chartres Cathedral with a search into the mysteries, the deeper meaning and purpose of a sacred place. Are there sacred sites? How do they affect us, if we allow ourselves to be sensitive to their energies?

How can Chartres Cathedral be understood, in terms of its sacred geometry? One hour is too short a time to unravel all its mysteries, but it can point the viewer towards some of the Cathedral’s deeper meanings. The documentary aims to both uplift and inspire, and leave the viewer with a feeling of hope, of being part of a wider community capable of working together in harmony, as were those who built Chartres Cathedral in 12th century France.

Memorable images of Chartres Cathedral’s stained glass windows, striking stonework and statues, the famous labyrinth and beautiful music by American composer Richard Einhorn, accompany an insightful commentary. Professor Keith Critchlow, a leading specialist in Sacred Geometry and Architecture, elaborates on his personal findings about the cathedral, and guides us with knowledge and wisdom throughout the documentary. Malcolm Miller, the well-known author, and Chartres Cathedral tour guide, offers his own perspective on the Cathedral and its Christian symbolism. The documentary represents a perfect starting point for those who may be interested in all things Sacred. It is an ideal resource for architectural students and those who want to know more about medieval buildings, European history and culture.

This documentary has now (2014) been re-mastered and reissued by the Producer and Director of the film, Louise Illig-Mooncie.

Louise Illig-Mooncie https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1cRhwHNSsNA&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

Keith Barry Critchlow (16 March 1933 – 8 April 2020) was born in London, UK in 1933. He was an Artist, lecturer, author, Sacred Geometer and professor of architecture and a co-founder of the Temenos Academy and Kairos Charity, both in the UK.

2019 Interview with Louise Illig-Mooncie, author of ‘Encounter Between Two Worlds.' German-born Louise Illig Mooncie has written about the coming to terms with her country’s uneasy past. Her spiritual journey has taken her to the UK, India and Ireland and she shares her experiences in the book Encounter Between Two Worlds. 

Q This book feels like a lifetime’s journey.

It is indeed a life-time’s journey, my soul-journey. It has been a search for a deeper meaning and understanding of life’s challenges and mysteries. I have a wealth of memories from a very young age of my world in post-war Germany with all of its difficulties and secrets. That’s where it all started and it’s when I started to try and make sense of the past.

Obviously, Germany is my birthplace and I maintained strong links with it after I moved to the UK through working for German TV in London. Following my divorce and  raising my son as a single parent, I almost reached burn-out as I started my spiritual journey. I felt that by staying in England I would find what I was looking for.

This search for peace and understanding finally led me to a guru (teacher) in India. At the time, I wrote a diary about this life-changing journey and my slow spiritual transformation. I experienced a warm feeling of home-coming and a deep inner happiness in India. And indeed, this happiness is still in my heart. It is not tied to a particular country or place, it is there at any moment.

I must mention that Ireland also played a pivotal role in my life, having had a near-death experience while visiting a friend in Dublin (described in the book). I am very fond of the people and the landscape.

Q From your book, it seems that one of the key turning points was your meeting with The Jewish Ghost?

Without this extraordinary experience my book would not exist. This was the WOW effect in my life, changing my way of thinking about my own life, and everyone else’s for that matter, completely upside down. I started researching the possibility of reincarnation and felt very lucky when the BBC ran a well researched series of programmes about this subject, exactly when I needed it most (please see below for details).

For many years I did not speak to anyone about my ‘encounter’ with The Jewish Ghost, which I believed was a meeting with, or vision of, myself in a former life. I spoke about it only to the well known author and psychic from Tunbridge Wells, Peggy Mason. She shed some light on my experience and I describe this in my book.

Although my book is about my personal journey, I believe that the message of peace is relevant to all of us. We, as a human race, are all connected with one another. The whole of creation is connected, everything is one, one breath, one heartbeat. With my book I am trying to make an offering for peace in the world, peace in our hearts.

Q Does your belief in reincarnation affect the way that you live?

Definitely! I think about the consequences of my actions-reactions much more, and I’ve pledged to myself to live a truthful, loving and compassionate life.

Q Who or what has had the greatest influence on your life?

I’m a child of the 60s and people like Martin Luther King, Gandhi and Albert Schweizer (the humanitarian) made a great impact on me, not to forget the Beatles whose records my father banned me from playing at home. When I was young, my generation desperately wanted to change Germany, to make it less ‘dusty’ and rigid. In those days, we looked to England for guidance.

Buddhism, the Dalai Lama and my Indian Guru played a big role in my life. Now I’m a ‘free spirit’, believing that all of us have a place and a role to play: unity in diversity.

Chartres Cathedral 

Q I understand that before you wrote this book, you filmed a documentary in India called ‘The Miracle of Puttaparthi’ and another in France?

episodes.title: The Arcadian Shepherds
episodes.description:
Et in Arcadia ego (also known as Les bergers d'Arcadie or The Arcadian Shepherds) is a 1637–38 painting by Nicolas Poussin (1594–1665), the leading painter of the classical French Baroque style. It depicts a pastoral scene with idealised shepherds from classical antiquity, and a woman, possibly a shepherdess, gathered around an austere tomb that includes this inscription. It is held in the Louvre. Poussin painted two versions of the subject under the same title. His earlier version, painted in 1627, is held at Chatsworth House. An earlier treatment of the theme was painted by Guercino circa 1618–1622, also titled Et in Arcadia ego.

episodes.title: L'Or du diable
episodes.description:
L'Or du diable est une série télévisée française en 6 épisodes de 52 minutes, en couleur, réalisée par Jean-Louis Fournier d’après le roman de Jean-Michel Thibaux et diffusée en 1989 sur FR3.

L’histoire vraie d’un jeune prêtre. L’abbé Bérenger Saunière est nommé curé de Rennes-le-Château, un petit village de la région du bas Languedoc ou subsistent des vestiges de l’ancien royaume des Wisigoths. Quelques années plus tard, il entreprend des travaux considérables, rebâtit l’église, achète des terrains, construit une villa et une tour médiévale. Il mène grand train, voyage, fréquente le monde politique et les artistes. En 1917, il meurt subitement sans avoir livré le secret de sa fabuleuse fortune. La question reste posée : quel était le secret de l’abbé Saunière ?

00:00 Episode 1 : Une étrange paroisse
47:52 Episode 2 : Le secret du Maître autel
01:37:32 Episode 3 : La force du destin
02:28:08 Episode 4 : L’Or du Diable
03:19:59 Episode 5 : La confession de l’abbé Boudet
04:14:58 Episode 6 : L’habit rouge

Rennes-le-Château https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxDJX9mFm_5cqaNWDvPJ20Oh

Le film fut tourné en décors naturels à Pégairolles-de-Buèges, dans la forêt domaniale de Saint-Guilhem-le-Désert et la grotte de Clamouse. Les scènes d'opéra ont été tournées à l'opéra de Montpellier. Le Château de l'Engarran, à Lavérune, représente le château de Cabrières, près de Millau. Mais Cabrières n'est pas une folie du xviie siècle comme dans la mini-série, mais un château médiéval restauré au xixe siècle dans un un style néo-gothique.

The true story of a young priest. Father Bérenger Saunière is appointed parish priest of Rennes-le-Château, a small village in the lower Languedoc region where vestiges of the ancient kingdom of the Visigoths remain. A few years later, he undertook considerable work, rebuilt the church, bought land, built a villa and a medieval tower. He leads a great lifestyle, travels, frequents the political world and artists. In 1917, he died suddenly without having revealed the secret of his fabulous fortune. The question remains: what was Abbé Saunière’s secret?

episodes.description:
Darshan l'etreinte (2005) is a film about Mata Amritanandamayi by Jan Kounen.

Throughout its history, India has kept a profound sense of the sacred. Hindu tradition offers a privileged place to “great souls” (Mahatma), to spiritual guides. As a travel diary deep inside the heart of India and Hinduism, “Darshan” focuses on one of the most important Mahatmas still alive : Amma.

This woman has won a very important place in the Indian community today. For the very first time, Amma agreed to open the doors of her own world to a foreign director. Jan Kounen had the opportunity to accompany her across India, from Jaipur to Calcutta, via Benares.

episodes.title: Sri Ramana Maharshi (1982)
episodes.description:
Produced by Krishnaswamy Associates Private Ltd in 1982. Drawn from his home by the power of Arunachala, one of India's traditional holy sites, at the age of sixteen, he challenged death by a penetrating enquiry into the source of his being. He perfectly embodied the ultimate truth of Self-realisation, or complete absorption in the Supreme itself, and stayed for the rest of his life as the Sage of Arunachala. Hailed as Bhagavan Sri Ramana Maharshi he revealed the direct path of practice of Self-enquiry and awakened mankind to the immense spiritual power of the holy Arunachala Hill. This video biography was produced and directed by Dr. S. Krishnaswamy, founder of Krishnaswamy Associates Private Ltd, Madras.

episodes.title: Paramhansa Hariharananda Giri Biography
episodes.description:
Ashrams of India Volume 2 : Hariharananda Gurukulam, the ashram of Swami Hariharananda Giri. 

Hariharananda Gurukulam is 3 km from the Hotel Toshali Sands and is situated in the natural surroundings of forest, fruit trees and gardens near the Jagannath Temple. It is a place for meditation, prayer, and worship. Hariharananda Giri obtained this 50-acre property in 1975. In December 1995, he called his monk and successor Swami Prajnanananda Giri to tell him about an exceptional visionary dream. In the dream, Sri Yukteswar directed Hariharananda to transfer the Balighai property to the name of Prajnanananda and predicted that in the future the property would become a beautiful place of international reputation where many people would come to meditate.

The ashram has accommodation for more than 300 guests, a large dining hall, a Shiva temple, a Hariharananda museum, a library and health centre. Adi Kutir, the small straw roofed cottage is Hariharananda’s room where his physical body lay during the final darshan. It now serves as a meditation room as well as the residence of Paramahamsa Prajnanananda. Across from this cottage is a building that has a large meditation hall, Yogananda Yoga Mandir, with a second floor that holds two hundred people. The Yukteswar Library is on the third floor and has a large collection of scriptures and many spiritual books by many saints and authors of the world.

The Brahmananda Sant Nivas and the Patanjali Yati Nivas are the residences for the swamis, Satyananda Brahmachari Nivas is the dormitory for the brahmacharis who reside at the ashram. The ashram has a dormitory, Nabin Kali Matru Nivas, for visiting female disciples. Shyamacharan Bhakta Nivas houses the visiting male disciples.

episodes.title: Shivapuri Baba
episodes.description:
Ashrams of India Volume 2 : Shivapuri Baba Ashram, ashram and samadhi of Shivapuri Baba who spent 40 years circumnavigating the world, meeting world leaders of his day. Shivapuri Baba aka Govindananda Bharathi (27 September 1826 - January 1963). Shivapuri Baba was born as a twin and lived to be a hundred and thirty-seven years old.

00:12 Shivapuri Baba and J.G. Bennett, author of The Long Pilgrimage - The Life and Teachings of Shivapuri Baba (Swami Govindananda Bharti). Bennett was the disciple of George Ivanovich Gurdjieff, whose external and internal journey was documented in his book "Meetings with Remarkable Men."

01:21 One of the few known and accessible recordings today of the voice of Shivapuri Baba. Recorded by J.G. Bennett between April 1 and 2, 1962, nine months before the Master left his body. The interview was also attended by: Marjorie von Harten, Melissa Marston (England).

episodes.title: The Shamanic Roots of Yoga
episodes.description:
"Yoga & Plant Medicine" by Brian James https://www.amzn.com/1088479847
 
PODCAST: http://medicinepathpodcast.com

A short documentary that traces the roots of yoga from its ancient origins to the present day, telling the story through historical art, photos and ancient texts.

This short film tells the story of how the first yogis who used the entheogenic plant brew Soma to access states of ecstasy developed the postures, breathwork, mantra and meditation practices of hatha yoga to achieve the same results.

Written and produced by Brian James / http://brianjames.ca
Music by Benjy Wertheimer / http://benjymusic.com

Many images for this film were taken from the excellent book Yoga: The Art of Transformation, Smithsonian Books, 2013

Dedicated to the teachers that awaken the inner healer in each of us.

episodes.title: Chi è Sathya Sai Baba Preview
episodes.description:
Questa è una "Preview" di un  documento storico...il documentario di Victor Tognola girato a Puttaparthi nello Stato dell' Andhra Pradesh su Sathya Sai Baba, Avatar, Guru, il Cristo che camminò in India. Scienziati e uomini di cultura analizzano il fenomeno Sai Baba: Materializzava con le Sue mani la Cenere Sacra "Vibuthi," anelli, collane, orologi per i Suoi devoti. Gli innumerevoli Suoi miracoli, le guarigioni ed i fantastici racconti sull'Uomo Divino più straordinario che abbiate mai incontrato.

"Ho deciso di pubblicare questo piccolo montaggio come Testimonianza di Verità in quanto sono stato testimone personalmente di alcuni dei "Fenomeni Miracolosi," qui descritti, accaduti precisamente nel Gennaio del 1997 durante l'incontro in interview con Sathya Sai Baba e il Sottoscritto assieme ad un Gruppo di Devoti appartenenti al Centro Sai di Milano di Via Savona!" (Francesco Bernasconi).

His countless miracles, healings and fantastic tales of the most extraordinary Divine Man you have ever met.

"I decided to publish this small montage as a Testimony of Truth as I personally witnessed some of the "Miraculous Phenomena," described here, which occurred precisely in January 1997 during the interview meeting with Sathya Sai Baba and the undersigned together with a Group of Devotees belonging to the Sai Center of Milan in Via Savona!" episodes.title: Lives of Jesus ~ Mark Tully (1996)
episodes.description:
Tully explores in depth the diversity of portraits of Jesus which face us at the approach of the second Christian millennium. He travels to key sites in Israel, Rome and India, amongst others, and investigates the secret of Jesus's abiding power to provoke and lead.

00:00 1 Lives of Jesus : Jesus the God is the first of four programmes in which Mark Tully sets out on a journey to reassess the life of Jesus for the next millennium. The story starts in India, where there are many gods in many forms.

47:13 2 Lives of Jesus : Jesus the Jew is the second of four programmes in which Mark Tully sets out on a journey to reassess the life of Jesus for the next millennium. The search for Jesus continues in the Holy Land and discovers a wandering Jewish prophet who lived at a crisis point in his people's history. 

01:35:03 3 Lives of Jesus : Jesus the Rebel is the third of four programmes in which Mark Tully sets out on a journey to reassess the life of Jesus for the next millennium. Jesus the Rebel is a look at the life of Jesus as an unwilling subject of the Roman empire.

02:20:07 4 Lives of Jesus : The Hidden Jesus is the last of four programmes. Mark Tully goes to Egypt to visit the oldest Christian monastery in the world. He spends a night in the desert under the stars, discovers new gospels so dangerous that they were suppressed, and makes the journey to the top of Mount Sinai.

Mark Tully PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxB3KiB6X-Ru2XWBjx4ys7l9

Sir William Mark Tully, KBE (born 24 October 1935) is a British journalist and the former Bureau Chief of BBC, New Delhi, a position he held for 20 years. He worked with the BBC for a total of 30 years before resigning in July 1994. The recipient of several awards, Tully has authored nine books. He is a member of the Oriental Club.

Tully was born in Tollygunge in India. His father was a British businessman who was a partner in one of the leading managing agencies of the British Raj. He spent the first decade of his childhood in India, although without being allowed to socialise with Indian people; at the age of four, he was sent to a "British boarding school" in Darjeeling, before going to England for further schooling from the age of nine. There he was educated at Twyford School (Hampshire), Marlborough College and at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, where he studied Theology.

episodes.title: Les femmes mystiques avec Michel Cazenave, Colette Poggi et Thierry Gosse
episodes.description:
Show #6 tribute to Michel Cazenave.

Produced on June 25, 2013 with Jean Claude Carton

The mystics of the past were great creators, but the twentieth century gave the world exceptional figures born on a background of positivism and atheistic humanism. Thérèse of Lisieux, Elizabeth of the Trinity, Simone Weil, Edith Stein, Marthe Robin, so many women animated by the same love of God and who each expressed it in their own way.

From the 15th to the 18th century, the centre of gravity of mysticism moved from Northern Europe to the Latin countries of the Mediterranean Basin: Spain with Saint Teresa established itself as the mystical land par excellence, but Italy he also illustrates with women like Catherine of Genoa and Marie Madeleine de Pazzi, and French spirituality shines with two very different women, Marie de l'Incarnation and Madame Guyon.

Colette Poggi has been conducting research on Kashmir Shaivism and Indian philosophies since the start of her university studies in Aix-en-Provence in 1977; she then tackles two courses: Literature and Germanic Civilization on the one hand, Indian Studies and Sanskrit on the other. As part of her Doctorate, in 1986, she highlighted the correspondences between the greatest philosopher of medieval Kashmir, Abhinavagupta, and one of the most eminent mystics and theologians of the West, Master Eckhart. In order to deepen her knowledge and meet other researchers, Colette Poggi then continued research in Paris as part of a CNRS team, in Oxford, and at the Sorbonne in Comparative Philosophy with M. Hulin. In 1994, for a doctorate in Philosophy at the Sorbonne, she presented the complete translation of Îshvara Pratyabhijñâ Vimarshinî, a fundamental text by Abhinavagupta which focuses on the experience of inner Recognition as an immediate path to Deliverance. Currently, Colette Poggi teaches Sanskrit and Indian thought in various university centres, while continuing her research and translations on Kashmir Shaivism.

Thierry Gosset is an editor and translator.

episodes.title: Cesta do Indie, (Czech 1998)
episodes.description:
Igor Chaun's three-part documentary about an incomprehensible world that sometimes seems like a fairy tale and sometimes like hell. - Shocking scenes of contemporary India alternate with the experiences of defenseless tourists and with pictorially stylized passages reminiscent of India's spiritual tradition. Experiences from the trip of Igor Chaun, Petr Čtvrtníček and the CT staff to India in 1998.

The first part is called AWESOME, the second part RECONCILIATION, the third part INSIGHT. With Petr Čtvrtníček on the Ganges. - With the Indian dead on the cremation bank. - With Richard Gere in a Tibetan shrine. - With the Dalai Lama among the Tibetan refugees. - In the final meditation under the Bodhi Tree.

The premiere took place at the Summer Film School in Uherské Hradiště in July 1999. - The television premiere took place on April 8, 2000 as part of the CT program "Tonight with India." The documentary met with considerable audience response.

SARVAMANGALAM - dokument o indických svatých mužích SARVAMANGALAM - documentary about Indian holy men https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AVHV3wyQFjw&ab_channel=GoschaTV1

Directed by: Viliam Poltikovič. - What do we really need to be happy? Peace of mind, really so little.... SARVAMANGALAM in Sanskrit means "blessing to all, happiness to all". The film's guide is Swami Ram Kripalu, who lived for 35 years in the high Himalayas in an area that is completely cut off from the outside world for six months during winter and where the temperature is around -30 to -40 degrees Celsius. He lived there almost naked and with only a little food. Ram Kripalu explains that the solitude, peace and positive energy that is in this area completely balances the harsh living conditions. One can eventually adapt to them. All it takes is a little perseverance, determination and some exercise, and within 40 days one is ready to handle even the worst climatic conditions. Human possibilities are much greater than people think. A person can and can do anything, we only set limits ourselves. Thought structures and barriers bind us very tightly and breaking them is not easy. Ram Kripalu comes from a rich family, his mother was a minister in an Indian state, he himself studied at the prestigious Indian University in Varanasi, but at the age of 16 he decided to leave everything, left his family and began to look for a spiritual master to help him to find the essence of oneself, the essence of all being. Ram Kripala found his spiritual master in the high Himalayas at the source of the sacred Ganga. In recent years, Ram Kripalu has been living in Rishikesh at the foot of the Himalayas, where he moved at the request of his mother. So Ram Kripalu takes us through the fascinating places of the Himalayas dressed only in two pieces of cloth and shod in wooden sandals. During the journey, he introduces us to the life of lonely yogis in harsh Himalayan conditions.

episodes.title: Auroville seit 1968 • Leben für die Utopie in Südindien • SRF 2018
episodes.description:
Auroville – Die Utopie-Stadt in Indien wird 50: Die Bündnerin Shivaya Ruth Hauser suchte ein anderes Leben in Indien – und fand Auroville. Seit 1968 sieht sich die utopische Stadt als Versuchslabor für ein Leben aller Menschen in Harmonie. Seit 37 Jahren arbeitet sie mit an diesem Ziel und hat trotz Schwierigkeiten nie aufgegeben.

22-jährig war Ruth Hauser, als sie die Schweiz und ihr repressives Elternhaus verliess und mit dem Magic Bus der Hippies nach Indien reiste. Es war das Jahr 1979. Sie besuchte verschiedene Ashrams und fand schliesslich Auroville.

Zwei Jahre später zog sie definitiv dorthin und arbeitet seither mit Herz und Seele mit an der Utopie einer anderen, besseren Welt. Zwei Kinder hat sie dort grossgezogen. Beide haben als Erwachsene das Leben in Auroville gewählt.

Shivaya Ruth Hauser gehört seit Jahren zum inneren Zirkel von Auroville und arbeitet mit an der Entwicklung der Utopie. Reporterin Anna Gossenreiter liess sich von der Schweizerin «ihr» Auroville zeigen und zog mit ihr Bilanz. Offen schildert die Insiderin ihre Schwierigkeiten und Ängste – aber auch die unerschütterliche Hoffnung, dass ein anderes Leben möglich ist.

Ashrams of India Volume 2 - Auroville, an experimental, multinational township founded as “a living experiment in human unity” in 1968 by the Mother, Mirra Alfassa, and designed by architect Roger Anger https://www.amazon.in/Ashrams-India-Bronte-Company-Limited-ebook/dp/B08MVXX75L

The utopian city without money, without a government, without religion and which welcomes all nationalities. #Auroville was founded in southern #India in February 1968 by #MirraAlfassa, a French woman nicknamed "the Mother." After her death in 1973, the city developed, despite being located in the middle of the desert, thanks to the work of its residents. Some 3,300 people from 52 different countries live there today. Half of the population is Indian and a fifth is French. Together, they dream of building a new humanity, where people live in peace and harmony. FRANCE 24's Marion Laouamen, Lucile Perrone and Navodita Kumari report.

The Matrimandir took 37 years to be built, from the laying of the foundation stone at sunrise on 21 February 1971 - the Mother’s 93rd birthday - to completion in May 2008. It is in the form of a huge sphere surrounded by twelve petals. The Geodesic dome is covered by golden discs and reflects sunlight, which gives the structure its characteristic radiance. Inside this central dome is a meditation hall known as the inner chamber - this contains the largest optically-perfect glass globe in the world.

The utopian city without money, without a government, without religion and which welcomes all nationalities. #Auroville was founded in southern #India in February 1968 by #MirraAlfassa, a French woman nicknamed "the Mother." After her death in 1973, the city developed, despite being located in the middle of the desert, thanks to the work of its residents. Some 3,300 people from 52 different countries live there today. Half of the population is Indian and a fifth is French. Together, they dream of building a new humanity, where people live in peace and harmony. FRANCE 24's Marion Laouamen, Lucile Perrone and Navodita Kumari report.

The Matrimandir took 37 years to be built, from the laying of the foundation stone at sunrise on 21 February 1971 - the Mother’s 93rd birthday - to completion in May 2008. It is in the form of a huge sphere surrounded by twelve petals. The Geodesic dome is covered by golden discs and reflects sunlight, which gives the structure its characteristic radiance. Inside this central dome is a meditation hall known as the inner chamber - this contains the largest optically-perfect glass globe in the world.

episodes.title: Professor Kasturi talks to foreign devotees, Prasanthi Nilayam, 28th December, 1984
episodes.description:
00:00 Professor Kasturi talks to foreign devotees, Prasanthi Nilayam.
01:01:54 Professor Kasturi talks to foreign devotees, Prasanthi Nilayam, 28th December, 1984.

Narayana Kasturi (25 December 1897 – 14 August 1987) was an Indian writer, professor, and journalist.

Kasturi authored the work 'Sathyam Sivam Sundaram,' which was translated into English as 'Truth, Goodness, Beauty'. The first part of the book was published in 1960 and covers the first 34 years of the life of Sathya Sai Baba. Kasturi stated that he gathered information for the book from various sources, including Sathya Sai Baba's father and brother, as well as teachers from the schools he attended. The second part of the book was published in 1968, and the complete work was published around 1980. 

Narayana Kasturi was a writer and journalist who wrote for the magazine Koravanji in the 1940s and 1950s. He was known for discovering and promoting the work of young writers. Kasturi also wrote hagiographic accounts of Sathya Sai Baba's life and his own autobiography, entitled "Loving God: Eighty-five Years under the Watchful Eye of the Lord" was published in 1982 by Sri Sathya Sai Books and Publications.

episodes.title: Documentaire Yoga, lart de vivre
episodes.description:
Avec la réalisatrice Solveig Klaßen, nous partons en Inde aux sources du Yoga en suivant un pèlerinage dans l’Himalaya, sur les traces d’un des grand maîtres du Yoga traditionnel Swami Sivananda.
Pour ces pratiquants de yoga de nationalités différentes, ce voyage initiatique est un moyen de se ressourcer dans les lieux mêmes qui ont vu naître cette philosophie et cet art de vivre.

A Chennai nous faisons connaissance avec R.Sriram, professeur de yoga qui fut le disciple du prestigieux Sri T.K.V. Desikachar, et qui perpétue la tradition de l’enseignement particulier de maître à élève en Allemagne et en Inde.
Sa femme Anjali est une danseuse allemande de Bharatanatyam.
Ces protagonistes joyeux et sereins nous permettent de découvrir que le yoga est un compagnon de route pour la vie, un art et une techniques séculaires pour apprendre à vivre en harmonie avec nous-mêmes et notre environnement.

Un documentaire initialement diffusé sur Arte en Avril 2013 

#yoga #sivananda

episodes.title: Radha Ma
episodes.description:
@JaiRadhaMaSri  Radha Ma (Ma) (15 June 1964 - 6 March 2011) at the foot of Arunachala, 2003. Radha Ma was also known as Radha Giridhar, Radha, Radhama, Radha Ma of Arunachala, Radhaji, Rada Ma.

Radha Ma PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxCvLt5Xe9pZZ4Pygqoprkab

Radha Ma ~ The Beginners Guide To Hinduism (2006) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pc7LXUdFmLI

Usha's Restaurant https://arunachalagrace.blogspot.com/search/label/usha%20restaurant?m=0

Ashrams of India Volume 2 : Radha Ma’s House ~ Home of Radha Ma, where she lived with her few devotees and husband.

Radha Ma was born in Hyderabad and later moved to Bangalore where she married and according to some may have been working as a chartered accountant. Later she decided to renounce worldly life and then began a life of a female sadhu, sleeping in the streets and moving from Bangalore to Tiruvannamalai. In Tiruvannamalai, devotees became attracted to her and urged her to move from the streets into a house that was rented for her. She lived there together with a few sannyasins, one of whom was her husband. The house is located off the Pradakshina Road (on the side of the Arunachala Hill) near the Sparsa Resort.

Until 2009, Radha Ma used to give occasional satsang at the Sri Kannappa Temple on Pradakshina Road from late September until March. In 2010, she gave no public satsang and in 2011 she gave one last satsang.

Rumours, as well as testimonies by past devotees, implied that Radha Ma had been occasionally involved with black magic. In her residence on the night of March 5th 2011, she poured kerosene over herself and then set herself alight, in what seems to be an act of self-immolation. She was rushed to a hospital by her devotees with 90% burns and died there the day after at 3.15 pm on the 6th of March 2011. Her body was not cremated since she was a sannyasin. She was interred into a samadhi at her residence on March 7th 2011. 

Samadhi: Radha Ma died in a Chennai Hospital from burns after being rushed there from Tiruvannamalai, after what was reported in local Tamil papers, to have been an attempt at self-immolation.

episodes.title: Colours from India (2002)
episodes.description:
"Colours of India" is about the three Russian painters who came to love India as their own, which is reflected in myriad nature in their works. Russians saw India first through the paintings of Saltykov. He painted everything he saw: common people, Nawabs, processions in Kanchipuram, during his two visits in 1841 and 1845. Vasili Vereschkegin, inspired by Saltykov's paintings travelled to India. He was more fascinated by the architecture. Nikolai Roerich, unlike Saltykov and Vereshchkegin, lived in India for a longer period, and thus witnessed British imperialism in India. His paintings reflected India's desire for freedom. Through the works of these three artists, "Colours of India" depicts the bond of friendship between the two nations that was not initiated by war or diplomacy, but by the sensitive strokes of artists. Publisher by the Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi, 2002.

episodes.title: Sri Aurobindo and Margaret Woodrow Wilson
episodes.description:
At the Jaipur Literature Festival New York, September 14, 2022, Journalist and writer Akash Kapur talks about his book Better to Have Gone: Love, Death, and the Quest for Utopia in Auroville, a haunting personal quest and an erudite study in the history of utopias https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AzYKoC_Z6WY&ab_channel=AsiaSociety

00:00 Better to Have Gone
01:07 Akash Kapur
04:55 US President's daughter Margaret arrives on the ashram in 1938
05:38 The Hippie Trail
06:26 Margaret Wilson
08:40 Margaret Wilson was buried in the Protestant section of the local Christian cemetery at Uppalam
08:43 Ashrams of India

Journalist and writer Akash Kapur’s book on the intentional community of Auroville, an international township of thousands located in South India, is at once a haunting personal quest and an erudite study in the history of utopias. “Better to Have Gone: Love, Death and the Quest for Utopia” unravels a personal tragedy, the mysterious deaths of John Walker and Diane Maes, parents to Kapur’s wife, Auralice. Kapur returns to Auroville, where both he and his wife were raised, and in confronting the ghosts of those distant deaths, reveals an astonishing history of faith, idealism, extremism, and the quest for perfectionism. In conversation with Myna Mukherjee, Kapur discusses Auroville, the opportunities and perils of utopia, and the nature of memory and personal grief and how they intersect with history.

In 1938, Margaret Woodrow Wilson travelled to the ashram of Sri Aurobindo in Pondicherry, India, where she remained for the rest of her life. As a member of the ashram she was given the new name ‘Nistha,’ meaning “dedication” in Sanskrit, for her devotion to its teachings. 

She and scholar Jospeh Campbell edited the English translation of the work on the classical Hindu mystic Sri Ramakrishna, The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna by Swami Nikhilananda, published in 1942. In spite of entreaties from the U.S. government, Wilson refused to leave India during WWII; she died and was buried in Pondicherry in 1944.

Auroville https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kU4qgF5Wil8&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

MARGARET WOODROW WILSON: American President's Daughter Lived and Died in the SRI AUROBINDO ASHRAM, Pondicherry. Margaret was an intelligent, capable, fiery woman of her times, a suffragette, and a famous concert singer. During the First World War she toured around America singing to raise funds for the Red Cross, and went to sing at the frontiers of war-torn France as a way of giving her support and making a contribution to the cause.

CONNECTION WITH SRI AUROBINDO AND THE MOTHER She was first introduced to eastern mysticism by her friend Eliot, an English army officer and follower of Sri Ramakrishna. In 1936, she discovered Sri Aurobindo’s ‘Essays on the Gita’ at the New York City Public Library and was so taken by it that the guards had to more or less throw her out at closing time. She returned eagerly the next day and continued to do so until she had read through the book. To her great joy, she realised that at long last she had found her path and her guru. She took up correspondence with the Mother and Sri Aurobindo and was anxious to be near them in order to receive their help and guidance for her inner progress. They advised her to “remain in America due to (her) ill health but to establish an inner contact”. Sri Aurobindo also wrote to her that “The silent answer and help can always go to you immediately - for there distance doesn’t count.”

episodes.description:
Sri Sri Ravi Shankar ~ Guru Purnima, 1990 is from https://www.youtube.com/@GurudevOldVideos

Ashrams of India Volume 1 : Art of Living Ashram, the principal ashram of Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, near Udipalya Village, Bangalore

Sri Sri Ravi Shankar (13 May 1956 - present) was born in Papanasam, Tamil Nadu. His parents named him Ravi because he was born on a Sunday, and Shankar as it fell on the same date as the 8th century Hindu saint, Adi Shankara. It is reputed that from the age of four he could recite verses from the Bhagavad Gita and was often found in deep meditation. His first teacher was Sudhakar Chaturvedi, an Indian Vedic Scholar and a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi.

After graduating with a BSc from the St. Joseph’s College of Bangalore University he travelled with his second teacher, Maharishi Mahesh Yogi (1918-2008), giving talks and arranging conferences on Vedic science, and setting up Transcendental Meditation and Ayurveda centres.

Shankar founded the Art of Living Foundation in 1982 to teach the breathing technique “Sudarshan Kriya,” a rhythmic breathing exercise. In the early 1990s, he added the honorific Sri Sri to his own name so as not to be confused with the renowned sitarist Ravi Shankar (1920-2012).

episodes.title: Richard Halliburton ~ India Speaks (1933)
episodes.description:
A 1933 Pre-Code* adventure film, combining elements of documentaries and travelogue programs, mostly taking place on the Indian sub-continent along with staged bits spliced in to aid story flow. Produced by Walter Futter from a screenplay by Norman Houston, the film was directed, narrated and starring Richard Halliburton. A sequel to the popular film Africa Speaks!

*Pre-Code Hollywood (1927–1934) was an era in the American film industry that occurred between the widespread adoption of sound in film in 1929 and the enforcement of the Motion Picture Production Code censorship guidelines (popularly known as the Hays Code) in 1934. Although the Hays Code was adopted in 1930, oversight was poor, and it did not become rigorously enforced until July 1, 1934, with the establishment of the Production Code Administration. Before that date, film content was restricted more by local laws, negotiations between the Studio Relations Committee (SRC) and the major studios, and popular opinion than by strict adherence to the Hays Code, which was often ignored by Hollywood filmmakers.

India Speaks (1933) is from https://www.travelfilmarchive.com/results.php?clip=n&num=10&keywords=Asia+India&startrow=0 A filmed recollection of Richard Halliburton's travels on the Indian sub-continent in the early 1930s. 

Richard Halliburton (January 9, 1900 - lost at sea, presumed dead after March 24, 1939) was an American travel writer and adventurer who swam the length of the Panama Canal and paid the lowest toll in its history - 36 cents in 1928. He disappeared at sea while attempting to sail the Chinese junk Sea Dragon across the Pacific Ocean from Hong Kong to the Golden Gate International Exposition in San Francisco, California.

episodes.title: Sufi Master Fida Hassnain
episodes.description:
Ashrams of India Volume 1 : Fida Hassnain (1924 - 2016) was a Kashmiri writer and Sufi mystic. He graduated from the University of Punjab and the Aligarh Muslim University, and became a barrister. After a short period of social work, he became a lecturer in 1947 at the Sri Patrap College in Srinagar. In 1954, he became Director of the Kashmir State Archives, retiring in 1983. After meeting with Buddhist Shamans of Ladakh in 1960 he went on to write several books about the lost years of Jesus and Kashmir and supported the teaching of the founder of Ahmadiyya Islam Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (1899) that Jesus of Nazareth died in India.

episodes.title: Rudi meets Bhagavan Nityananda in 1960
episodes.description:
Rudi, (Swami Rudrananda) tells the story of how he met Swami Bhagavan Nityananda in India in 1960, and how it completely changed his life and spiritual work. At the age of 30, Rudi was at a turning point in his life when a friend took him to meet Bhagavan Nityananda at his ashram in Ganeshpuri. Rudi later wrote, "My first meeting, in India in 1958, with the great Indian saint Bhagavan Nityananda was of such depth that it changed the course of my life." Rudi continued to study with Nityananda, whom he considered his ultimate guru, until his master died in 1961.

episodes.title: Roza Bal
episodes.description:
Ashrams of India Volume 1 : Roza Bal / Tomb of Yuz Asaf / Tomb of Jesus, the tomb of Jesus in Srinagar.

Inside the Roza Bal Tomb in Srinagar (lingua italiana) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=blu0SWAK5VQ&list=PLfvx-cbEOmxCBRf8Qc2cDyt0d8PLpVZDV&index=68&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

00:00 Sergio Fernandez Gomez's film of the way to Roza Bal www.youtube.com/@sergiosfg71
06:43 The story of Roza Bal is an excerpt from Jesus Lived in India https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpF7yLbaBZE&list=PLfvx-cbEOmxCBRf8Qc2cDyt0d8PLpVZDV&index=17&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia
18:43 Ashrams of India

In the Gospel of Thomas (the Nag Hammadi Scriptures) Jesus said “If you bring forth what is within you, what you bring forth will save you. If you do not bring forth what is within you, what you do not bring forth will destroy you.”

It is believed that in approximately 89 AD, Jesus instructed one of his disciples Anjuna (Sanskrit for John/Johannes) to construct the tomb. The tomb is first mentioned in documents from 112 AD stating that a protective building had been built over the crypt. Now tended by an Israeli looking family in an unbroken line throughout the centuries, the shrine is preserved in the memory of the ancient Israelites to this day. They call the shrine ‘The tomb of Hazrat Issa Sahib,’ ‘The Tomb of Lord Jesus.’

Roza Bal is also known as the mausoleum of the prophet Yuz Asaf (Yus Asaf is the Islamic name for Jesus) and the Islamic Saint Syed Nasr-ud-Din. According to website for the minority Islamic sect founded in 1889, the Ahmadis, Yuz Asaf was a preacher of the Sabi religion, that dates earlier than Moses and Jesus. There is a sign in front that says it is the tomb of Ziarati Hazrati Youza Asouph and Syed Nasir-u-Din. There are many ancient literary works in Kashmir testifying to the fact that Yuz Asaf and Jesus are the same person. One old manuscript describes the shrine as the grave of Issa Rooh-Allah - “Jesus the Spirit of God.”

episodes.title: Sathya Sai Baba lighting the Hanukkah Menorah at Brindavan
episodes.description:
Sathya Sai Baba lighting the Menorah on the first day of Hanukkah in the Brindavan ashram in Whitefield, just outside of Bangalore, India, December, 1980

© Jack Lenchiner, 2019

The Hanukkah (Chanukah) Menorah is a nine-branched candelabrum lit during the eight-day holy Jewish festival of Hanukkah. On each night of Hanukkah, a new branch is lit. The ninth holder is for a candle used to light all other candles.

The menorah in this video belonged to Rubin Moses & Sons, a renowned shoe store on Commercial Street in Bangalore.

Swami Abhedananda (2 October 1866 - 8 September 1939), born Kaliprasad Chandra, was a direct disciple of the 19th century mystic Ramakrishna Paramahansa and the founder of Ramakrishna Vedanta Math. Swami Vivekananda sent him to the West to head the Vedanta Society of New York in 1897, and spread the message of Vedanta, a theme on which he authored several books through his life, and subsequently founded the Ramakrishna Vedanta Math, in Calcutta and Darjeeling.

episodes.title: Jesus in India
episodes.description:
This 2008 (filmed in 2005) documentary follows the story of a former Fundamentalist from Texas who is ousted from his church for asking unwelcome questions about the "missing years" of Jesus - the years from 12 to 30 unaccounted for in the Bible. The Texan, author Edward T. Martin, undertakes a seeker's question across 4,000 miles of India in search of evidence and answers about where Jesus was during those "Lost Years." An impressive array of Religious scholars and authorities weighs in, developing the cases for and against the theory of Jesus having traveled extensively in India.

episodes.title: Al Druker (1986)
episodes.description:
Al Druker narrates a story about his youth in pre-war Germany.

David: In the talk that you gave yesterday, you related the story about meeting the SS colonel in the railway carriage, as you tried to escape from persecution in Nazi Germany. This impressive figure, dressed in the black uniform, must have absolutely taken your breath away, and yet he talked to you about the Bible and made that amazing statement, "There is no Moses to save you this time."

Al: I was just a kid of nine and, of course, I was terrified. I was frightened out of my wits when he came into that train compartment. I lived in Cologne and I was travelling across Germany to Poland and had stopped off in Berlin. In Berlin I had some well-to-do relations and they had decided to put me into this first class compartment, but unknown to me, Jews were not permitted to be there. I had the compartment to myself until the train stopped some twenty-five miles outside of Berlin and that was when this SS colonel appeared. So I sat there, petrified, expecting to be arrested, but he was charming He loosened his jacket and took off all of his imposing paraphernalia - the cap with the skull emblem on it, the black leather belt, the gun, the dagger, the leather gloves, the monocle and the big black leather boots.  He made himself comfortable and told me to sit comfortably and not to be afraid of him. So, in a sense, he became an ordinary guy for me. He talked to me about God and the Jews, quoting extensively from the Old Testament. He warned me that the Holocaust was coming and advised me to escape westwards not eastwards which, of course, is what I eventually did.

David: You said that you felt that the SS colonel was Sai Baba, that he manifested as that colonel to warn you, in fact, to save your life. Are you really sure of that?

Al: It is very clear to me now that the colonel was Swami. He simply didn't fit the SS character at all. There was no way that man would have taken the chance in Nazi Germany at that time of saying the things that he said to me, even if he felt that way.

David: The SS colonel came out with this amazing statement "There is no Moses to save you this time. You will have to be your own Messiah." What do you think that Swami meant when he said that? How do you view that message in the light of what eventually happened to the Jews? What would be the purpose of the Jews being subject to the Holocaust? Was it to prove to them that there is no Messiah?

Al: I wish I even had the beginning of some answers for that. I have no idea, David. But two world wars in two successive generations, which destroyed or uprooted hundreds of millions of people, and then the development of atomic and hydrogen weapons that promised to snuff out all of civilisation, and God knows what other insane weapons of death are in the offing to destroy Mankind, only proves what madness has come upon us in this Kali Yuga, and how absolutely vital it was in this time of darkness for the Avatar to come and rescue Mankind from itself. The genocide of the Jews is just an outward symptom of the genocidal feelings of hatred and mayhem inside all of us. Swami has come to correct that. As for the Messiah, I once had the chance to ask Swami whether he was the Messiah for which we had long been waiting. He answered "Not one Messiah. You are all Messiahs. You have the power to save yourself and to save others also." In other words, he will drive the chariot, he will direct us from within, but it is our job to save ourselves and we have been given the full power of God to transform the internal enemies of greed, hatred and jealousy, etc. which are polluting our hearts into the divine love that is Swami. For me, personally, Swami gave me the chance to clear up most of my haunting memories of Nazi Germany. It relates to the first time I had to leave India very unexpectedly.  Let me tell you the story.

episodes.title: Paramahansa Yogananda's 1935/36 tour of India
episodes.description:
Paramahansa Yogananda's 1935/36 tour of India.

00:00 In 1935, Yogananda returned to India for a final visit with his great guru, arriving in Bombay in the summer of 1935.
00:25 Yogananda meets his guru Sri Yuketswar Giri for the first time in 15 years, here at his Serampore ashram ‘Priyadham.’
02:54 Yogananada and Mahatma Gandhi.
03:52 Yogananda and Ramana Maharshi. Yogananda travels with Buddha Bose, Bishnu Ghosh, Ettie Bletsch, Bijoy Mullick and C. Richard Wright.
05:38 Yogananda and Anandamayi Ma.
09:13 Sri Yukteswar Giri enters Mahasamadhi March 9, 1936. While  in Calcutta, a telegram calls Yogananda to Puri where Sri Yukteswar had entered Mahasamadhi.
10:52 Yogananda and Swami Keshabananda https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WTCutevq1qs&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia
11:58 Ashrams of India.

https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxA8KJwokikIC6tjTDO3lw7b

1935
In August 22, 1935, Yogananda arrives by ship in Bombay. His first stop, still in August, is in Wardha, visiting the great political saint, Mahatma Gandhi.
Then Yogananda travels to Calcutta, seeing family and friends.
In Serampore, he meets his guru Sri Yukteswar again, after 15 years.
The next visit is to his school in Ranchi.
In October and November 1935, in South India, he visits in Mysore (meeting Sir C. V. Raman, the Indian Nobel Prize physicist), Bangalore, Hyderabad, Madras, Arunachala (meeting Ramana Maharishi). He gives many lectures.
In December, Yogananda meets the great woman saint, Anandamayi Ma in Calcutta, and later again in his school at Ranchi.
In late December 1935, the day after Sri Yukteswar’s Winter Solstice Festival, Yogananda receives from his guru the highest spiritual title “Paramhansa.”

1936
In January, Yogananda visits the Kumbha Mela in Allahabad. Afterwards he travels to Agra (Taj Mahal), Brindaban (Swami Keshabananda, and ancient temples), Delhi, Meerut (once his brother Ananta’s home), Bareilly (visiting a boyhood friend), Gorakhpur (his birthplace), and Benares (Vishvanath temple, Lahiri Mahasaya’s home).
In early March, back in Calcutta, a telegram calls him to Puri: there Sri Yukteswar entered Mahasamadhi on March 9.
In June, back in Bombay, Yogananda witnesses the resurrection of Sri Yukteswar.

episodes.title: Frédéric Lionel
episodes.description:
Frédéric Lionel was born on 17 July 1908, at 5 AM in Amphion les Bains, France. His father was a successful engineer. After finishing the high school in Geneva, Lionel studied mechanical engineering at the Technischen Hochschule in Zürich, later cybernetics in the United States. During the 1930s, he worked in Paris as an engineer in his own firm.

This is an excerpt from Transformations (Episode 4/Final) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PaVKy9GXZSg&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

Early during World War Two he and his family escaped to England. He became an officer of the British Secret Service and went back to occupied Europe to help smuggle persecuted people out of the Nazi’s occupied territory. Lionel was widely decorated for his heroic work.

After the war, he rebuilds his firm, but at age 55 he sold the firm and dedicated his life to spiritual exploration. He wrote around 30 books and essays about spirituality, mysticism, the Cathars, Alchemy, Astrology and the Tarot. 

Some of the titles available in English: “Mirrors of Truth: Reflections of Living Mastery,” “The Magic Tarot: Vehicle Of Eternal Wisdom,” “The Seduction of the Occult Path,” “Challenge,” “Revolution in Consciousness.” His work was published in Franch, German and English and translated to several other languages. However, his work remains widely unknown to the general public.

As a lecturer on Alchemy, he warned for the dangers of technology that was not rooted in old wisdom.

Frédéric Lionel died on 22 December 1999 at age 91 in Paris.

#alchemy #tarot #cathars

episodes.description:
A Christian's Pilgrimage To The Master ~ Sathya Sai Baba by Lawrence Galante PhD https://www.holistic-arts.com/

Note: The booklet (A Christian's Pilgrimage to the Master) is not available to the public, as it was originally intended as an introduction to a much larger publication about Sathya Sai Baba.

00:00 Intro and interview with Michelle Hammerton. @saiforeveryone This is an excerpt from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eIGXydd5axw&t=561s&ab_channel=SaiforEveryone 
03:42 Sai Baba - Master & Avatar by Lawrence Galante. In 1976, Professor Lawrence Galante, had a dream to change his Master's Thesis in Comparative Religions from that on Saint Teresa of Avila, and instead to write his thesis on Sathya Sai Baba. Sceptical that the stories he had heard of Sai Baba's miracles might be made up by his devotees, and having suddenly and mysteriously received and unexpected $2,000. (enough for a plane trip to India). Dr Galante made a three month visit to Sai Baba's ashram to get the facts about this mysterious person first hand and for himself. This video was shot by L. Galante on a Super 8 camera. Most of the narrated dialogue, are direct quotes spoken and written by Sathya Sai Baba. @LawrenceGalante

episodes.title: Svetoslav Roerich and his father Nicholas
episodes.description:
Svetoslav Nikolaevich Roerich (1904 - 1993), Russian painter and youngest child of Nicholas and Helena Roerich. Born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, on October 23, 1994 and died in Bangalore, India, on January 30, 1993. He married Devika Rani, an Indian film star.

During the first decade of the 1900s and in the early 1910s, Nicholas Roerich (1874 - 1947), largely by the influence of his wife, Helena, developed an interest in eastern religions, as well as alternative belief systems such as Theosophy. Both Roerichs became avid readers of the Vedantist essays of Ramakrishna and Vivekananda, the poetry of Rabindranath Tagore, and the Bhagavad Gita.

The Roerichs' commitment to occult mysticism increased steadily. It was especially intense during World War I and the 1917 Russian Revolution to which the couple, like other many Russian intellectuals, accorded apocalyptic significance. The influence of Theosophy, Vedanta, Buddhism, and other mystical topics can be detected not only in many of Roerich's paintings but also in the many short stories and poems that Roerich wrote before and after the 1917 revolutions, including the Flowers of Morya cycle, which was begun in 1907 and completed in 1921.

00:00 Svetoslav Nikolaevich Roerich
02:36 Elizabeth Clare Prophet speaks about NICHOLAS ROERICH (1996)

Lumou is the spiritual name of Svetoslav Nikolaevich Roerich the younger son of Nicholas and Helena Roerich, was born on the 23rd of October, 1904 in Saint Petersburg, Russian Empire and died on the 30th of January, 1993 (aged 88) in Bangalore, and is buried there. 

From 1914 to 1916 he studied at the Karl May School. From 1920, he lived in the US. Svetoslav entered Columbia University, where he received a Bachelor’s Degree in Architecture. From 1923, he was the director of the Corona Mundi International Art Centre in New York, which was founded by Mikołaj Roerich. In 1928, Svetoslav moved from the US to India (Darjeeling), to be with his family. Studying the culture, art and philosophy of India, he created many paintings. 

Along with landscapes, he painted many portraits, including portraits of Nicholas Roerich, Jawaharlal Nehru and Devika Rani – his wife. One of the most beautiful is the portrait of his mother, Helena Roerich, a woman of exceptional spiritual and physical beauty. His paintings of Nehru and Indira Gandhi, adorn the historic Central Parliament Hall in New Delhi. He married in 1945 to an Indian movie star Devika Rani, widow of producer Himanshu Rai and known as “The First Lady of the Indian Screen.” Devika Rani founded the Bombay Talkies along with Himanshu Rai. Svetoslav headed the department of Folk Art and Pharmacopoeia at the Himalayan Institute “Urusvati.” 

In 1989, on the initiative of Svetoslav, the Soviet Roerich Foundation was established in the USSR, at the base of which was the study and dissemination of the idea of ​​Agni Yoga. In 1991, he donated the archives of his parents and eldest brother, which had been in India until then, to the Foundation. https://ashramsofindia.com/early-western-devotees-of-sathya-sai-baba-from-the-1940s-to-the-1960s/

Apparitions of the Virgin Mary in Garabandal, Spain

The Apparitions at Garabandal began on June 18, 1961, when four young girls said that they saw an angel. The angel made another appearance on June 25. The story quickly spread throughout the village. They subsequently reported seeing the Blessed Virgin. These claims continued for a number of years.

Garabandal is a tiny hamlet of about 300 people, and very primitive, in the Cantabrian Mountains of northern Spain.

On June 18th, 1961 four girls: Conchita González, Jacinta González and Mari Loli Mazón (all 12 years old at the time) and Mari Cruz González (who was 11), were playing together near the village when they heard a sound like thunder and suddenly an angel (identified as Saint Michael the Archangel) in dazzling white stood before them. The angel said nothing and the girls, terrified by what they had seen, ran to the village church. Over the next few days the angel appeared to them again, but once again said nothing.

They encountered skepticism from their parents, local parish priest and most of the villagers, who accused them of making the whole thing up. But over the next several days, many of the villagers began to join the girls and prayed the Rosary with them.

Finally, on July 1st, the angel spoke for the first time: announcing that he had come to tell them that on the following day, the Blessed Virgin Mary would appear to them as Our Lady of Mount Carmel.

The next day, July 2, Our Lady did indeed appear as Our Lady of Mount Carmel, holding the infant Jesus with two angels at her side. Interestingly, at that time, this day was the feast of the Visitation, until it was later changed to the 31st of May by Paul VI in the reform of the Calendarium Romanum on February 14, 1969.

Our Lady foretold three momentous events that would occur:

1.  A world-wide warning to be seen and felt by all (an illumination of conscience).

2.  A miraculous sign to be left at the Pines in Garabandal within 12 months of the warning.

3.  A final chastisement if mankind does not repent.

episodes.title: Josyp Terelya : The Mother of God in Hrushiv (1990)
episodes.description:
In 1914 and again in 1987, Our Lady allegedly appeared in the village of Hrushiv, Ukraine. The first alleged apparition occurred on May 12, 1914, just before World War I broke out.

Our Lady appeared to 22 people working the fields near the church of the Holy Trinity in Hrushiv, Ukraine.

This Was Her 1914 First Message:
“There will be a war. Russia will become a godless country. Ukraine, as a nation, will suffer terribly for eighty years – and will have to live through the world wars, but will be free afterwards.”

Ukraine suffered underneath the KGB terror for almost 80 years. They became independent on Aug. 24, 1991.

The second apparition occurred in 1987 to 12-year-old Maria Kyzin, also in Hrushiv.

Because the 1914 prophesy was fulfilled, Canadian priest Fr. Mark Goring explained that the Catholic Church takes the alleged 1987 apparitions seriously.

Our Lady appeared on April 27, 1987 – exactly one year after the Chernobyl disaster. Approximately 500,000 people supposedly witnessed these apparitions, including the KGB soldiers!

Here’s Some Quotes From The Alleged 1987 Apparitions:
“I have come on purpose to thank the Ukrainian people because you have suffered most for the church of Christ in the last 70 years,” Our Lady said.

“I have come to comfort you and to tell you that your suffering will soon come to an end. Ukraine will become an independent state.”

“Do not forget those who have died in the Chernobyl disaster. Chernobyl is a reminder and a sign for the whole world.”

“Forgive your enemies. Through you and the blood of martyrs will come the conversion of Russia. Repent and love one another. The times are coming which have been foretold as being those in the end times.

“See the desolation which surrounds the world…the sin, the sloth, the genocide. Pray for Russia. Oppression and wars continue to occupy the minds and hearts of many people. Russia, despite everything, continues to deny my Son. Russia rejects real life and continues to live in darkness. episodes.title: Gli Extraterrestri Torneranno (Documentario, 1970)
episodes.description:
Gli Extraterrestri Torneranno (The Extraterrestrials Will Return).

DOWNLOAD the book in PDF https://www.famigliafideus.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/GLI-EXTRATERRESTRI-TORNERANNO-Erich-von-Daeniken.pdf

2023 review by DankoCardi : Documentary based on the book of the same name in which the theory of ancient astronauts is proposed. The film starts from the religions that would have been generated by encounters with alien beings mistaken for gods, also reporting quotes from the Bible itself; then he takes us around the world (not in that sense) showing various clues, from cave paintings to gigantic constructions, to works of art that would testify to the ancestral encounter with extraterrestrial civilizations that would have helped humanity even at the age of stone or so in their evolution; I believe the cases of the Palenque astronaut or the Baghdad pile are known to everyone. At the time it was believed and the film also achieved good success, paving the way, a few years later, for another book with subsequent documentary on the Bermuda Triangle by Charles Berlitz. It's a shame that today all these theories, although fascinating and also disturbing, have been almost entirely refuted and the alleged mysteries have been demonstrated with scientific facts with the consequent downgrading of ufology to pseudoscience. However, it remains an excellent, well-made and evocative documentary film that will be an interesting vision to watch more than anything else for nostalgia. Recommended for everyone, mandatory for those who are fond of documentaries.

episodes.title: Richard Bock Films : AMRITHA ~ NECTAR OF IMMORTALITY ~ Guru Poornima Prasanti Nilayam 1970 (1984)
episodes.description:
Richard Bock joined Indra Devi in India for Baba’s forty-third birthday in November 1968, and returned with eight millimetre film and the recordings of Baba which became the LP entitled, Sathya Sai Baba Chants the Bhajans.

Richard Bock was the Founder-President of Pacific Jazz and World Pacific Records. Through a long personal and professional relationship with Pandit Ravi Shankar, the world renowned sitar maestro, Mr. Bock was instrumental in introducing classical Indian music to large audiences in the West. He has produced several films on Sathya Sai Baba.

00:00 Intro : Janet Bock appears in the 1975 documentary THE MAN OF MIRACLES. Ravi Shankar and George Harrison receive the darshan of Sathya Sai Baba in December 1976, at the Dharmakshetra Ashram in Bombay. This video is an excerpt from the film IN THE LIGHT OF PROPHECY by Richard and Janet Bock (who had earlier in 1972, introduced Ravi Shankar to Sathya Sai Baba).

Tantra, Guru, Yoga: the Gods of the New Era : Hinduism and the West.

Website: http://www.centrosangiorgio.com/
Quoting CCSG "After two centuries of "scientific" positivism and atheism, the de-Christianized West, in the grip of spiritual emptiness, turns to the East convinced that it has found an answer to the questions that torment it. This film unmasks the insidious deception that hides behind the fascination of Hinduism and its gurus. Duration 55 minutes. Produced in the United States."

It was nineteenth-century Theosophy, and its popularity, that brought Indian superstitions to America and Europe, and even the ringleaders of modernism, condemned by Saint Pius X, were theosophists, therefore occultists. In this regard, to know in detail how things went - which also allows us to understand what happened in the Church since the modernists took power starting from the Second Vatican Council - I recommend you read this pdf. of a 1907 book "Occultism and Modernism. Family letters to a friend": https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B_gXGsuyncMRdkt3cGdZdzkyaGs/view?resourcekey=0-Y65SX-lM117Jtqw0ClQrHA

Questo filmato smaschera l'insidioso inganno che si nasconde dietro il fascino esercitato dall'induismo e dai suoi guru. Durata 55 minuti. Prodotto negli Stati Uniti."

Fu la Teosofia ottocentesca, e le sue papesse, a portare le superstizioni indiane in america ed europa, e persino i caporioni del modernismo, condannato da san Pio X, furono teosofi, quindi occultisti.
