episodes.title: Astronaut Jim Irwin and the search for Noah's Ark
episodes.description:
James Benson Irwin (March 17, 1930 – August 8, 1991) was an American astronaut, aeronautical engineer, test pilot, and a United States Air Force pilot. He served as Lunar Module pilot for Apollo 15, the fourth human lunar landing. He was the 8th person to walk on the Moon. 

00:00 Colonel James B. Irwin interviewed in 1966
01:11 Photos from the Apollo 15 Mission in 1971
01:40 Colonel Jim Irwin, Apollo 15 astronaut shares his Timeless Testimony with Focus on Faith
17:33 Noah’s Ark on Mt. Ararat ~ Jim Irwin (1986)
Text of Dutch voice over 25:08 – 26:05
“Major problems every time we are recording! Isn’t it the 6th time by now that they forbid us to do filming?”
“We’re getting used to the hours of waiting. This time it’s for a reconnaissance flight over the mountains of Ararat.
The authorities are very helpful in everything, but this isn’t all that easy in an area in which there is a state of emergency, where rebellious Kurds at the Russian and Iranian borders make the situation dangerous.
Yet, together with Jim Irwin we are very eager to make this historical flight.”
For more info: www.arkinsight.nl https://www.youtube.com/@GerritAalten
36:14 Galileo Galilei and the Apollo 15 Hammer-Feather Drop
37:40 More Than Earthlings: An Astronaut's Thoughts for Christ-Centered Living
37:45 More Than an Ark on Ararat: Spiritual Lessons Learned While Searching for Noah's Ark
37:50 To Rule the Night: The Discovery Voyage of Astronaut Jim Irwin

Beyond his NASA accomplishments, Irwin was well known for his involvement with Christianity and creationism. He wrote about the importance of his NASA experience to his Christianity:

I am now more than an earthling, because I have walked on the moon. Being on the moon had a profound spiritual impact upon my life. Before I entered space with the Apollo 15 mission in July of 1971, I was…[a] silent Christian, but I feel the Lord sent me to the moon so I could return to the earth and share his Son, Jesus Christ.

In 1972, Irwin left NASA, retired from the Air Force, and founded the High Flight Foundation. High Flight focused on helping others realize that science supports creation, not evolution. For almost 20 years, he consistently proclaimed that Jesus walking on the earth was far more important than mankind walking on the moon. Irwin was firm in his stance that “[it is critically] important to recognize the Creator of this great planet and the universe in which it exists. After all, He is the one who created the laws of science that make space travel possible.”

He also frequently spoke about how his experiences in space made the presence of God far more real to him than ever before. One example is his account of the finding of the Genesis Rock:

episodes.title: Immanuel Velikovsky : Bonds of the Past (1972)
episodes.description:
Immanuel Velikovsky : Bonds of the Past , a 1972 CBC Documentary.
This is a documentary about Immanuel Velikovsky's discoveries by Henry Zemel. First televised on February 22, 1972 by the Canadian Broadcasting Company. 

Immanuel Velikovsky proposed in his 1950s book "Worlds in Collision" that many myths and traditions of ancient peoples and cultures are based on actual events: worldwide global catastrophes of a celestial origin, which had a profound effect on the lives, beliefs and writings of early mankind.

Immanuel Velikovsky 1895-1979
Immanuel Velikovsky, born in Vitebsk, Russia, 10 June 1895. He learned several languages as a child, graduating with full honours from Medvednikov Gymnasium, Moscow. He later studied at Montpelier, France, and Edinburgh, Scotland. At the outbreak of World War I, he returned to Moscow studying law and ancient history. He received his medical degree from Moscow University in 1921. In 1923, he married Elisheva Kramer, an accomplished violinist from Hamburg. That year they moved to Palestine, and he began medical practice. After studying in Vienna under Bleuler, a pupil of Freud’s, he began practising Psychoanalysis. In 1930, Velikovsky was the first to suggest that encephalograms would be found that would characterise epilepsy. In the summer of 1939, Velikovsky came to America to further his researches. He was one of the greatest original thinkers of the twentieth century, and his legacy continues to be the boldest, most provocative theory on the history of this earth, physical and cultural, a theory that has and will only increase in significance as time passes. If not correct in every detail, many of his ideas pass for the original work of others.   “During the course of his life, Velikovsky suffered the loss of his homeland, and the family left behind as he was forced to flee Bolshevik Russia, the near extermination of his race at the hands of the Nazis, the attempted suppression of his life’s work, and savage attacks upon his character and scholarship throughout the last three decades of his life”. As he once said, ” A newly discovered truth is first attacked as being false; but when it is finally accepted as true it is attacked as not being new.”

Published works:

Worlds in Collision (1950)
Ages in Chaos (1952)
Earth In Upheaval (1955)
Oedipus and Akhnaton (1960)
Peoples of the Sea (1977)
Ramses II and His Time (1978)
Mankind in Amnesia (1982)
Stargazers and Gravediggers (1983)

*** Robert Adams Satsang Video July 19th, 1992 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8hUBqiPD8CQ&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

Robert Adams (1928 – 1997) was an Advaita teacher from Manhattan. As a child, he would often be visited at night by an old man who sat on the end of his bed, it was Ramana Maharshi.

Later he discovered that he had a siddhi power in so much that he could manifest what he wanted. He often visited Christian mystic Joel S. Goldsmith who sent him on to Paramahansa Yogananda who sent him to Ramana Maharshi, saying that he should go as soon as possible.

He arrived in Ramanasramam in 1947, at the age of 18 and stayed until a few months before the Maharshi’s passing.

episodes.title: Are We Alone? (1992)
episodes.description:
Paradox Media and Why Not Productions present Are We Alone? : A film by Franco B. Bottenelli and Marcel C. Kahn. Based on the Book GENISIS REVISITED by Zecharia Stichen (1990). In this remarkable companion volume to his landmark EARTH CHRONICLES series, author Zecharia Sitchin reexamines the teachings of the ancients in the light of mankind's latest scientific discoveries -- and uncovers breathtaking, never-before-revealed facts that challenge long-held, conventional beliefs about our planet and our species.

Zecharia Sitchin (July 11, 1920 – October 9, 2010) was an author of books proposing an explanation for human origins involving ancient astronauts. Sitchin attributed the creation of the ancient Sumerian culture to the Anunnaki, which he stated was a race of extraterrestrials from a planet beyond Neptune called Nibiru. He asserted that Sumerian mythology suggests that this hypothetical planet of Nibiru is in an elongated, 3,600-year-long elliptical orbit around the sun. Sitchin's books have sold millions of copies worldwide and have been translated into more than 25 languages https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y3NRQAc8Ctc&t=1203s&ab_channel=ComicsOccultFan

episodes.title: Brahmachari Atmananda Interview
episodes.description:
Brahmachari Atmananda : Blanca Schlamm  (1904-1985), an Austrian concert pianist, first travelled to India in 1925, to attend the 50th anniversary celebrations of The Theosophical Society, at its headquarters in Adyar, Madras. She returned to India in 1935, and remained there for the rest of her life. She went to Ramana Maharshi’s ashram in 1942 and stayed for six weeks. She taught at the Rajghat School in Benares and was a devotee of Anandamayi Ma.

episodes.title: Sanchi Stupa (Great Stupa) filmed in 1930
episodes.description:
00:00 Sanchi Stupa (Great Stupa) filmed in 1930 (J. Shipley Dixon). One of the most famous stupas, the Great Stupa (Mahastupa) in Madya Pradesh, was built at the birthplace of Ashoka’s wife, Devi, daughter of a local merchant in the village of Sanchi located on an important trade route. https://www.youtube.com/@TheBharatArchives
01:11 Bodhgaya Pilgrimage by Tsem Rinpoche https://www.tsemrinpoche.com/ is an edited excerpt from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pI9f_vrGC-w&ab_channel=TsemRinpoche

Download : Buddhist India https://www.tsemrinpoche.com/download/Buddhism-General/en/T.W.%20Rhys%20Davids%20-%20Buddhist%20India.pdf

The significance of going on pilgrimage to the four holy sites as advised by Lord Buddha.

1. When we visit the Buddha’s birthplace:

We create the karma to have control of our rebirth; create causes to be born in pleasant places where we will have the right conditions and opportunities to practise Dharma.

2. When we visit the place where Buddha attained Enlightenment:

Seeds are planted in our mindstreams for us to also gain Enlightenment; we go towards the path of Enlightenment in all future lifetimes; even if we fail to attain Enlightenment within Buddha Shakyamuni’s age, we create the causes to be among the foremost disciples of Maitreya, the future Buddha, when he manifests.

3. When we visit the place where Buddha first taught Dharma:

We create the karma for…

the Dharma to really go into our mind and we are able to transform when we receive the teachings
being able to sponsor, propagate and put our energy towards the growth of Dharma
being able to speak and share Dharma to others, to transform their lives

4. When we visit the place Buddha passed away:

We create the cause to increase our life to be able to engage in spiritual practice and gain enlightenment; we will not die ordinary deaths with fear, anxiety, and we create causes to have control over our death and rebirth.

24:36 1927/28 The ghats, life on the ghats, large stone stairs on the left bank of the Ganges. Camera Operator: Roger Dumas Music: The Blue Pearl - Jesse Gallagher (original footage does not have any audio)
30:54 1927/28 The conduct of a cremation; Sandalwood is installed on the most popular incineration ghat Manikarnika Ghat (the second being Harishchandra). There, the richest families take their places in height, while the poorest will be at the edge of the river. The body is purified in the Ganges before being placed on the pyre that the eldest son (or failing that a nephew) lights with clarified butter by making seven times the turn clockwise. The next day the relatives will come to collect the ashes (and the remains when the family could not buy enough wood) and throw them into the Ganges. Only sadhus and babies, considered pure, are thrown directly into the river without being cremated. Camera Operator: Roger Dumas. episodes.title: The Tibetan Book of the Dead : A Way of Life and The Great Liberation Narrated by Leonard Cohen
episodes.description:
The Tibetan Book of the Dead : A Way of Life and The Great Liberation (1994) Narrated by Leonard Cohen 

Death is real, it comes without warning and it cannot be escaped. An ancient source of strength and guidance, The Tibetan Book of the Dead remains an essential teaching originating in the spiritual cultures of the Himalayas. Narrated by Leonard Cohen, this enlightening two-part program explores the sacred text and boldly visualises the afterlife according to its profound wisdom. 

00:00 Part 1: A Way of Life reveals the history of The Tibetan Book of the Dead and examines its traditional use in northern India, as well as its acceptance in Western hospices. Shot over a four-month period, the film contains footage of the rites and liturgies for a deceased Ladakhi elder and includes an interview with the Dalai Lama, who shares his views on the book’s meaning and importance. Documents the history of The Tibetan Book of the Dead, tracing the book’s acceptance and use in Europe and North America. 

47:52 Part 2: The Tibetan Book of the Dead : The Great Liberation
This two-part series explores ancient teachings on death and dying and boldly visualizes the afterlife according to Tibetan philosophy. Tibetan Buddhists believe that after a person dies, they enter a state of “bardo” for 49 days until a rebirth. Observes an old Buddhist lama and a 13-year-old novice monk as they guide a deceased person into the afterlife.

episodes.title: Arunachala (Red Mountain)
episodes.description:
Arunachala is a hill in Tiruvannamalai, Tamil Nadu, and one of the five main Shaiva holy places in South India. The Arunachalesvara Temple to Shiva is located at the base of the hill. The hill is also known by the names Annamalai, Arunagiri, Arunachalam, Arunai, Sonagiri, and Sonachalam. Every year in the Tamil month of Kārttikai (November–December), the Kārttikai tīpam light is lit atop the hill. It is also an important place for devotees of Ramana Maharshi, with the Sri Ramanasramam situated at its base.

episodes.title: The Wish Fulfilling Tree (Kalpavriksha) in Puttaparthi
episodes.description:
The Wish Fulfilling Tree (Kalpavriksha) in Puttaparthi. As a young boy, Sathya Sai Baba used to climb this hill by the Chitravathi River with his devotees to get to this old Tamarind Tree. He would often ask them, “What do you want?” Baba would then pick from the tree sugar candy, rosary, peppermint, or any of the fruit that they had requested. There is a cave here too that Baba would use at times, the entrance to which is next to the green concrete canopy.

episodes.title: The Answer ~ A True Story
episodes.description:
"The Answer" is an autobiographical film made on the relationship of an Indian Guru and an American disciple James Donald Walters (Swami Kriyananda). 

The first film to portray Paramahansa Yogananda, author of spiritual classic Autobiography of a Yogi, in a dramatic characterisation, essayed by the actor Victor Banerjee. 

This movie is based on the celebrated book 'New Path' written by Swami Kriyananda. 

This is a true story of an American seeker James Donald Walters who forsakes the worldly life to enter upon an amazing spiritual journey. His quest for truth led him at age 22 to meet and live with Paramahansa Yogananda, author of International best seller 'Autobiography of a Yogi,' who immediately accepts him as his disciple. 

He later came to be known as Swami Kriyananda, renowned teacher, author, music composer and founder of the worldwide Ananda Community. 

Swami Kriyananda died 21st April 2013 in Assisi, Italy. The film is set in the 1930's, 40's and 50's and has been shot across India, Europe and the US.

episodes.title: Alice Boner
episodes.description:
Swiss artist Alice Boner’s (1889-1981) fascination for dance brought her to India in the mid 1930s. She formed life-long friendships with dancer Uday Shankar, Rabindranath Tagore, musician Ali Akbar Alauddin Khan, and art historian Stella Kramrich.

Varanasi PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxCK-uHgrQqGZGXd1M709Hon

Alice Boner was a friend of Blanca Schlamm https://ashramsofindia.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=2566&action=edit (Atmamnanda) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ltSlLhh5AWY&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia 

The bibliography from ‘A Death Must Die’ by Ram (Lee) Alexander provides a comprehensive list of books by and about Atmananda’s friends and contemporaries, many of whom were Westerners who, like her, spent their lives in India immersed in its sacred culture. 

These are the pioneers and spiritual ancestors of the generations who have come after them to discover the wisdom of the East. This group includes such exceptional souls as 
Lewis Thompson 
Ethel Merston https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kn1am9FVfRc&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia 
Sujata Sen (Suzanne Curtil) 
Sunya Baba https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NPkBLkr0z8E&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia 
Swami Jnanananda
Melita Maschmann https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HZHfxiOv6II&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia 
Ella Maillart https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h4BgeY6ph0M&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia 
Swami Vijayananda https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6DEtELAsGks&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia 
Sri Krishna Prem and Lama Anagarika Govinda.

There have been a number of little known but fascinating studies of these outstanding, although in many cases all but forgotten, individuals in recent years (along with other long out of print works). 

00:00 Photos

02:21 Alice Boner in Indien – Ein Leben für die Kunst
Trailer zur Ausstellung (Alice Boner in Indien – Ein Leben für die Kunst)

03:09 Alice Boner in India - A Life for Art
Embassy of Switzerland in India. The traveling exhibition ‘Alice Boner in India  - A Life for Art,’ offers a tribute to Swiss artist and scholar Alice Boner (1889 - 1981). The exhibition presents one of the most unusual Swiss female artists of the twentieth century, who spent more than four decades of her life in the Indian city of Varanasi, where she worked as an artist, patron of the arts and an art historian. The exhibition provides a fascinating insight into the many facets of the life of a woman who was at home in two cultures and a true cultural Ambassador between Switzerland and India. 

05:48 Alice from Switzerland: A Visionary Artist Across Two Continents
An exhibition on the life and work of the Swiss sculptor and painter Alice Boner (1889-1981) who moved to India in 1935. Her insights into form in Indian sculpture, and writings on architecture and the metaphysical principles of art remain landmarks in art history. A walk through the exhibition with Dr Johannes Beltz and Andrea Kuratli at the National Museum, New Delhi.

21:26 Alice Boner - Swiss Art Historian - Hidden Heritage in Varanasi
From an elite Swiss Family, Alice Boner came to India to capture 'movement in the Indian Sculpture', said Dr Kapila Vatsyayan. She was a Swiss painter, sculptor, art historian, and Indologist who was captivated by the dancer Uday Shanker, the older brother of the Sitar player Ravi Shanker. It was Boner who introduced Shanker to the beauty of the dance of Shiva in the Ellora Caves, for instance. Her work on the Shilpshastra, or treatise on Indian Sculpture, remains an extraordinary template for dancers and visual artists to dialogue in lines and body alignments.

episodes.title: Swami Shantananda Puri speaks at the Aurobindo Ashram, Bangalore
episodes.description:
Swami Shantananda Puri speaks to about 10 young students about the Ultimate Reality. Recorded in Aurobindo Ashram, Bangalore on the 2nd of October, 2013. Dr Mohan is seen next to Shantananda in the video.

Swami Shantananda Puri speaks about the Power of Arunachala https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpA9qCA2Ujo&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

Swami Shantananda Puri was a great Mahatma, an Advaitin of the highest order. At the age of four, he had the fortune of coming into contact with Paramacharya of Kanchi. In 1950 after joining the government service he came across the ‘Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna’ which resulted in a deep attraction to the life and teachings of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. In 1957, Shantananda met his Guru Sri Purushottamanada Puri Maharaj (of Vasishta Guha, Himalayas) a disciple of Swami Brahmananda (Rakhal Maharaj), the mentally adopted son of Sri Ramakrishna. In 1959 after getting mantra diksha from Swami Purushottamananda, Shantananda had to enter worldly life by establishing a family, as ordered by his Gurudev. As predicted by his Guru, he had to wait 32 years to get Sanyasa. On 2nd February 1992 (Sivaratri day) Shantananda was ordained into Sanyas by his Guru Bhai Swami Shankarananda at Mangalashram, Uttar Kashi.

He was a Srotriya (One who had mastered all the Vedic scriptures and understood the true purport) and Brahmanishta (One who was always established in Brahman, the Ultimate Reality). He was a scholar par excellence in Vedic scriptures, Mantra Sastra and Puranas. His deep knowledge and lucid exposition of scriptures like Srimad Bhagavatham, Ashtavakra Gita and many other scriptures made him a popular guide to spiritual aspirants. From 1998 to 2014, Shantananda wrote 33 books on various spiritual topics. Several of these books (originally written in English) were translated into various Indian languages. Shantananda was proficient in Sanskrit, English, Hindi, Bengali as well as several South Indian languages. He came down to the level of a spiritual seeker in order to explain profound truths in a simple manner. Shantananda attained Maha Samadhi on October 14th 2014.

His guidance was the complete outpouring of love, without any expectation, and out of sheer compassion for the devotees to discover the Truth; and discovery of the Truth being the only aim of life to be able to come out of the imagined suffering that we go through. 

Shantananda wished well for everyone and wanted people to realise that there is unlimited happiness in store for us. Forgetting our true nature, we are continuously alternating between small joys and sorrows and undergoing sufferings and tribulations.  He constantly guided us to make the goal one-pointed and firm and be clear about what we want from life.

All books and articles written by Swami Shantananda Puri Maharaj are available for free download on the website www.swamishantanandapurimaharaj.org https://swamishantanandapurimaharaj.org/index.html#

episodes.title: Sivananda Ashram : AUDIO documentary of life in an indian ashram (1962)
episodes.description:
Sivananda Ashram :  An AUDIO documentary of life in an indian ashram, recorded in India by Leslie Shepard in 1962, and released in 1962 https://folkways.si.edu/sounds-of-yoga-vedanta-a-documentary-of-life-in-an-indian-ashram/sacred-world/album/smithsonian

Swami Sivananda and other Great Saints (EXTENDED VERSION) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rMBLo7czbwA&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

Choruses of bells, chanting voices, and repetitive hums all serve to transport the listener to an Indian Ashram filled with those practicing the ancient art of yoga. Focusing on the specific discipline of Vedanta yoga, Leslie Shepard sought to record not only the yoga practice itself, but surrounding sounds in the area. The album features the River Ganges, a town crier, and prayers sung throughout the day.

episodes.title: Journey to Awareness
episodes.description:
This documentary was made in the 1970's about Chitrabhanu's annual pilgrimage to Jain sites in India, with his western students. 

Chitrabhanu (July 26, 1922 – April 19, 2019) was a prominent figure in American Jainism. He was one of the co-founders of JAINA in 1971.

Chitrabhanuj took his American students on annual pilgrimages to Shatrunjay and Mt. Abu. They were required to adopt vegetarianism and meditation as a condition for Joining him in Yatra. 

In one of the annual yatras in 1974, students were able to meet with the Prime minister Indira Gandhi while attending “World Fellowship of Religions” in Delhi.

episodes.title: Nadi Gruha, Bangalore
episodes.description:
Astrology professor, Sri Ganjur Narayana Shastry, traced a Shuka Naadi Grantha (a volume of palm leaf manuscripts by Sage Shuka) on Sathya Sai Baba. It consists of hundreds of palm leaf manuscripts in Sanskrit, thought to have been written over 5,000 yrs ago. It describes accurately and at great length, Baba's family tree and many other facts. Shastry thinks that the Shuka Naadi is a Chaitanya Grantha (a book of soul power) written by the ancient seers to form a bridge spanning time and space. After Ganjur Narayana Shastry's passing at age 40, his son is now a Sri Shuka Nadi Interpreter at 'Nadi Gruha,' Chamarajpet, Bangalore.

episodes.title: The Wish Fulfilling Tree (Kalpavriksha) in Puttaparthi
episodes.description:
The Wish Fulfilling Tree (Kalpavriksha) in Puttaparthi. As a young boy, Sathya Sai Baba used to climb this hill by the Chitravathi River with his devotees to get to this old Tamarind Tree. He would often ask them, “What do you want?” Baba would then pick from the tree sugar candy, rosary, peppermint, or any of the fruit that they had requested. There is a cave here too that Baba would use at times, the entrance to which is next to the green concrete canopy.

The utopian city without money, without a government, without religion and which welcomes all nationalities. #Auroville was founded in southern #India in February 1968 by #MirraAlfassa, a French woman nicknamed "the Mother." After her death in 1973, the city developed, despite being located in the middle of the desert, thanks to the work of its residents. Some 3,300 people from 52 different countries live there today. Half of the population is Indian and a fifth is French. Together, they dream of building a new humanity, where people live in peace and harmony. FRANCE 24's Marion Laouamen, Lucile Perrone and Navodita Kumari report.

The Matrimandir took 37 years to build, from the laying of the foundation stone at sunrise on 21 Feb 1971 - the Mother’s 93rd birthday - to completion in May 2008. It is in the form of a huge sphere surrounded by twelve petals. The Geodesic dome is covered by golden discs and reflects sunlight, which gives the structure its characteristic radiance. Inside is a meditation hall known as the inner chamber - containing the world's largest optically-perfect glass globe.

Swami Yatiswarananda was famed for his meditative life and spiritual attainment. His book, Meditation and Spiritual Life, is a compilation of his class talks to earnest spiritual aspirants in Europe, the USA and India, and is considered one of the finest compendiums on spiritual life. It is perhaps the best manual of spiritual life with special emphasis on meditation. The book includes practical hints and secrets of meditation and covers all aspects of spiritual life, including a chapter on the reactions to spiritual practice. An uncompromising approach. Readers should keep in mind that this book, as with all spiritual books, contains teachings given to certain people at a certain time in a certain place.

Ashrams of India Volume 1 Chapter 15, Odisha. Karar Ashram ~ Ashram and samadhi of Sri Yukteswar Giri

Karar Ashram is the coastal hermitage founded by Sri Yukteswar Giri (guru of Yogananda Paramahansa) in 1903 to teach Kriya Yoga as taught by Babaji and Sri Lahiri Mahasaya. The ashram is now looked after by Swami Yogeswarananda Giri who is the Sadhu Sabhapati (President) of the ashram.

Priyanath Karar was known as the famous Karar Swami of Serampore and the foremost monastic disciple of Shyamacharan Lahiri Mahasaya, the father of Kriya Yoga. Karar Swami first came to Puri in the late 19th century with the intention of meeting the famous Oriya astronomer, Samanta Chandrasekhar. Destiny ruled otherwise as by the time Karar Swami returned to Puri again in 1903 to try to meet him he had already died.

As Karar Swami was aware of the potent spiritual vibrations emanating from Puri, he decided to build an ashram and with the help of a few locals, he built a hut over a sandy plot of land and thus was born the Karar Ashram. He chose the day of the Vernal Equinox, March the 22nd 1903, as the foundation day of the ashram. In 1906, he obtained a permanent lease of the land from the Puri Municipality. 

As Karar Swami later entered the monastic order, he was christened Swami Sri Yukteswar Giri. 

Every year the ashram celebrates the foundation day and there are monthly special prayers and meditation guided by the Acharya on the last Sunday of each month. There is a weekly satsang (discourse on the Bhagavad Gita) held on Sundays and a daily meditation guided by the Acharya. Currently, the ashram offers the courses in vedic, stellar, traditional and modern astrology on the 2nd and 4th Sundays of each month and Yogic interpretation of the Bhagavad Gita and Vedanta on Sundays. There is of course, training and practical instruction with respect to  God realisation through Kriya Yoga at the ashram.

episodes.title: LOSING GEMMA
episodes.description:
Losing Gemma is a two-part British television thriller (both parts are in this one film), based on the debut novel by Writer Katy Gardner. The screen adaptation was written by Robert Murphy, directed by Maurice Phillips and starred Jonas Armstrong, Alice Eve, Jason Flemyng and Rachel Leskovac. 

It originally aired on ITV on 18 and 19 December 2006.  

The plot centres on the disappearance of the eponymous Gemma (Leskovac) after she goes backpacking with friend Esther (Eve) in India. 

When Esther returns from the trip alone, she is haunted by the belief that Gemma's disappearance is her fault, but mystery surrounds what really happened. 

Notably, the drama has never been released on DVD. The reviews weren’t very kind in general and it barely scores a 5.2/10 on IMDB. "To be honest it isn’t worthy of a much better rating simply due to the fact that the character of ‘Gemma’ will give you a migraine after 5 minutes of watching."

episodes.title: The Launching of a Global Yoga Revolution
episodes.description:
In 1966, Swami Satchidananda arrived in NYC as a guest of artist Peter Max (after being invited to Europe by filmmaker Conrad Rooks). Swami Satchidananda was quickly surrounded by eager students who wanted to learn from this Yoga master from India. The Integral Yoga Institute (IYI) was first founded in New York at 500 West End Avenue in 1966. 

In October 1970, the IYI moved into its expanded home at 227 W. 13th Street, where it remains. The IYI served to launch a global Yoga revolution and gave birth to over 30 centers globally and over 20,000 Yoga teachers who share the Integral Yoga teachings and practices throughout the world. This short documentary was produced as a tribute to New York City and the Integral Yoga Institute, as the birthplace of Integral Yoga in America—and a birthplace that launched a global Yoga revolution that continues today.

episodes.title: Man Alive ~ The Hippy Trail (1970)
episodes.description:
This 1970 BBC Documentary from the Man Alive (S5 E6) series begins in London's Kings Road, New York's Greenwich Village, Toronto's Market Street and in Amsterdam's Dam Square. It goes all the way through Istanbul, Tehran, and Kabul to the East. For some it ends in contemplation on the Ganges or meditation in Khatmandu. But for others it may lead to drug addiction-in Delhi, among the drifting hippy communes of Asia. For too many it ends in repatriation, disease, even death. The hippy trail is more than a journey, it's an idea; people sometimes looking for new values, more often simply opting out, hoping for short cuts to a Nirvana that does not exist.

Jeremy James and a Man Alive film unit followed the hippy trail to India and Nepal. But their journey brought them to London where the trail has finally and perhaps tragically ended for an 18-year-old girl they met in Delhi.

First screened on Wednesday 11th November 1970, 20:10 on BBC Two England.

Reporters Jim Douglas Henry, Jeremy James, Jeanne La Chard, Gillian Strickland, Desmond Wilcox, Harold Williamson.

episodes.title: Lingua Italiana ~ Don Mario Mazzoleni interview, Puttaparthi
episodes.description:
Interview with Don Mario Mazzoleni, Puttaparthi

A Catholic Priest Meets Sai Baba https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vERgnkzlXsk&ab_channel=AshramsofIndia

GIANCARLO ROSATI: DON MARIO MAZZOLENI PARLA DI SAI BABA https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bllsTBkrMbk&ab_channel=SriSathyaSaiGlobalCouncilItalia-Zone6

SATHYA SAI BABA SU ANTENNA TRE con G.ROSATI E DON MAZZOLENI (1° parte) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ss6FUdXXKEM&ab_channel=SriSathyaSaiGlobalCouncilItalia-Zone6

A CATHOLIC PRIEST MEETS SAI BABA (1991) In the course of his spiritual inquiry, a Catholic priest meets an enlightening and extraordinary being: Sathya Sai Baba, a spiritual Master who lives in Puttaparthi, India. Like Jesus, Sai Baba performs miracles, materialises objects, heals the sick, and knows the past, present and future of everything that exists. Above all a transcendent peace and harmony flow from Him.

Who is Sai Baba? A saint, a magician, a demon, God in person? Don Mario Mazzoleni discovers how Sai Baba's teachings mirror those of Jesus Christ. Telling the story of his encounter with Sai Baba, and describing life in the ashram, he narrates the progress of his own spiritual search. His path begins with the need to detach himself from dogma and prejudice, and leads to the discovery of the fundamental unity of all religious creeds, a unity which transcends all cultural differences.

Don Mario Mazzoleni is 48 years old. He has a degree in Moral Theology from the Higher Institute of Theological Sciences of the Alphonsian Academy in Rome. In the 1970s he was associated with the Vatican Radio and the newspaper L'Avvenire. He was particularly concerned with the relationship of the mass media to spiritual instruction. He has been studying the miracle that is Sai Baba for twelve years, and has made eight trips to His ashram.

Mario Mazzoleni l' intervista

L'autore, un giornalista del Vaticano che si reca in India per conoscere Sai Baba redige una sorta di reportage espresso in forma autobiografica. Durante i suoi viaggi, egli cerca di intervistare Sai Baba, prima con di- staccato scetticismo, poi, man mano, con sempre maggiore partecipa-
zione.

Sono nove le interviste che il "reporter vaticanense”, ancora sacerdote, ha con Sai Baba, al quale sottopone le domande più svariate e scottanti: meriti e demeriti della religione, la morte, il dolore, la reincarnazione, i miracoli e i giochi "divini" di Sai Baba, l'influsso del pensiero, la medianicità, l'autoguarigione, la sessualità, il matrimonio, ecc.

In un capitolo strettamente autobiografico e storico sono riportati i dia- loghi dell'autore con i superiori, vescovi e cardinali, la sua sincera risposta alle minacce di scomunica e i decreti testuali del provvedimento mai pubblicati prima d'ora: una vera anteprima.

Mario Mazzoleni, 54 anni, fu ordinato sacerdote nel Giugno 1969, e perfezionò gli studi teologici a Roma negli anni 1972-75, conseguendo la Licenza in Scienze Teologiche e il Dottorato in Sacra Teologia Morale. Dal 1976 al 1979 colla- borò con il quotidiano L'Avvenire e con Radio Vaticana. Studioso e cultore di filosofia, ha compiuto alcuni studi personali e viaggi in terra indiana, visitando vari ashram e, fra tutti i Saggi incontrati sia personalmente che mediante lo studio del loro insegnamento (Babaji Haidakhan, Krishnamurti, Yogananda, Kriyananda, Maharishi Mahesh Yogi, ecc.), trova in Sai Baba una grandezza spirituale mai riscontrata in altri. È autore di alcuni libri, il più noto dei quali - "Un sacerdote incontra Sai Baba" - ha avuto una larga diffusione ed è stato finora tradotto in dieci lingue.

episodes.title: Nær Himlen, Nær Jorden ~ Near Heaven, Near Earth (1968)
episodes.description:
This Danish film is about hippie life in Nepal. The interviews give an insight into the hippie philosophy. Filmed in 1967, released in 1968.

Autumn 1967, among European and American hippies in Nepal. We observe the way of life these hippies have chosen to live 'outside of society' in the light of the everyday rites and ceremonies of the Nepalese. We see that the hippie movement is not just a caprice of fashion, but a religion. "We have to be here. To meditate. To pray. This way we can turn the atomic bomb into a flower."

In the autumn of 1967, Jørgen Leth and Ole John left for Nepal to film a group of hippies, who had set up a tent camp on a piece of land and proclaimed it a free state. The story of hippy culture told here leaves you with a sinking impression of apathy -- and boredom. The hippies plod around like marionettes in a fantastic setting of Buddhist temples and local populace. Their dreams and expectations seem to have lost all direction and aim. They smoke a huge chillum with their guru, holy man, and they sit together smoking in a circle at the campground. One fellow engagedly demonstrates how he eats LSD, then staggers on his hippie paradise. Leth does not conceal how, he and John were impacted by their surroundings how their initial curiosity quickly burned out. Not even the shots of daily life in Kathmandu or the experimental camera and editing work can shake off that felling. As the rights to the soundtrack (by The Beatles) could not be obtained, it has been omitted in this edition.

From: IMDB
Near Heaven, Near Earth is a film about hippie life in Nepal shot completely at the same level as its participants. A couple of interviews provide insight into the hippie philosophy and we follow a visit to a temple in which the hippies seem like peaceful beings from another planet. The visuals, in black and white and colour, are kaleidoscopic, and reveal a dramatic interest in the camera as a physical object: there is a constant toying with zoom, the camera swings back and forth, and in a series of zany shots from a rickshaw the film provides some very tangible sensory impressions from Kathmandu. Two sequences stand out in terms of form: flickering fast motion communicates what is clearly a filmic acid trip and towards the end of the film six or seven different visual materials are blended into a repetitive, metrical montage.

episodes.title: The Hippie Trail ~ Interview with Sharif Gemie
episodes.description:
This is the first history of the Hippie Trail. It records the joys and pains of budget travel to Kathmandu, India, Afghanistan and other 'points east' in the 1960s and 1970s. Written in a clear, simple style, it provides detailed analysis of the motivations and the experiences of hundreds of thousands of hippies who travelled eastwards. The book is structured around four key debates: were the travellers simply motivated by a search for drugs? Did they encounter love or sexual freedom on the road? Were they basically just tourists? Did they resemble pilgrims? It also considers how the travellers have been represented in films, novels and autobiographical accounts.

Order the book here: https://manchesteruniversitypress.co.uk/9781526114624/

Shri Udiya Baba Ji Maharaj (1875 – 1948) was a Paramahansa, a supreme sage, firmly established in the Non-Dual state of Self-Abidance. He was a Parivrajaka, and would not stay in any one place for too long. He would walk all along the banks of Ganges, moving from one place to another. Sometime during 1937-38 he came to Vrindavan. The Shri Krishna Ashram was constructed by his devotees as a place for his permanent stay. Maharaj would never say "You are Brahman," nor would he ever say, "I am Brahman." If some body asked him "who are you?,” he would reply, "the same as what you see." Sometimes he would say, "I am the servant of the whole world consisting of living and non-living." Yet some other times, "millions and millions of Brahmas, Vishnus, and Maheshas flash (sparkle) and disappear like a spark, in my each hair follicle."

Udiya Baba was also the guru of Shri Akhandanandji Saraswati Swami Maharaj of Vrindavan.

श्रीमत् परमहंस परिव्राजकाचार्य श्री उड़िया बाबा जी महाराज अपने समय के एक सर्वमान्य संत थे। उनके अनुभव, ब्रह्मनिष्ठा और त्याग-वैराग्य के कारण साधु-समाज में उनका बहुत ऊँचा स्थान था। उनके कथन में एक नविन ओज और प्रभाव होता था। वे सदा लक्ष पर दृष्टि रखकर बोलते थे और थोड़े शब्दों में ही बहुत ऊँची बात कह जाते थे। वे यद्यपि कोई वक्ता, व्याख्याकार या लेखक नहीं थे। तथापि उनमें कुछ ऐसा आकर्षण था कि लोग उनके दर्शन और वाक्य-श्रवण को सर्वदा लालायित रहते थे।

श्रीमहाराजजी 'तुम ब्रह्म हो' ऐसा प्रायः नहीं बोला करते थे। 'मैं ब्रह्म हूँ' ऐसा भी नहीं बोलते थे। उनसे जब कोई पूछता कि आप कौन हैं तो कहते 'जो तुम देख रहे हो'। कभी कहते 'मैं चराचर का सेवक हूँ'। कभी कहते 'मेरे एक-एक रोमकूपमें कोटि-कोटि ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, महेश चिंनगारियोंकी तरह चमकते और बुझते रहते हैं।
श्रीमत् प.प श्री उड़िया बाबा जी महाराज पूज्य श्री स्वामी अखण्डानन्द सरस्वतीजी महाराज के सदगुरु थे।

Ashrams of India Volume 2 - Auroville, an experimental, multinational township founded as “a living experiment in human unity” in 1968 by the Mother, Mirra Alfassa, and designed by architect Roger Anger https://www.amazon.in/Ashrams-India-Bronte-Company-Limited-ebook/dp/B08MVXX75L

The utopian city without money, without a government, without religion and which welcomes all nationalities. #Auroville was founded in southern #India in February 1968 by #MirraAlfassa, a French woman nicknamed "the Mother." After her death in 1973, the city developed, despite being located in the middle of the desert, thanks to the work of its residents. Some 3,300 people from 52 different countries live there today. Half of the population is Indian and a fifth is French. Together, they dream of building a new humanity, where people live in peace and harmony. FRANCE 24's Marion Laouamen, Lucile Perrone and Navodita Kumari report.

The Matrimandir took 37 years to be built, from the laying of the foundation stone at sunrise on 21 February 1971 - the Mother’s 93rd birthday - to completion in May 2008. It is in the form of a huge sphere surrounded by twelve petals. The Geodesic dome is covered by golden discs and reflects sunlight, which gives the structure its characteristic radiance. Inside this central dome is a meditation hall known as the inner chamber - this contains the largest optically-perfect glass globe in the world.

episodes.title: Seven Years In Tibet (1956) Hans Nieter
episodes.description:
Seven Years in Tibet is a 1956 British documentary film directed by Hans Nieter. It is based on the book of the same name. It was entered into the 1956 Cannes Film Festival.

Heinrich Harrer films Lhasa https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OpbiHXfRmdQ

Heinrich Harrer describes the last days in Lhasa https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gl0v4B5zoN4

Heinrich Harrer Limited Edition Portfolio ~ Seven Years in Tibet, 1944 - 1951 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xKM4vVf-UPA

Tibet : The Bamboo Curtain Falls (1982) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OgTwKmhlr8A

Brad Pitt Interview ~ Seven Years in Tibet (1997) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zNmiQs57EW4

Buddhism PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxBF0LuI7e50STgecNxZEBIK

Tibet PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxDs8FtNtVrKVOrWfcTLyXh7

Dalai Lama PLAYLIST https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLfvx-cbEOmxBVUTOyHsYyGhxgg6mWWtHY

In 1939, Heinrich Harrer was captured and imprisoned in a PoW camp in British India having been recruited by the Nazis for his mountaineering expertise. The 1956 film documents Harrer's escape from the camp and his consequent journey through the jungles of India and over the Himalayas, eventually leading him to Tibet and the Holy City of Lhasa.

The tenacity and sheer bravery of Harrer's journey cannot be overstated as, with only inadequate clothing and provisions along with his own maps and compass, he was in mortal peril throughout his crossing of the Himalayas. The passage over the frozen peaks proved to be both perilous and unforgiving and only Harrer's abilities as a climber and his fervent desire to escape his captors kept him alive.

Having fled the camp disguised as army officers and Indian coolies Harrer and his fellow escapees decided that their best collective chance of survival lay in separating and going ahead alone.

The dramatic re-enactments of Harrer's escape from the camp and journey through the jungle are understandably poor by modern standards but that does not distract from the overall quality of the film.

The inconceivable trek that first leads Harrer through the dense jungle then takes him to the freezing peaks of the Himalayas where he comes face to face with the Tibetan demons that guard the mountain pass. The landscape of Tibet is initially revealed as a collection of unwelcoming plains where Harrer successfully traded for yak cheese and meat that proved to be life-saving sustenance on his journey.

As foreigners were forbidden to enter Tibet, Harrer surprisingly finds his way into the Holy City with relative ease and receives little resistance from its people who he describes as both kind and welcoming. The majority of the documentary focuses on the customs, rituals and daily activities of those living within the city along with the life of the Dalai Lama, the living God.

Having been given a camera by the Dalai Lama to record images of his people, Harrer was able to obtain previously unseen footage of life within Tibet. Armed with only 16mm film he successfully documented his stay in Lhasa and the surprisingly quaint and idyllic lives of the cities inhabitants. The film is made all the more poignant by the fact that the idyllic and instinctively peaceful lives of Tibet's people are shattered by the invading Chinese army forcing the Dalai Lama to flee into exile.

The footage of his stay among the Tibetan nobility reflects the undeniable warmth and generosity of a people whose lives adopt an air of inherent tranquillity. The combination of footage showing the Tibetan people at work and play, coupled with the stunning images of the surrounding landscape, give the documentary an inimitability that remains timeless.

As both mountaineer and explorer, Harrer lends the film a quiet sensitivity that exposes both the richness of the Tibetan people's lives and the stunning scenery that surrounds them. Although some elements of the documentary will obviously seem very dated, Harrer's account of his journey offers all of the intrigue and breathtaking cinematography as its modern counterparts.

episodes.title: The reading of Genesis from Lunar Orbit, 1968
episodes.description:
On Christmas Eve, December 24, 1968, the crew of Apollo 8 read from the Book of Genesis as they orbited the Moon. Astronauts Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders were the first humans to travel to the Moon, recited verses 1 through 10 of the Genesis creation narrative from the King James Bible. 

Lunar Module Pilot William A. Anders read verses 1–4, Command Module Pilot James A. Lovell Jr verses 5–8, and Commander Frank F. Borman II read verses 9 and 10.

05:37 The Apollo 8 Mission.
08:54 Earthrise : "Earthrise" is the first image of Earth captured by humans from space. The photo of Earth was taken aboard Apollo 8 on December 24, 1968, by lunar module pilot Bill Anders. The image highlighted Earth's fragility, since it was seen against the vast blackness of space.
14:03 Apollo 14 Lunar Module Pilot - Edgar D. Mitchell's mystical experience in space while homeward bound from the successful Lunar Mission in 1971.

episodes.title: A Taxi Ride in India
episodes.description:
00:00 The story is first narrated in the video by Jack Hislop on the 27th of May 1989, in Eureka, Missouri, USA. 
03:15 In the second part, Heidi King recalls the events. 
05:03 Heidi recalls the event in 2019.

In the taxi were the driver, Jack and Victoria Hislop, Heidi King and her parents. Dr Jack Hislop writes - One evening in 1973, we left Brindavan at about 8 pm to return to Bangalore. There were five of us in the taxi, plus the driver. The Bangalore road is only two lanes. Some miles from Brindavan, we overtook a bus. Although the driver of our taxi saw some lights ahead, he estimated that there was plenty of time to pass the bus. He could not have been more mistaken – the lights ahead were that of a car moving at a very high speed towards us.

In this particular area, the layout of the road was also deadly. The road was under repair, and there was a high bank of dirt and rocks covering the side of the road. Thus, there was no possibility of the oncoming car being the miraculous escape able to swerve off the road. We, too, could not take evasive action, for the bus was on our left and the road-repair material on the right, and by this time the oncoming car was directly in front of us. A foolish driver in that car and an equally foolish driver in our taxi! …. The lights of the oncoming car now struck directly into the windscreen of our taxi. The cars could not have been more than a second or so apart. We were stunned. Not one of us remembered Baba or called out to Him. We felt we were as good as dead, and we instinctively tensed for the crash. But at that very moment something happened that was without any rational explanation. At one moment the two cars were upon each other, about to be smashed in a fatal head-on collision. The very next moment, the oncoming car was behind us, and we were continuing to pass the bus with a clear road ahead. Looking back, we could see the red tail-lamp of the other car. There was no crash.

The next day we drove out to Brindavan as usual at 8 am so as to be waiting near the veranda for Baba to appear for morning Darshan. As soon as He came into the room, I touched the Lotus feet and said, “We want to thank Baba for saving our lives last night.”

Baba smiled and said, “Yes, that was a close one. You were so shocked that not even one of you called out for Swami! But Swami saved you anyway.” Then He turned to a group of men and in Telugu told them the entire story of the incident.

I then said, “Swami, You must have altered time and space in order to save us.” Baba just smiled and did not answer.

episodes.title: Light In The West - Jesus "lost years" and Joseph of Arimathea in Britain
episodes.description:
Whether Jesus did or did not visit the west of England during his unrecorded youth is an open question, but there is too much evidence for this story to be dismissed lightly; evidence shown in this documentary.

Cornwall is known as “The Land of the Saints” because of the great number of “Saints” associated with the county. In fact there are over sixty of these saints who have Cornish connections. Mostly they were from the branch of Christianity known as Celtic Christianity and came to Cornwall from Ireland or Wales. St Piran the patron saint of Cornwall was a 5th-century Cornish abbot and saint, probably of Irish origin. He is the patron saint of tin-miners. St Petroc was born in Wales, he primarily he is associated with a monastery at Padstow and is known as “the captain of the Cornish saints. The list of saints goes on and on with many Cornish towns and villages named after saints.

In folklore, Christianity came to Cornwall even before these saints. According to the Talmud, the primary source of Jewish teaching and theology, Joseph of Arimathea was an uncle of the Virgin mary and therefore the great-uncle of Jesus. This would explain why he was allowed, as a close relative, to bury the body of Jesus in his tomb. There are very persistent traditions in Cornwall that Joseph was involved in the trade of tin.The existence of a tin trade between Cornwall and Phoenicia is frequently referred to in Classical writers, and is described at considerable length by Diodorus Siculus.

episodes.title: Prasanthi Nilayam (1989)
episodes.description:
Trip to India, tour of Sai Baba's Ashram and its surroundings. By Anne Rodriguez Barfoot-Argentina, filmed by Renzo Zanutel and Martina de Col-Italy-edited by SAI BABA TV.

00:00 Prasanthi Nilayam, 1989
39:55 Darshan, 1989
01:29:10 Sathya Sai Baba’s place of birth in Puttaparthi, 1989
01:35:33 Puttaparthi, 1989
01:43:50 The Wish Fulfilling Tree in Puttaparthi, 1989
01:46:16 Sathya Sai Baba devotees Fred and Vallery, 1989

1989 was  a year of great movement in my life. I went on vacation to San Marcos Sierras with my boyfriend Pablo. In the middle of one night, we joined in with the Mahashivaratri singing for with a group of Sai Baba Devotees who were in the field next to the campsite. The following morning we joined a Human Values workshop, based on the story by Enrique Barrios, Ami el Niño de las Estrellas.

The year passed, after various situations and transformations in my life, in September of that 1989, the possibility of traveling to India arose. Actually, I first thought about traveling to Spain, Holland, Denmark, but I woke up one morning knowing that I had to go to India, they asked me why and I answered that I only knew that I was going, so I did all the paperwork to travel, and I left everything, my job, my house, my eldest son was living with his father in Villa Mercedes San Luis, a month later on October 1, I was on the plane traveling to India, to Sai Baba's Ashram.

Arriving alone, I met an Italian couple Renzo Zanutel and Martina De Col, we filmed ashram to share with people, friends, family, or to screen it on TV some day.

Anne Rodriguez Barfoot.

episodes.description:
Traces the life of the Buddha from his birth as a prince through time spent as a wandering mendicant in search of a solution for life’s sorrow to his later years when he trudged the dusty paths of India preaching his ego-shattering life-redeeming message. That message is threaded throughout the film as we visit monasteries and families in two different craft communities and see how Buddhism has influenced the lives of these gentle people in southeast Asia.

episodes.title: Yoga for Health (1950)
episodes.description:
Yoga for Health (1950) | Directed by A. Bhaskar Rao.

'Yoga for Health' made in 1950 by A. Bhaskar Rao is one of the early works highlighting the importance of Yoga in our life. The 11-minute documentary introduce us to the ancient science of Yoga and shows certain ASANAS which if practised, can help to build up bodily strength, stamina and mental alertness.

The film was presented by the Films Division/Documentary Films of India with the supervision of The Yoga Institute (Santa Cruz, India).

Crew:
 Cinematography -Dara Mistry,
 Sound - P. K. Vishwanath,
 Editing - Pratap Parmar,
 Music - V. Shirali,
 Commentary - Berkeley Hill.

Ashrams of India Volume 2 : The Yoga Institute, known as the oldest yoga centre in the world, founded in 1918 

Mumbai
Area: Santacruz East

Founder: Shri Yogendra (1897 - 1989). Born as Mani Haribhai Desai  in Gujarat. Through a chance meeting he found his Guru, Paramahansa Madhavadasa (1798 - 1921), a great master of Yoga from Bengal who initiated him into the path of yoga. With the blessings of his Guru, he went on to spread the then-secret knowledge of yoga among the masses, as he felt that yoga could help improve the lives of householders.

He founded The Yoga Institute at ‘The Sands,’ the residence of Dadabhai Naoroji in Versova in 1918 (moving to the present premises in Santacruz in 1947). There, he cured many people from various ailments through therapeutic yoga. He later travelled to America and founded a Yoga Institute in Harriman, New York in 1920. Much research work was done on the subtle physiological and psychological effects of yoga along with scientists and doctors.

Yogendra then returned to India and following the wishes of his father, married and remained a householder Yogi. He wrote many authoritative texts on yoga based on ancient scriptures. Some of his books are preserved in the Crypt of Civilization for posterity, to be opened in 6000 years. Along with his wife, Sitadevi Yogendra, he continued to teach and spread the awareness of authentic classical yoga at The Yoga Institute, Santacruz until his death in 1989.

episodes.title: SOUL OF THE EAST part 4 - Ashrams, places of peace and knowledge
episodes.description:
SOUL OF THE EAST part 4 - Ashrams, places of peace and knowledge / DUŠE VÝCHODU 4 - Ášramy, místa klidu a poznání / 1992 Czech documentary. The Soul of the East is a seven-part documentary series focused on various manifestations of spiritual life in today's India. Created in Studio 61 T. Formáčka KF a.s. Viliam Poltikovič - author and director of the entire project. Filming took place from the beginning of December 1991 to the end of February 1992.

People in India have the opportunity to become familiar with spiritual knowledge, the essence of yoga, in ashrams and yoga centers. In the ashram of Swami Gitananda in the south of India, we see morning meditation on the shore with the many foreigners who have come here to gain energy and spiritual instruction. 

Nearby is Auroville - the lotus city of the future, which was built and is being built by people from 40 countries of the world. The impetus for its construction was the teachings of the great thinker Aurobindo imbued with truth, love and knowledge.

The personality of Ramana Maharishi, the sage of Mount Arunachala, is well known to the spiritually minded intellectuals of the Western world. Today he is no longer alive, but foreigners from all over the world still come to his ashram. 

In the great ashram at Mont Abu we find the World Spiritual University of the Brahma Kumaris movement. They are concerned not only with the inner knowledge of our being and essence, but also with maintaining and spreading peace in the world.

The beautiful large ashram has Sathya Sai Baba, who is considered a divine incarnation and is undoubtedly the most famous spiritual figure in contemporary India. He is worshiped not only in India but also all over the world where he has 6000 centers. At least 20,000 people from all over the world come to greet him every day. The atmosphere of the ashram is remarkable, people are clearly changing for the better. In addition to teachings and miracles, Sai Baba implements an extensive social program - he builds schools, hospitals, scientific workplaces all over India - everything is accessible to everyone and free of charge.

Comprehensive teaching of yoga and spiritual teachings is in famous ashrams in Rishikesh such as Shivananda and Parmarth Niketan.

episodes.title: Auroville
episodes.description:
Auroville

00:00 Justine Shappiro visits Auroville in 1995 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HfhpQBrcu9Q
10:47 The Matrimandir and I, 2023
17:25 Ashrams of India

Ashrams of India Volume 2 - Auroville, an experimental, multinational township founded as “a living experiment in human unity” in 1968 by the Mother, Mirra Alfassa, and designed by architect Roger Anger https://www.amazon.in/Ashrams-India-Bronte-Company-Limited-ebook/dp/B08MVXX75L

The utopian city without money, without a government, without religion and which welcomes all nationalities. #Auroville was founded in southern #India in February 1968 by #MirraAlfassa, a French woman nicknamed "the Mother." After her death in 1973, the city developed, despite being located in the middle of the desert, thanks to the work of its residents. Some 3,300 people from 52 different countries live there today. Half of the population is Indian and a fifth is French. Together, they dream of building a new humanity, where people live in peace and harmony. FRANCE 24's Marion Laouamen, Lucile Perrone and Navodita Kumari report.

The Matrimandir took 37 years to be built, from the laying of the foundation stone at sunrise on 21 February 1971 - the Mother’s 93rd birthday - to completion in May 2008. It is in the form of a huge sphere surrounded by twelve petals. The Geodesic dome is covered by golden discs and reflects sunlight, which gives the structure its characteristic radiance. Inside this central dome is a meditation hall known as the inner chamber - this contains the largest optically-perfect glass globe in the world.

episodes.title: Ashram Bhole Baba Ψ - Cisternino, Italy
episodes.description:
Ashram Bhole Baba Ψ - Cisternino, Italy

00:00 Haidakhan Babaji said that Cisternino will survive world's end (2012 AP) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqkYEoo-d8A&ab_channel=APArchive Cisternino https://www.google.com/maps/place/Ashram+Bhole+Baba/@40.7176778,17.4034693,21z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x1346519756dcc09b:0xaa0bbf0c6ba7d633!8m2!3d40.7177108!4d17.4035672!16s%2Fg%2F11cjj7jnxf?entry=ttu
1. Wide of Cisternino, with "trulli," typical white buildings with conical roofs, visible
2. Mid of "trullo" roof at Ashram Bhole Baba centre 
3. Wide of Ashram Bhole Baba centre
4. Mid of painting on centre's wall
5. Wide of temple in centre's grounds
6. SOUNDBITE (Italian) Federico Esposito, spokesman, Ashram Bhole Baba centre:
"Our master never gave us such a message. Babaji certainly told us about a big change in the future, a change in human consciences, a change for better times, a change that would bring a sense of humanity on earth."
7. Mid of Babaji follower near temple
8. Close-up of wind-chime, ribbon and bells 
14. SOUNDBITE (Italian) Antonio Giacchetti, Translator, "Maya Factor":
"Every 26,000 years the solar system is aligned with the centre of the  galaxy and this will cause us to receive a new frequency emission. Some experts say that this new frequency will release endorphin inside our brains. This will change our perceptions. We will see, hear and perceive a different reality." 
13. Various of Giacchetti looking at book "Maya Factor"
14. Wide of Cisternino
15. SOUNDBITE (Italian) Donato Baccaro, Mayor of Cisternino:
"Cisternino is one of the most beautiful villages in Italy, it's a slow town, where everything goes on slowly, the quality of life is different, better. A lot of foreign people, once they have visited the town, choose to live here, this confirms that this place has an special energy."
16. Wide of guests at dinner table in Calongo Bed & Breakfast 
17. Close up coffee cups
18. SOUNDBITE (English) Aurane Mendy, tourist:
"Everyone in Cisternino was talking about the end of the world, so we decided to stay here a little bit longer to see if something happens."
15. Wide exterior of Calongo Bed & Breakfast 
STORYLINE
A small town in southern Italy is experiencing a spike in visitor numbers with clocks counting down to December 21, the end of the Mayan calendar, which some believe signals the end of the world.
There has been a long held belief that the Cisternino in Puglia, would survive the cataclysm. 
Its status as a safe haven has grown out of an apparent prediction by Babaji, Indian guru Shri Herakhan Baba who revealed that "Cisternino will become an island" once the world comes to an end. 
Followers of Babaji built a strong community in Cisternino, which rotates around an ashram built in 1979. 
But the foundation behind Babaji followers, the Bhole Baba Foundation, has denied any specific reference to the end-of-days theory in any of their guru's messages. 
Babaji had predicted that a cultural revolution would change the world, a transformation that would enlighten consciences and create new values.
"Babaji certainly told us about a big change in the future, a change in human consciences, a change for better times, a change that would bring a sense of humanity on earth," said Federico Esposito, spokesman of the Ashram Bhole Baba centre.
According to Antonio Giacchetti, translator of the book "Maya Factor", the end of the Mayan calendar could have another interpretation. 
"Every 26, 000 years the solar system is aligned with the centre of galaxy and this will cause us to receive a new frequency emission. Some experts say that this new frequency will release endorphin inside our brains. This will change our perceptions. We will see, hear and perceive a different reality," he told the Associated Press. 
Regardless, tourists continue to flock to the Cisternino.
"A lot of foreign people, once they have visited the town, choose to live here, this confirms that this place has an special energy," he said.

episodes.title: Uttarakhand Chardham Yatra, 1952
episodes.description:
This is an excerpt from the 1952 movie YATRIK https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AgKiAbmFUgQ&ab_channel=CinecurryClassics.

YATRIK depicts a group of pilgrims on an arduous trek in the high Himalayas. It is the Hindi-language version of the Bengali film Mahaprasthaner Pathey. Basanta Choudhury plays a young brahmachari, while Arundhati Mukherjee plays Rani, a strong-willed young widow who develops a soft corner for him.

A part of the film was shot in the Garhwal region in the Himalayas. The film contains images of Rishikesh, Devprayag, Srinagar, Rudraprayag, Agastyamuni, Guptkashi, Phata, Rampur, Sonprayag, Gaurikund, Lincholi, Kedarnath in Uttarakhand (then Uttar Pradesh).

Producer: NEW THEATRES Genre: Adventure Director: Kartick Chatterjee Cast: Basanta Choudhury I Molina Devi I Raj Lakshmi Country: India Year: 1952 Duration: 02:20:11 Language: Hindi.

episodes.title: Rabindranath Tagore (1961)
episodes.description:
Films Division presents 'Rabindranath Tagore,' a 1961 documentary directed by Satyajit Ray. This semi-documentary on Ray's mentor was commissioned for the centenary of Tagore’s birth. The extraordinarily diverse literary and visual output of Tagore, the Shantiniketan experiment and the Tagore family’s contributions to India’s freedom struggle are condensed into one hour, relying on a voice-over commentary that eschews historical analysis in favour of a fairly reverential approach. Ray includes some re-enactments of episodes in Tagore’s life together with images of paintings, photographs, documents, etc. The best moments are the reconstructed Balmiki Pratibha, and the song Tobu mone rekho (‘Yet remember me’) in Tagore’s own voice.

episodes.title: Veena Swami
episodes.description:
Swami Dattatreya Rama Rao Parvatikar (1916 - 1990) also known as Veena Baba was a sannyasi and musician and a skilled player of the Rudra Veena and the Dattatreya Veena or Datta Veena, which he invented by blending the Sitar, Swarmandal and Rudra Veena. From the little known about him we can gather that he was not too much involved in professional performing, rather exploring his Sadhana of spiritual practice and music as well as teaching both of them. He started a Nada Yoga School in Rishikesh in the late 1950s.

episodes.title: Bob Raymer
episodes.description:
Bob Raymer (1921 - 2008) was a former commercial airline pilot who met Paramahansa Yogananda in the latter years of Yogananda's life. Yogananda initiated Raymer into Kriya Yoga and made him a minister of SRF. Raymer conducted services in Minneapolis for many years, telephoning Yogananda before each to receive his blessing. Raymer later moved to Hawaii where he conducted his Clear Light retreats, and then to Song of the Morning retreat center in Michigan, where he was the spiritual director from 1991 to 2004.

episodes.title: Adyar, 2021
episodes.description:
This video is part of the Theosophical Society in America’s Classics Series.

This documentary explores the international Theosophical Society in Adyar, Chennai, India; and examines some of the reasons that founders H. P. Blavatsky and Col. Henry Steel Olcott might have had for moving the Society's headquarters from the United States to India. Rare film footage and archival photos highlight the program along with appearances by leading members of the Society, including international Theosophical Society president, Radha Burnier, Theosophical scholar and historian Michael Gomes, and more. episodes.title: Fairlawn Hotel, Calcutta
episodes.description:
Elgin Fairlawn, Kolkata (formerly known as Fairlawn Hotel) was built around 1783. It is located on Sudder Street in Kolkata. Initially built as a house, it was later turned into a hotel in 1936.

00:00 City of Joy (Soundtrack : Save the Day by Niamh Regan).
03:39 A 1994 visit to the Fairlawn Hotel - a glimpse of British colonial history from days gone by. Mrs. Smith, the gracious proprietor of the Fairlawn Hotel, personally guides us through the remarkable journey of this magnificent establishment. With her warm hospitality and wealth of knowledge, Mrs. Smith offers us an exclusive glimpse into the bygone era that has left an indelible mark on this historic gem.
07:15 Mrs. Violet Smith was a second generation immigrant to Calcutta from Armenia. During WW1, her parents fled to India, and finally settled in Calcutta. They started Fairlawn hotel there. But, it reached its heyday when the hotel fell in the hands of Mrs. Smith. Gradually, Fairlawn developed into an Anglo-Indian cultural hub. Many world famous celebrities like Indian film star Shashi Kapoor, poet Gunter Grass, or Geoffrey Kendal, the eminent theatre personality, fell in love with Fairlawn. This is surely for the special ‘old world charm’ of the place, and the love of Mrs. Smith. Immense was her vitality. Even in her 90s, she lived life like a teenager! In this film about her beloved hotel, the film captures her celebrations of life. At the start, it tells of the Armenian migration, but soon it becomes the search of Mrs. Smith’s parents, Mrs. Smith herself, her guests, all. Fairlawn has always remained a focal point in their search. The film is full of the anecdotes of the eminent guests at the hotel. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sHIafV2Z-IE&ab_channel=NautankiTheatreCompany
40:10 Video and Photos (Soundtrack : Shallow by Allie Sherlock).
44:05 Ashrams of India.

The colonial bungalow was built in 1783 by an Englishman William Ford, when Warren Hastings was the Governor General. The house on Sudder Street became a hotel in 1936 after passing into the hands of Mrs. Rose Smith (née Sarkies) of Armenian roots. In 2018, the hotel was bought by Elgin Hotels & Resorts.

The hotel has been a host to Eric Newby, a travel writer. Another notable guest was the French Writer Dominique Lapierre who stayed here while writing the story about Calcutta titled City of Joy published in 1985. This was made into a film in 1992 and the cast and crew of the film, including Patrick Swayze has also stayed here. Ismail Merchant and James Ivory, whose 1965 film Shakespeare Wallah was loosely based on and starred the Kendals also has been the guests at this hotel.

episodes.title: The India Trip (1971)
episodes.description:
National Film Board of Canada documentary from 1971.

This documentary is a portrait of modern-day Pondicherry, an ancient city near the southern tip of India. For several centuries an outpost of France, the city is now home to Auroville, a spiritual community growing on its periphery. There, European and North American devotees of Sri Aurobindo, a Bengali poet and mystic, come to live the contemplative life. Their guru is a 94-year-old woman from France. This mecca of sorts is seen through the eyes of Albert Jordan, a professor from Concordia University, in Montreal, who spent a year there with his family in 1971.

episodes.description:
Zina Rachevsky (1930 – 1973) was a socialite, film actress, and Gelug Tibetan Buddhist nun. Her Buddhist name is Thubten Changchub Palmo.

The Religions of Man

In 1955, a small miracle occurred in St. Louis when an affable and enthusiastic young professor from Washington University offered a landmark series of talks on the World's Religions at KETC television, and broadcast nationally on National Educational Television - NET.  Huston Smith, whom the Christian Science Monitor would later call "Religion's Rock Star," opened the minds of Americans, using public television to reveal exactly why members of the various religions found their faith traditions compelling.  Even now, more than sixty years later, Smith's descriptions of the various faiths are entirely relevant and compelling -  a refreshing tonic for a troubled world.  And now these films are once again available! Dana Sawyer, Huston Smith Biographer

In 1955, the Religions of Man was the first college accredited course given on TV. It was broadcast on KETC in St. Louis and featured Dr. Huston Smith, associate professor of philosophy at Washington University. The course surveyed the great living religions of the world and how they influenced human history, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Taoism, Judaism, Christianity (Protestant and Catholic) and Islam. Lectures trace the start of these religions, their founders and what each teaches as life’s meaning and the way to its fulfilment.

Born in China of missionary parents, Dr. Huston Smith has had first-hand acquaintance with the religions of both East and West. Dr. Smith’s graduate studies were completed at the University of California and the University of Chicago, where he received his PhD in 1945. He was president of the Missouri Philosophy Association and is the author of The Purpose of Higher Education, published in 1955 by Harper and Brothers. Dr. Smith taught at the University of Denver and the University of Colorado before joining the Washington University faculty. His course on The Religions of Man grew from 13 to 140 students in the first seven years he taught it. The 17 episodes that comprise this series were originally recorded on kinescope.

The Religions of Man

In 1955, a small miracle occurred in St. Louis when an affable and enthusiastic young professor from Washington University offered a landmark series of talks on the World's Religions at KETC television, and broadcast nationally on National Educational Television - NET.  Huston Smith, whom the Christian Science Monitor would later call "Religion's Rock Star," opened the minds of Americans, using public television to reveal exactly why members of the various religions found their faith traditions compelling.  Even now, more than sixty years later, Smith's descriptions of the various faiths are entirely relevant and compelling -  a refreshing tonic for a troubled world.  And now these films are once again available! Dana Sawyer, Huston Smith Biographer

In 1955, the Religions of Man was the first college accredited course given on TV. It was broadcast on KETC in St. Louis and featured Dr. Huston Smith, associate professor of philosophy at Washington University. The course surveyed the great living religions of the world and how they influenced human history, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Taoism, Judaism, Christianity (Protestant and Catholic) and Islam. Lectures trace the start of these religions, their founders and what each teaches as life’s meaning and the way to its fulfilment.

Born in China of missionary parents, Dr. Huston Smith has had first-hand acquaintance with the religions of both East and West. Dr. Smith’s graduate studies were completed at the University of California and the University of Chicago, where he received his PhD in 1945. He was president of the Missouri Philosophy Association and is the author of The Purpose of Higher Education, published in 1955 by Harper and Brothers. Dr. Smith taught at the University of Denver and the University of Colorado before joining the Washington University faculty. His course on The Religions of Man grew from 13 to 140 students in the first seven years he taught it. The 17 episodes that comprise this series were originally recorded on kinescope.

Himalaya : Terre de Serenite by Arnaud Desjardins (1968), consists of two remarkable early films shot in the 1960's for French television, focusing on the Tibetan yogis at the sacred lake of Padmasambhava in India, Rewelsar. The first film, Le Lac des Yogis, features rare footage of the early years of Tibetan refugees in India, with a young Dalai Lama and his sister Jetsun Pema, plus Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche performing an initiation at Rewelsar, or Tso Pema. The second film, Les Enfants de la Sagesse, features a young Dalai Lama and his Gelugpa monks, and the 16th Gyalwa Karmapa training the main young tulkus of the Kagyu lineage - now renowned teachers in their own right.

Arnaud Desjardins (1925 - 2011) was a leading figure in introducing the broader French public to the philosophies and religious practices of Asia

His films devoted to Tibetan Buddhist leaders, Indian religious teachers, Japanese Zen philosophers, and Afghan Sufis were widely shown on French television in the 1960s and early 1970s, when such topics were largely unknown among non-specialists

His films were often accompanied by books and later radio interviews and talks

Arnaud Desjardins (1925 - 2011) was a French author. He was a producer at the Office de Radiodiffusion Télévision Française from 1952 to 1974, and was one of the first high-profile practitioners of Eastern religion in France.

He worked on television documentaries about spiritual traditions not well known to many Europeans at the time, including Hinduism, Tibetan Buddhism, Zen, and Sufism from Afghanistan.

He was the son of Jacques Guérin-Desjardins. He was part of the George Gurdjieff group, his first contact with mysticism. Educated in a Protestant Christian environment, he was exposed to spiritual aspects of Christianity on a visit to a trappist Catholic monastery. He then became interested in yoga, and when asked to direct a film for French television, he chose to make a series of films on India, for which he gained attention for his first film, Ashrams.

In 1959 he traveled to India, where he met and filmed Swami SHIVANANDA SARASWATI of Rishikesh, Swami Ramdas, and Anandamayi Ma. Back in France, his finished documentary was shown on national television and very well received by the public as well as critics. He then specialized in documentaries on living spiritual traditions, filming with his 16-millimeter camera, assisted only by his wife. They traveled for extensive periods, taking their two children with them. In 1965, Desjardins produced several documentaries on the Tibetans, became close to the Dalaï Lama, and went on to produce films on Zen Buddhism in Japan and Sufi brotherhoods in Afghanistan. Those films, available today on DVD and videotapes, are considered unique documents. The expeditions enabled Desjardins to spend a lot of time in close contact with some of the greatest teachers of the East and to pursue his spiritual quest while developing a growing reputation in France as a filmmaker and lecturer.

He became a practitioner of Adhyatma yoga, which is a branch of Advaita Vedanta.

Mr Halagappa (d. 2019) devoted his reformed life to running this orphanage. In his younger days, he was a baggage lifter (a thief) until Sathya Sai Baba told him to stop and open the Sri Ranga Patna orphanage. He bought land on the banks of the river Cauvery and started the orphanage with four children in 1965. Halagappa says that in 1965 Sai Baba visited the ashram to see and guide the activities here while on his way to Kodaikanal. Sathya Sai Baba continued to regularly stop at this ashram to speak and give darshan to Halagappa and his family members until 1985.

A small temple or shrine is part of the orphanage, it contains many photographs of Sai Baba covered with materialized vibhuti. The temple also has in its possession some amulets (with portraits of Sathya Sai Baba and Shirdi Sai Baba) which were blessed by Sathya Sai Baba more than 30 years ago. When the amulets are held, amritha continuously flows from them. Amritha is sacred honey nectar or ambrosia that is also known as amrita and amrit, it is Sathya Sai Baba’s holy substance that has a distinctive taste and odour. The amulets are for all to hold and see.

There is also carved in black stone on a pedestal, feet representing those of Shirdi Baba’s which exude a particularly fragrant amrit. These symbolic feet were installed there on Sai Baba’s directions by N. Kasturi in the 1960s. 

Amrit is the ‘nectar of the gods,’ which in the ancient Ramayana gave eternal life to those who were fortunate enough to taste it. Those who did not succeed were consigned to more lifetimes as demonic asuras. It is also considered to be symbolic of the subtle liquid secreted by the pituitary gland of yogic adepts which is said to confer immortality.
